<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Contributing to Meshery Docs</h1>
          
          <div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Important</div>
<p>Before contributing, please review the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#documentation-contribution-flow">Documentation Contribution Flow</a>.</p>
</div>
<p>Use the following steps to set up your development environment depending on your Operating System of choice, fork the repository, install dependencies and run the site locally.  You can then make changes, test locally, sign-off and commit, and push the changes made for review.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Meshery Documentation Design Specification</div>
<p>See the <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/17guuaxb0xsfutBCzyj2CT6OZiFnMu9w4PzoILXhRXSo/edit">Meshery Documentation Design Specification</a> which serves to provide an overview of the tooling and approach used to create Meshery&rsquo;s documentation and its information architecture.</p>
</div>
<h2 id="documentation-framework">
	Documentation Framework
</h2>
<p>Meshery documentation is built using the following components:</p>
<ul>
<li>Framework - <a href="https://gohugo.io">Hugo</a> (Extended)</li>
<li>Theme - <a href="https://www.docsy.dev">Docsy</a> (imported as a Hugo module)</li>
<li>Repo - <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/docs">https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/docs</a></li>
<li>Site - <a href="https://docs.meshery.io">https://docs.meshery.io</a></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="set-up-your-development-environment">
	Set up your development environment
</h2>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Hugo</div>
<p>The Meshery Docs site is built using Hugo - a fast static site generator. Hugo is installed automatically as an npm dependency, so you only need Node.js and Go installed on your system.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="prerequisites">
	Prerequisites
</h3>
<p>The following tools are required to build and run the Meshery documentation site locally:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://nodejs.org/">Node.js</a> (LTS recommended)</li>
<li><a href="https://go.dev/dl/">Go</a> (required for Hugo modules)</li>
</ul>
<div class="alert alert-light" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Note</div>
<p>In case of any installation issues, use the <a href="https://discuss.meshery.io">discussion forum</a>.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="get-the-code">
	Get the code
</h3>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Fork and then clone the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery">Meshery repository</a></p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/meshery
</code>
</div></pre>
</li>
<li>
<p>Change to the docs directory</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">cd docs
</code>
</div></pre>
</li>
<li>
<p>Install dependencies</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make setup
</code>
</div></pre>
<p>This runs <code>npm install</code>, which installs Hugo Extended and all other required dependencies.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="serve-the-site">
	Serve the site
</h3>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Serve the site locally.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make site
</code>
</div></pre>
<p>This runs <code>hugo server -D -F</code>, which serves the site with draft and future content enabled. The site will be available at <code>http://localhost:1313</code>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>To build the site without serving:</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make build
</code>
</div></pre>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="using-docker">
	Using Docker
</h3>
<p>If you have Docker and <code>make</code> installed on your system, then you can serve the site locally. This doesn&rsquo;t require the need to install <em>Hugo</em>, <em>Node.js</em>, or <em>Go</em> on your system.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert">
<p>This may not work in Windows.</p>
</div>
<p>Run the following command from the <em>docs</em> folder.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">make docker
</span></span></code></pre></div><p>This runs <code>docker compose watch</code>, which builds and serves the site inside a container.</p>
<h3 id="using-gitpod">
	Using Gitpod
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Ensure you have an account on <a href="https://www.gitpod.io/" class="meshery-light">Gitpod</a> and add the <a href="https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/gitpod/dodmmooeoklaejobgleioelladacbeki" class="meshery-light">Gitpod extension</a> to your browser.</li>
<li>Open your forked Meshery repository on GitHub.</li>
<li>Click on the &ldquo;<strong>Gitpod</strong>&rdquo; button in the top right corner of the repository page (it is only visible with the <a href="https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/gitpod/dodmmooeoklaejobgleioelladacbeki" class="meshery-light">Gitpod browser extension</a> installed).</li>
</ul>
<div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">About Gitpod</div>
<p>Gitpod will automatically clone and open the repository for you in a browser-based version of Visual Studio Code. It will also automatically build the project for you on launch, comes with Docker and other tools pre-installed, making it one of the fastest ways to spin up a development environment for <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery">Meshery</a>.</p>
</div>
<ul>
<li>
<p>After opening the project on Gitpod, change to the docs directory.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">cd docs
</code>
</div></pre>
</li>
<li>
<p>Install dependencies and serve the site.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make setup
make site
</code>
</div></pre>
</li>
</ul>
<p>You should be able to access the site on port <code>1313</code>. If you want to access it in your localhost read the <a href="https://www.gitpod.io/docs/configure/workspaces/ports#local-port-forwarding-via-ssh">docs for port-forwarding using ssh</a>.</p>
<h3 id="using-github-codespaces">
	Using GitHub Codespaces
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Ensure you have an account on <a href="https://www.github.com/" class="meshery-light">GitHub</a></li>
<li>Open your forked Meshery repository on GitHub.</li>
<li>Click on the &ldquo;<strong>Code</strong>&rdquo; button of your forked repository it will give you the option to open the project in GitHub Codespaces.</li>
</ul>
<div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">About GitHub Codespaces</div>
<p>GitHub Codespaces will automatically clone and open the repository for you in a browser-based version of Visual Studio Code. It comes with pre-installed tools which are quite helpful to spin up the development environment for <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery">Meshery</a>.</p>
</div>
<ul>
<li>
<p>After opening the project on GitHub Codespaces, change to the docs directory.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">cd docs
</code>
</div></pre>
</li>
<li>
<p>Install dependencies and serve the site.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">make setup
make site
</code>
</div></pre>
</li>
</ul>
<p>You should be able to access the site on port <code>1313</code>. If you want to access it in your localhost just click the <code>code</code> button on your forked repository and select open with Visual Studio Code under your GitHub Codespace this will launch a GitHub Codespace instance in your local machine and connects with the remote GitHub Codespace environment after that run <code>cd docs</code> then <code>make setup &amp;&amp; make site</code> and it will start the development server on port <code>1313</code>.</p>
<h3 id="make-necessary-changes">
	Make Necessary Changes
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Make changes as required based on the issue you are solving.</li>
<li>Ensure to verify that your changes reflect correctly by serving the site locally using <code>make site</code>.</li>
</ul>
<div class="alert alert-light" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Note</div>
<p>If the issue requires making new doc page that replaces the old page, please don&rsquo;t forget to add a redirect link on the old page. In Hugo, you can add an <code>aliases</code> field in the frontmatter of the new page to redirect from the old URL.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="create-a-pull-request">
	Create a Pull Request
</h3>
<ul>
<li>
<p>After making changes, don&rsquo;t forget to commit with the sign-off flag (-s)!</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">git commit -s -m "my commit message w/signoff"
</code>
</div></pre>
</li>
<li>
<p>Once all changes have been committed, push the changes.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">git push origin [branch-name]
</code>
</div></pre>
</li>
<li>
<p>Then on GitHub, navigate to the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery">Meshery repository</a> and create a pull request from your recently pushed changes!</p>
</li>
</ul>
<hr>
<ul>
<li><em>See the <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/17guuaxb0xsfutBCzyj2CT6OZiFnMu9w4PzoILXhRXSo/edit">Meshery Documentation Google Doc</a> for additional reference.</em></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="using-the-features-of-meshery-docs">
	Using the features of Meshery Docs
</h2>
<h3 id="clipboard-feature">
	Clipboard Feature
</h3>
<p>Most popular clipboard plugins like Clipboard JS require the manual creation of a new ID for each code snippet. A different approach is used here. For code snippets, we either use html tags or markdown in the following manner:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>&lt;pre class=&#34;codeblock-pre&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;codeblock&#34;&gt;
&lt;code class=&#34;clipboardjs&#34;&gt;code_snippet_here&lt;/code&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;
</code></pre><p>You can also use the <code>code</code> shortcode created for this feature to make it easy to use. It can be used by passing the code snippet to it.</p>
<p>If the code snippet does not contain any special characters then, it can be used directly as below:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>{{&lt; code code=&#34;code_snippet_here&#34; &gt;}}
</code></pre><p>If the code snippet has special characters then use backtick delimiters:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>{{&lt; code code=`code_snippet_here` &gt;}}
</code></pre><p>Don&rsquo;t use <code>code</code> shortcode when the snippet is in between an ordered list, this breaks the order and next item in the list will start numbering from 1. Instead, use <code>&lt;pre class=&quot;codeblock-pre&quot;&gt;...&lt;/pre&gt;</code> method described above.</p>
<p><strong>A full block:</strong></p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>```code snippet```
</code></pre><p><strong>Inline formatting:</strong></p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">`code snippet`: `code snippet`</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p><strong>Language specific:</strong></p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">(language name)
code snippet
</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Whenever the code tags are detected, the clipboard javascript file is automatically loaded. Each code element is given a custom id and a clipboard-copy icon to copy the content.</p>
<h2 id="documentation-contribution-flow-summary">
	Documentation Contribution Flow Summary
</h2>
<div class="alert alert-light" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Note</div>
<p>For contributing <code>mesheryctl</code> reference section, refer <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-cli/">Contributing CLI</a></p>
</div>
<p>The following is a concise summary of the steps to contribute to Meshery documentation.</p>
<ol>
<li>Create a fork, if you have not already, by following the steps described <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-gitflow/">here</a></li>
<li>In the local copy of your fork, navigate to the docs folder.
<code>cd docs</code></li>
<li>Create and checkout a new branch to make changes within
<code>git checkout -b &lt;my-changes&gt;</code></li>
<li>Edit/add documentation.
<code>vi &lt;specific page&gt;.md</code></li>
<li>Add redirect link on the old page (only when a new page is created that replaces the old page). In Hugo, use the <code>aliases</code> frontmatter field.</li>
<li>Run site locally to preview changes.
<code>make site</code></li>
<li>Commit, <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-docs/#commit-signing">sign-off</a>, and push changes to your remote branch.
<code>git push origin &lt;my-changes&gt;</code></li>
<li>Open a pull request (in your web browser) against the repo: <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery">https://github.com/meshery/meshery</a>.</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="navigation-table-of-contents-in-sidebar-toc">
	Navigation Table of Contents in Sidebar (toc)
</h3>
<p>Sidebars use a data file at <code>data/toc.yml</code> to create a table of contents. It is written in the following manner:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>- title: Group 1
  url: group1
  links:
    - title: Thing 1
      url: group1/thing1
    - title: Thing 2
      url: group1/thing2
    - title: Thing 3
      url: group1/thing3
</code></pre><p>The output of the code snippet would be:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>    Group 1
      Thing 1
      Thing 2
      Thing 3
</code></pre><p>In this example, <strong>Group 1</strong> is a <code>parent</code> section within the Table of Contents, and <strong>Thing 1</strong>, <strong>Thing 2</strong>, and <strong>Thing 3</strong> are <code>children</code> of <strong>Group 1</strong>. This is a direct hierarchy with a single level of children under the parent.</p>
<p><code>Grandchildren</code> are added in the sidebars in the following manner:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>- title: Group 1
  url: group1
  links:
    - title: Thing 1
      url: group1/thing1
      children:
        - title: Subthing 1.1
          url: group1/thing1/subthing1_1
        - title: Subthing 1.2
          url: group1/thing1/subthing1_2
    - title: Thing 2
      url: group1/thing2
    - title: Thing 3
      url: group1/thing3
</code></pre><p>The output of the code snippet would be:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>    Group 1
      Thing 1
       Subthing 1.1
       Subthing 1.2
      Thing 2
      Thing 3
</code></pre><p>Here, <strong>Subthing 1.1</strong> and <strong>Subthing 1.2</strong> are the <code>grandchildren</code> of <strong>Thing 1</strong>.</p>
<p>The sidebar template in <code>layouts/partials/sidebar.html</code> reads from <code>data/toc.yml</code> and supports up to four levels of navigation hierarchy.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Parent</strong>: It serves as a top level category for related content.</li>
<li><strong>Children</strong> (<code>links</code>): They are immediate subsections or topics that fall under the parent section.</li>
<li><strong>Grandchildren</strong> (<code>children</code>): They are nested under a link and provide a more detailed breakdown of information within the child section. Grandchildren are used to organize content further, offering a more detailed structure for a specific topic.</li>
<li><strong>Great-grandchildren</strong> (<code>grandchildren</code>): An additional level of nesting for even finer-grained organization.</li>
</ul>
<p>These sections create a hierarchical and organized navigation experience for readers.</p>
<h3 id="alerts">
	Alerts
</h3>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">What is an alert?</div>
<p>An alert is a box that can stand out to indicate important information. You can choose from levels success, warning, danger, info, and primary. This example is an info box, and the code for another might look like this:</p>
</div>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">{{% alert color=&#34;info&#34; title=&#34;Here is another!&#34; %}}
{{% /alert %}}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Just for fun, here are all the types:</p>
<div class="alert alert-warning" role="alert">
<p>This is a warning</p>
</div>
<div class="alert alert-danger" role="alert">
<p>This alerts danger!</p>
</div>
<div class="alert alert-success" role="alert">
<p>This alerts success</p>
</div>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert">
<p>This is useful information.</p>
</div>
<div class="alert alert-primary" role="alert">
<p>This is a primary alert</p>
</div>
<div class="alert alert-secondary" role="alert">
<p>This is a secondary alert</p>
</div>
<div class="alert alert-light" role="alert">
<p>This is a light alert</p>
</div>
<div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert">
<p>This is a dark alert</p>
</div>
<h4 id="alert-shortcode">
	alert shortcode
</h4>
<p>Meshery Docs uses the <code>alert</code> shortcode (provided by the Docsy theme) to provide consistent formatting for notes, warnings, and various informative callouts intended for the readers.</p>
<p>To use the <code>alert</code> shortcode feature in our documentation include the following code:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">{{% alert color=&#34;info&#34; title=&#34;Here is another!&#34; %}}
{{% /alert %}}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Other supported alert colors include <code>warning</code>, <code>danger</code>,<code>success</code>,<code>primary</code>, <code>secondary</code>, <code>light</code>, <code>dark</code> .</p>
<h3 id="image-handling">
	Image Handling
</h3>
<p>Control image display in documentation pages using the following methods.</p>
<h4 id="default-image-size-in-markdown-format">
	Default Image Size in Markdown Format
</h4>
<p>Using the Markdown image syntax:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">[![Image Title](/assets/img/your-image.png)](/assets/img/your-image.png)</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>This renders as:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">&lt;a href=\&#34;/assets/img/your-image.png\&#34;&gt;
    &lt;img src=\&#34;/assets/img/your-image.png\&#34; alt=\&#34;Image Title\&#34;&gt;
&lt;/a&gt;</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p><strong>Effect:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Image is displayed at its original resolution, limited by global CSS (<code>max-width: 90vw; max-height: 90vh; height: auto; width: auto;</code>)</li>
<li>On larger screens (<code>min-width: 1200px</code>), image width can be up to <code>1200px</code></li>
<li>Clickable, opening in Lightbox if the format is supported</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="custom-image-size-for-control">
	Custom Image Size (for Control)
</h4>
<p>If you need to specify dimensions, use:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">&lt;a href=\&#34;/assets/img/your-image.png\&#34;&gt;
    &lt;img src=\&#34;/assets/img/your-image.png\&#34; style=\&#34;width:500px; height:auto;\&#34; alt=\&#34;Image Title\&#34;&gt;
&lt;/a&gt;</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p><strong>Effect:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Image width is fixed at <code>500px</code>, maintaining aspect ratio</li>
<li>If <code>500px</code> exceeds <code>90vw</code>, it will be constrained to <code>90vw</code></li>
<li>Clickable, opening in Lightbox for full-size viewing</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="quotes">
	Quotes
</h3>
<p>You can include block quotes to emphasize text.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Here is an example. Isn&rsquo;t this much more prominent to the user?</p>
</blockquote>
<h2 id="development">
	Development
</h2>
<h3 id="adding-integration-specific-information-to-individual-integration-pages">
	Adding Integration Specific Information to Individual Integration Pages
</h3>
<p>Integration pages (<a href="/extensibility/integrations/aws">example</a>) are automatically generated, however, integration specific documentation is often needed.</p>
<p><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/docs/data/modelscustominfo">modelscustominfo</a> collection holds custom markdown files. Follow these steps:</p>
<ol>
<li>Create a file inside the <code>modelscustominfo</code> collection.</li>
<li>Ensure the file includes frontmatter with the <code>title</code> key, set to the title of the integration.</li>
</ol>
<p>The content that follows the frontmatter in this file will be automatically parsed and rendered on the integration page</p>
<p>Example:</p>
<p>file: <code>modelscustominfo/aad.md</code></p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>---
title: Azure Active Directory (AAD)
---
&lt;h2&gt;Azure Active Directory (AAD)&lt;/h2&gt;
</code></pre><p>In this example, the heading &ldquo;<b>Azure Active Directory</b>&rdquo; will be displayed on the integration page:
<a href="/extensibility/integrations/aad-pod-identity">Azure Active Directory Integration Page</a></p>
<h3 id="suggested-reading">
	Suggested Reading
</h3>
<p>Disable suggested reading by setting the <code>suggested-reading</code> frontmatter variable to <code>false</code>.</p>
<h3 id="editable-intra-page-table-of-contents-toolbar">
	Editable Intra-page Table of Contents Toolbar
</h3>
<p>Control the display of this intra-page navigator with either page level or layout level frontmatter variables:</p>
<p><code>display-toolbar</code></p>
<p>Set to <code>true</code> (make &ldquo;editable&rdquo; toolbar visible) or <code>false</code> (hide &ldquo;editable&rdquo; toolbar)</p>
<h3 id="if-conditional">
	<code>if</code> conditional
</h3>
<p>In Hugo templates, conditionals are written using Go template syntax:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">{{ if eq .Params.title &#34;Awesome Shoes&#34; }}
  These shoes are awesome!
{{ end }}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>If the condition is true, the output would be:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>    These shoes are awesome!
</code></pre><h3 id="range-loop">
	<code>range</code> loop
</h3>
<p>The <code>range</code> action iterates over a collection. It is written in the following manner:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">{{ range .Pages }}
  {{ .Title }}
{{ end }}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>The output produced by the above code snippet would list the titles of all pages in the current section.</p>
<h3 id="comment">
	Comment
</h3>
<p>In Hugo templates, comments are written using Go template comment syntax:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">{{/* This is a comment */}}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Any content inside <code>{{/* */}}</code> will not be rendered in the output.</p>
<h3 id="partial">
	Partial
</h3>
<p>Partials are used to include reusable template fragments. They are written in the following manner:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">{{ partial &#34;header.html&#34; . }}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="shortcode">
	Shortcode
</h3>
<p>Shortcodes are reusable content snippets that can be used in Markdown files. They are written in the following manner:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">{{&lt;/* shortcode-name param=&#34;value&#34; */&gt;}}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="variable">
	Variable
</h3>
<p>In Hugo templates, variables are defined using the <code>:=</code> operator:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">{{ $variable1 := true }}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Two helpful resources:</p>
<ol>
<li>Hugo Docs - <a href="https://gohugo.io/documentation/">https://gohugo.io/documentation/</a></li>
<li>Go Template Docs - <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/text/template">https://pkg.go.dev/text/template</a></li>
</ol>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>How to write MeshKit compatible errors</h1>
          
          <p>Meshery pervasively uses MeshKit as a golang and infrastructure management-specific library in all of its components. MeshKit helps populate error messages with a uniform and useful set of informative attributes.</p>
<p>To help with creating error codes, MeshKit contains a tool that analyzes, verifies and updates error codes in Meshery source code trees. It extracts error details into a file that can be used for publishing all error code references on the Meshery <a href="/v0.9/reference/error-codes/">error codes reference page</a>. The objective to create this was to avoid centralized handling of error codes and automating everything</p>
<p>In order to create a Meshery error object, you will need to create a custom wrapper object for the native golang error. This can be done from the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit/tree/master/errors">MeshKit Error</a> package.</p>
<p>This tool will create a couple of files, one of them is designed to be used to generate the error reference on the Meshery Documentation website. The file errorutil_analyze_summary.json contains a summary of the analysis, notably lists of duplicates etc.</p>
<h2 id="conventions-to-follow-while-creating-errors">
	Conventions to follow while creating errors
</h2>
<ol>
<li>Errors names and codes are namespaced to components, i.e. they need to be unique within a component, which is verified by this tool.</li>
<li>Errors are not to be reused across components and modules.</li>
<li>Error codes are not to be set as integer. CI will take care of updating Error codes from a string to an integer.</li>
<li>Running <code>make error</code> analyzes your code and returns any warnings to be aware of.</li>
<li>Capitalize the first letter of the every error description.</li>
<li>Using errors.NewDefault(&hellip;) is deprecated. This tool emits a warning if its use is detected.</li>
<li>Use errors.New(&hellip;) from MeshKit to create actual errors with all the details.
This is often done in a factory function. It is important that the error code variable is used here, not a literal.
Specify detailed descriptions, probable causes, and remedies. They need to be string literals, call expressions are ignored.
This tool extracts this information from the code and exports it.
For the Code argument in the errors.New use the same Error name and append a &ldquo;Code&rdquo; after it. e.g error name : ErrApplyManifest then the error code is ErrApplyManifestCode</li>
<li>Set the value to any string, like &ldquo;replace_me&rdquo; (no convention here), e.g. ErrApplyManifestCode = &ldquo;replace_me&rdquo;.</li>
<li>By convention, error codes and the factory functions live in files called error.go. The tool checks all files, but updates only error.go files.</li>
</ol>
<p>Use the <code>errors.New()</code> function to create a new instance of the error object and pass situation-specific attributes as function arguments. These attributes are:</p>
<ul>
<li>Code</li>
<li>Short Description</li>
<li>Long Description</li>
<li>Probable Cause</li>
<li>Suggested Remediation</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="syntax">
	Syntax
</h3>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">errors.New(ErrExampleCode, errors.Alert, []string{&#34;&lt;short-description&gt;&#34;}, []string{&#34;&lt;long-description&gt;&#34;}, []string{&#34;&lt;probable-cause&gt;&#34;}, []string{&#34;&lt;suggested remediation&gt;&#34;})</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="example">
	Example
</h2>
<p>In this example we are creating an Error for being unable to marshal JSON</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">var (
	// Error code
    ErrMarshalCode= &#34;replace_me&#34;

    //Static errors (for example)
    ErrExample = errors.New(ErrExampleCode, errors.Alert, []string{&#34;&lt;short-description&gt;&#34;}, []string{&#34;&lt;long-description&gt;&#34;}, []string{&#34;&lt;probable-cause&gt;&#34;}, []string{&#34;&lt;suggested remediation&gt;&#34;})
)

// Dynamic errors
//Error Name
func ErrMarshal(err error, obj string) error {
	return errors.New(ErrMarshalCode, errors.Alert, []string{&#34;Unable to marshal the : &#34;, obj}, []string{err.Error()}, []string{}, []string{})
}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="replacing-old-error-codes">
	Replacing old Error Codes
</h3>
<p>Old</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">bd, err := json.Marshal(providers)
	if err != nil {
		http.Error(w, &#34;unable to marshal the providers&#34;, http.StatusInternalServerError)
		return
	}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>New</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">bd, err := json.Marshal(providers)
  if err != nil {
          obj := &#34;provider&#34;
          http.Error(w, ErrMarshal(err, obj).Error(), http.StatusInternalServerError)
          return
      }</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="replacing-logrus">
	Replacing logrus
</h2>
<p>There already exists an <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit/blob/master/logger/logger.go">interface for logger</a> in MeshKit.<br><br></p>
<div class="alert alert-warning" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">WARNING</div>
<p>To enforce the use of meshkit errors, meshkit logger was designed such that it only works with meshkit errors. If a non-meshkit error is logged through the logger, it would panic and kill the process. See: <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit/pull/119">meshkit#119</a> for more insight.</p>
</div>
<h4 id="defining-a-logger">
	Defining a Logger
</h4>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">type Logger struct {
	log   logger.Handler
}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h4 id="debug">
	Debug
</h4>
<h5 id="old">
	Old
</h5>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">logrus.Debugf(&#34;meshLocationURL: %s&#34;, meshLocationURL)</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h5 id="new">
	New
</h5>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">l.log.Debug(&#34;meshLocationURL: &#34;, meshLocationURL)</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h4 id="error">
	Error
</h4>
<h5 id="old-1">
	Old
</h5>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">logrus.Errorf(&#34;error marshaling data: %v.&#34;, err)</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h5 id="new-1">
	New
</h5>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">l.log.Error(ErrMarshal(err, obj))</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="a-small-program-using-meshkit-errors-and-logger">
	A small program using meshkit errors and logger
</h2>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">package main

import (
	&#34;fmt&#34;
	&#34;os&#34;

	meshkitErrors &#34;github.com/meshery/meshkit/errors&#34;
	&#34;github.com/meshery/meshkit/logger&#34;
	&#34;github.com/sirupsen/logrus&#34;
	&#34;github.com/spf13/viper&#34;
)

var (
	// CI will replace test_code with new error code
	ErrOpeningFileCode = &#34;test_code&#34;
)

func main() {
	logLevel := viper.GetInt(&#34;LOG_LEVEL&#34;)
	if viper.GetBool(&#34;DEBUG&#34;) {
		logLevel = int(logrus.DebugLevel)
	}
	log, err := logger.New(&#34;test&#34;, logger.Options{
		Format:   logger.SyslogLogFormat,
		LogLevel: logLevel,
	})
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println(err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// logging meshkit error
	err = openFileWithMeshkitError(&#34;some.txt&#34;)
	if err != nil {
		log.Error(err)
	}
	// OUTPUT
	// ERRO[2021-11-10T17:31:28+05:30] open some.txt: no such file or directory
	// app=test code=1001 probable-cause=&#34;empty string passed as argument .file with this name doesn&#39;t exist&#34;
	// severity=2 short-description=&#34;unable to open file&#34; suggested-remediation=&#34;pass a non-empty string as
	// filename .create file before opening it&#34;

	// logging non meshkit error
	err = openFile(&#34;some.txt&#34;)
	if err != nil {
		log.Error(err)
	}
	// OUTPUT
	// ERRO[2024-07-01T19:09:09+05:30] open some.txt: no such file or directory
	// app=test code= probable-cause= severity=0 short-description= suggested-remediation=

}

// this returns a non meshkit error
func openFile(name string) error {
	_, err := os.Open(name)
	return err
}

// this returns a meshkit error
func openFileWithMeshkitError(name string) error {
	_, err := os.Open(name)
	return ErrOpeningFile(err)
}

func ErrOpeningFile(err error) error {
	return meshkitErrors.New(ErrOpeningFileCode, meshkitErrors.Alert, []string{&#34;unable to open file&#34;},
		[]string{err.Error()},
		[]string{&#34;empty string passed as argument &#34;, &#34;file with this name doesn&#39;t exist&#34;},
		[]string{&#34;pass a non-empty string as filename &#34;, &#34;create file before opening it&#34;})
}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Contributing to Meshery using git</h1>
          
          <h1 id="working-by-forking">
	Working by Forking
</h1>
<p>Just head over to the GitHub page and click the &ldquo;Fork&rdquo; button. It&rsquo;s just that simple. Once you&rsquo;ve done that, you can use your favorite git client to clone your repo or just head straight to the command line:</p>
<h2 id="clone-your-fork-to-your-local-machine">
	Clone your fork to your local machine
</h2>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>git clone git@github.com:USERNAME/FORKED-PROJECT.git
</code></pre><p>Keeping Your Fork Up to Date
While this isn&rsquo;t a necessary step, if you plan on doing anything more than just a tiny quick fix, you&rsquo;ll want to make sure you keep your fork up to date by tracking the original &ldquo;upstream&rdquo; repo that you forked. To do this, you&rsquo;ll need to add a remote:</p>
<h2 id="add-upstream-repo-to-list-of-remotes">
	Add &lsquo;upstream&rsquo; repo to list of remotes
</h2>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>git remote add upstream https://github.com/meshery/meshery.git
</code></pre><p>(&ldquo;meshery&rdquo; is used as the example repo. Be sure to reference the <em>actual</em> repo you&rsquo;re contributing to e.g. &ldquo;meshery-linkerd&rdquo;).</p>
<h2 id="verify-the-new-remote-named-upstream">
	Verify the new remote named &lsquo;upstream&rsquo;
</h2>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>git remote -v
</code></pre><p>Whenever you want to update your fork with the latest upstream changes, you&rsquo;ll need to first fetch the upstream repo&rsquo;s branches and latest commits to bring them into your repository:</p>
<h2 id="fetch-from-upstream-remote">
	Fetch from upstream remote
</h2>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>git fetch upstream
</code></pre><h2 id="view-all-branches-including-those-from-upstream">
	View all branches, including those from upstream
</h2>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>git branch -va
</code></pre><p>Now, check out your master branch and merge the upstream repo&rsquo;s master branch:</p>
<h2 id="checkout-your-master-branch-and-merge-upstream">
	Checkout your master branch and merge upstream
</h2>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>git checkout master
git merge upstream/master
</code></pre><p>If there are no unique commits on the local master branch, git will simply perform a fast-forward. However, if you have been making changes on master (in the vast majority of cases you probably shouldn&rsquo;t be - see the next section, you may have to deal with conflicts. When doing so, be careful to respect the changes made upstream.</p>
<p>Now, your local master branch is up-to-date with everything modified upstream.</p>
<p><strong>Create a Branch</strong> (doing your work)
Whenever you begin work on a new feature or bugfix, it&rsquo;s important that you create a new branch. Not only is it proper git workflow, but it also keeps your changes organized and separated from the master branch so that you can easily submit and manage multiple pull requests for every task you complete.</p>
<p>To create a new branch and start working on it, perform the following flow.</p>
<h2 id="check-out-the-master-branch---you-want-your-new-branch-to-come-from-the-master">
	Check out the master branch - you want your new branch to come from the master
</h2>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>git checkout master
</code></pre><h2 id="create-a-new-branch-give-your-branch-its-own-simple-informative-name">
	Create a new branch (give your branch its own simple informative name)
</h2>
<p>For enhancements use <code>feature/your_username/issue#</code> or <code>feature/your_username/name_of_feature</code></p>
<p>For bugs use <code>bug/your_username/issue#</code> or <code>bug/your_username/name_of_bug</code></p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>git branch feature/jdoe/567
</code></pre><h2 id="switch-to-your-new-branch">
	Switch to your new branch
</h2>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>git checkout feature/jdoe/567
</code></pre><p>Now, go to town hacking away and making whatever changes you want to.</p>
<h2 id="submitting-your-changes-a-pull-request">
	Submitting your changes (a Pull Request)
</h2>
<p>Before submitting your pull request, you might want to do a few things to clean up your branch and make it as simple as possible for the original repo&rsquo;s maintainer to test, accept, and merge your work.</p>
<p>In the time that you&rsquo;ve been working on your changes, if any commits have been made to the upstream master branch, you will need to rebase your development branch so that merging it will be a simple fast-forward that won&rsquo;t require any conflict resolution work.</p>
<h2 id="fetch-upstream-master-and-merge-with-your-repos-master-branch">
	Fetch upstream master and merge with your repo&rsquo;s master branch
</h2>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>git fetch upstream
git checkout master
git merge upstream/master
</code></pre><h2 id="if-there-were-any-new-commits-rebase-your-development-branch">
	If there were any new commits, rebase your development branch
</h2>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>git checkout feature/jdoe/567
git rebase master
</code></pre><p>Now, it may be desirable to squash some of your smaller commits down into a small number of larger more cohesive commits. You can do this with an interactive rebase:</p>
<h2 id="rebase-all-commits-on-your-development-branch">
	Rebase all commits on your development branch
</h2>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>git checkout
git rebase -i master
</code></pre><p>This will open up a text editor where you can specify which commits to squash.</p>
<h2 id="submitting">
	Submitting
</h2>
<p>Once you&rsquo;ve committed and pushed all of your changes to GitHub, go to the page for your fork on GitHub, select your development branch, and click the pull request button. If you need to make any adjustments to your pull request, just push the updates to GitHub. Your pull request will automatically track the changes in your development branch and update it.</p>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Contributing to Models Quick Start</h1>
          
          <p><strong>Models follow Meshery&rsquo;s schema-driven development approach.</strong> Model, Component, and Relationship definitions are validated against schemas in <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/tree/master/schemas/constructs/v1beta1/model"><code>Model schema</code></a>. See <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/">Contributing to Schemas</a> for details.</p>
<p><a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/">Meshery Models</a> are a way to represent the architecture of a system or application. Models are defined in JSON and can be used to visualize the components and relationships between them. This guide will walk you through the process of creating a new model.</p>
<p><a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/">Meshery Components</a> are the building blocks of a model. Each component represents a different part of the system or application. Components can be anything from a database to a microservice to a server. Relationships define how components interact with each other. For example, a database component might have a relationship with a microservice component that represents the microservice&rsquo;s dependency on the database.</p>
<h3 id="creating-your-first-meshery-model">
	Creating your first Meshery Model
</h3>
<p>To get started quickly, check out the <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/creating-models/">Creating Models</a>  guide for step-by-step instructions.</p>
<h3 id="contributing-a-model-definition">
	Contributing a Model Definition
</h3>
<ol>
<li>Fork the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery.io">meshery/meshery.io</a> repository.</li>
<li>Create a new branch in your fork of the meshery/meshery.io repository.</li>
<li>Add your model definition to the <code>collections/_models</code> directory.</li>
<li>Create a pull request to the meshery/meshery.io repository.</li>
<li>Once your pull request is merged, your model will be available in the next Meshery release.</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="next-steps">
	Next Steps
</h3>
<p>To learn more about how to contribute and customize your models, check out the full <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-models/">Contributing to Models</a> documentation. We encourage you to get involved in the development of Meshery Models and to share your feedback!</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Meshery Models are Extensible</div>
<p>Meshery Models are designed to be extensible, allowing you to define new components as needed. If you have an idea for a new component, please create one and share it with the Meshery community.</p>
</div>

        </div>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Contributing to Models</h1>
          
          <p><strong>Meshery Models are schema-driven.</strong> Model definitions, including their structure, metadata, and versioning, are defined by JSON Schemas in the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas"><code>meshery/schemas</code></a> repository. Before contributing to models, familiarize yourself with the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/tree/master/schemas/constructs/v1beta1/model">Model schema</a> and see <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/">Contributing to Schemas</a> for the development workflow.</p>
<h2 id="understanding-the-internals-of-mesherys-logical-object-model">
	Understanding the internals of Meshery&rsquo;s logical object model
</h2>
<p>Meshery uses a logical object model to describe the infrastructure and capabilities it manages in a consistent and extensible way.</p>
<h4 id="what-are-meshery-models">
	What Are Meshery Models?
</h4>
<p>At the core of this system are <strong>Meshery Models</strong> — packages that define a specific type of infrastructure, application, or capability. These models include:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong><a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/">Components</a></strong>: Individual parts of a system (e.g., services, databases).</li>
<li><strong><a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/relationships/">Relationships</a></strong>: How those parts interact.</li>
<li><strong>Metadata</strong>: Visual and behavioral traits, such as icons or capabilities.</li>
</ul>
<p>Models can describe traditional technologies (like Kubernetes workloads), or more abstract entities (like annotations or diagrams).</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Learn more: <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/">What are Meshery Models?</a></p>
</blockquote>
<h4 id="what-is-the-model-schema">
	What Is the Model Schema?
</h4>
<p>Each model includes a set of entities (in the form of definitions) that Meshery can manage. Models are defined and versioned using the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/blob/master/schemas/constructs/v1beta1/model/model.yaml">Model Schema</a>.</p>
<p>The schema defines the structure of the model, including the entities it contains, their relationships, and the properties they have. The schema also defines the version of the model and the version of the schema itself.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>See <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/registry/">Registry</a> to learn more about Meshery&rsquo;s internal registry and how to use it.</p>
</blockquote>
<p><a href="/project/contributing/images/meshery-models.png"><img class="content-image" src="/project/contributing/images/meshmodel-architecture.svg" alt="Model Entity Classification"  /></a>
<em>Figure: Model Entity Classification</em></p>
<h2 id="meshery-entities-and-their-lifecycle">
	Meshery Entities and their Lifecycle
</h2>
<p>This section aids in your understanding of the vernacular of Meshery&rsquo;s internal object model and discusses the difference beteween schemas, definitions, declarations, and instances. The lifecycle of Meshery entities (components, relationships, policies) is represented by the following terms, which are used to describe the various stages of their lifecycle.</p>
<h3 id="schema">
	Schema
</h3>
<p><strong>Schema</strong> <em>(static)</em> <strong>: the skeletal structure representing a logical view of the size, shape, characteristics of a construct.</strong></p>
<p>The schema represents the skeletal structure of an entity and provides a logical view of its size, shape, and characteristics. It defines the expected properties and attributes of the entity. The schema serves as a blueprint or template for creating instances of the entity. It is a static representation that defines the structure and properties but does not contain specific configuration values.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Schema example</div>
<details><summary>Component schema excerpt</summary><pre> {
"$id": "https://schemas.meshery.io/component.json",
  "$schema": "<http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#>",
"description": "Components are the atomic units for designing infrastructure. Learn more at <https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/components>",
"required": [
"apiVersion",
"kind",
"schema",
"model"
],
"additionalProperties": false,
"type": "object",
"properties": {
"apiVersion": {
"type": "string",
"description": "API Version of the component."
},
"kind": {
"type": "string",
"description": "Kind of the component."
.
.
.
<p></pre></details> See <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas">github.com/meshery/schemas</a> for more details.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="definition">
	Definition
</h3>
<p><strong>Definition</strong> <em>(static)</em> <strong>: An implementation of the Schema containing an outline of the specific attributes of a given, unconfigured entity.</strong></p>
<p>A definition is an implementation of the schema. It contains specific configurations and values for the entity at hand. The definition provides the actual configuration details for a specific instance of the entity. It is static because it is created based on the schema but does not change once created. The definition is used to instantiate declarations of the entity.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Definition example</div>
<p>a generic, unconfigured Kubernetes Pod.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="declaration">
	Declaration
</h3>
<p><strong>Declaration</strong> <em>(static)</em> <strong>: - A configured entity with detailed intentions of a given Definition.</strong></p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Declaration example</div>
<p>NGINX container as a Kubernetes Pod with port 443 and SSL termination.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="instance">
	Instance
</h3>
<p><strong>Instance</strong> <em>(dynamic)</em> <strong>: A realized entity (deployed/discovered); An instantiation of the declaration.</strong></p>
<p>An <em>instance</em> represents a realized entity. An <em>instance</em> is a dynamic representation that corresponds to a deployed or discovered instantiation of a <em>declaration</em>. An <em>instance</em> is created based on its corresponding <em>definition</em> and represents an actual running or deployed version of the entity within the environment.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Instance example</div>
<p>NGINX-as234z2 pod running in a cluster as a Kubernetes Pod with port 443 and SSL termination.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="capabilities">
	Capabilities
</h3>
<p><strong>Capabilities</strong>: Capabilities are used to describe the operations that a model supports.</p>
<p>Models use <strong>capabilities</strong> to describe the operations which they support, such as styling, configurations, interactions, and runtime behavior. Entities may define a broad array of capabilities, which are in turn dynamically interpreted by Meshery for full lifecycle management.</p>
<p>To simplify the assignment of these capabilities, Meshery organizes these capabilities into reusable and assignable sets, such as:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Default Set:</strong>
A foundational set covering configuration (<code>Workload Configuration</code>, <code>Labels and Annotations</code>), UI interaction (<code>Styling</code>, <code>Change Shape</code>, <code>Compound Drag and Drop</code>), and component introspection (<code>Relationships</code>, <code>Json Schema</code>).</li>
<li><strong>Shapes:</strong>
Visual components with layout and appearance-related capabilities. Includes <code>Styling</code>, <code>Change Shape</code>, <code>Compound Drag and Drop</code>, and <code>Body Text</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Comment:</strong>
Annotation-like elements with light interaction. Similar to <strong>Shapes</strong>, but focused on non-functional overlays.</li>
<li><strong>Ghost:</strong>
Lightweight visual components with minimal styling. Typically lacks body text or complex interactions.</li>
<li><strong>Shapes without Text:</strong>
Variant of <strong>Shapes</strong>, omitting <code>Body Text</code> to support simpler block structures.</li>
<li><strong>Component with Logging and Terminal Session Support:</strong>
Extends the Default set with operational capabilities like <code>Performance Test</code>, <code>Interactive Terminal</code>, and <code>Stream Logs</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Container Alias:</strong>
Alias components that simulate real workloads, combining configuration, view, and operational capabilities.</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="individual-capabilities">
	Individual Capabilities
</h4>
<table>
  <thead>
      <tr>
          <th>Capability</th>
          <th>Description</th>
          <th>Kind</th>
      </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Performance Test</strong></td>
          <td>Initiate a performance test. Meshery will execute the load generation, collect metrics, and present the results.</td>
          <td>action</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Workload Configuration</strong></td>
          <td>Configure the workload specific setting of a component.</td>
          <td>mutate</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Labels and Annotations Configuration</strong></td>
          <td>Configure Labels And Annotations for the component.</td>
          <td>mutate</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Relationships</strong></td>
          <td>View defined relationships for the component.</td>
          <td>view</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Json Schema</strong></td>
          <td>View the underlying JSON Schema definition of the component.</td>
          <td>view</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Styling</strong></td>
          <td>Configure the visual styles for the component.</td>
          <td>mutate</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Change Shape</strong></td>
          <td>Change the shape of the component.</td>
          <td>mutate</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Compound Drag and Drop</strong></td>
          <td>Drag and Drop a component into a parent component in graph view.</td>
          <td>interaction</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Body Text</strong></td>
          <td>Add textual content within the body of a node.</td>
          <td>mutate</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Show Label</strong></td>
          <td>Display label text associated with a node (similar to <code>Body Text</code>).</td>
          <td>view</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Resolve Component</strong></td>
          <td>Mark the status of a component as resolved.</td>
          <td>mutate</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Interactive Terminal</strong></td>
          <td>Initiate a terminal session.</td>
          <td>action</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Stream Logs</strong></td>
          <td>Initiate log streaming session.</td>
          <td>action</td>
      </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Capabilities Schema example</div>
<details><summary>Capabilities schema excerpt</summary><pre> {
"$id": "https://schemas.meshery.io/capability.json",
"$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
"description": "Meshery manages entities in accordance with their specific capabilities. This field explicitly identifies those capabilities largely by what actions a given component supports; e.g. metric-scrape, sub-interface, and so on. This field is extensible. Entities may define a broad array of capabilities, which are in-turn dynamically interpretted by Meshery for full lifecycle management.",
"additionalProperties": false,
"type": "object",
"required":
.
...
.
"kind": {
"description": "Top-level categorization of the capability",
"additionalProperties": false,
"anyOf": [
{
"const": "action",
"description": "For capabilities related to executing actions on entities. Example: initiate log streaming on a Pod. Example: initiate deployment of a component."
},
{
"const": "mutate",
"description": "For capabilities related to mutating an entity. Example: the ability to change the configuration of a component."
},
.
.
.
<p></pre></details> See <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/blob/master/typescript/constructs/v1alpha1/capability/CapabilityOpenApiSchema.ts">Capabilities Schema</a> for more details.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="importing-and-creating-models">
	Importing and Creating Models
</h3>
<p>Models can be created from scratch or imported using either the Meshery UI or the Meshery CLI.<br>
To learn more, see the detailed guides on <a href="%7B%7Bsite.baseurl%7D%7D/guides/configuration-management/importing-models">Importing Models</a> and <a href="%7B%7Bsite.baseurl%7D%7D/guides/configuration-management/creating-models">Creating Models</a>.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Use <strong>Create</strong> if you&rsquo;re starting from scratch. Use <strong>Import</strong> if you already have model definitions (e.g., JSON, CSV, tar).</p>
</blockquote>
<h3 id="model-generation-from-schemas">
	Model Generation from Schemas
</h3>
<p>Meshery automatically generates models and components by parsing schemas from various sources. While <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/extend-kubernetes/api-extension/custom-resources/">Kubernetes Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs)</a> are a common source, Meshery can create components from any valid schema definition.</p>
<h4 id="component-grouping-into-models">
	Component Grouping into Models
</h4>
<p>When generating components, Meshery processes input schemas and automatically organizes them into <strong>Models</strong>. This grouping process logically binds related components together based on their source.</p>
<p><strong>Source-Based Grouping:</strong><br>
Components are grouped based on their origin—such as a specific GitHub repository, Helm chart, or Kubernetes cluster. For example:</p>
<ul>
<li>Importing a Helm chart for Prometheus from ArtifactHub creates a &ldquo;Prometheus&rdquo; Model containing all resources defined in that chart (Services, Deployments, ConfigMaps, etc.) as components</li>
<li>Connecting to a Kubernetes cluster creates a &ldquo;Kubernetes&rdquo; Model containing all discovered CRDs as components</li>
<li>Importing from a GitHub repository creates a model named after the repository</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Metadata Preservation:</strong><br>
For Kubernetes CRDs, the <code>spec.group</code> field is extracted and stored as part of each component&rsquo;s API version (e.g., <code>networking.k8s.io/v1</code>). This metadata is preserved but does not determine model assignment for direct imports.</p>
<h4 id="component-generation-behavior">
	Component Generation Behavior
</h4>
<p>When Meshery processes schemas:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Parsing</strong>: The source is parsed to extract schema specifications for every entity.</li>
<li><strong>Component Creation</strong>: A component definition is generated for each entity, capturing its kind, version, and schema.</li>
<li><strong>Model Assignment</strong>: Components are automatically assigned to a Model based on their source context.</li>
<li><strong>Registration</strong>: Components are registered in Meshery&rsquo;s <a href="%7B%7Bsite.baseurl%7D%7D/concepts/logical/registry">Registry</a> under their respective model.</li>
<li><strong>Enrichment</strong>: Components inherit default properties from their model and can be further customized.</li>
</ol>
<p>This automatic grouping allows you to manage related resources as cohesive units within Meshery designs.</p>
<h4 id="advanced-grouping-by-api-group-csv-imports">
	Advanced: Grouping by API Group (CSV Imports)
</h4>
<p>When importing models via CSV or Google Spreadsheet, you can optionally specify a <code>group</code> field to filter which CRDs are included based on their <code>spec.group</code> value. This filtering capability is <strong>specific to CSV/spreadsheet imports</strong> and is not available for direct imports from GitHub repositories, ArtifactHub packages, or live Kubernetes clusters.</p>
<p><strong>How Group Filtering Works:</strong></p>
<p>During CSV import, if you specify a <code>group</code> value in your model definition, Meshery will only process CRDs whose <code>spec.group</code> field matches the specified value. This allows you to create focused models containing only components from a specific Kubernetes API group.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>With a group specified</strong>: Only CRDs matching the <code>spec.group</code> value are processed</li>
<li><strong>Without a group specified</strong> (empty field): All CRDs from the source are processed</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Example:</strong></p>
<p>In the CRD below, the <code>spec.group</code> field has the value <code>cloudquota.cnrm.cloud.google.com</code>:</p>
<p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  annotations:
    cnrm.cloud.google.com/version: 1.140.0
  name: apiquotaadjustersettings.cloudquota.cnrm.cloud.google.com
spec:
  group: cloudquota.cnrm.cloud.google.com # API group used for filtering
  names:
    kind: APIQuotaAdjusterSettings
    plural: apiquotaadjustersettings
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
    - name: v1beta1
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          properties:
            apiVersion:
              type: string
            kind:
              type: string</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<strong>CSV Model Definition Example:</strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-csv" data-lang="csv"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="s">model</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">group</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">category</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">modelDisplayName</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">registrant</span><span class="p">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="s">gcp-cloudquota</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">cloudquota.cnrm.cloud.google.com</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">Cloud Native Network</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">GCP Cloud Quota</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">artifacthub</span><span class="p">
</span></span></span></code></pre></div><p>When this CSV is imported with associated CRD files, only CRDs from the <code>cloudquota.cnrm.cloud.google.com</code> API group will be included as components in the &ldquo;gcp-cloudquota&rdquo; model.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">CSV Import Only</div>
<p>Group filtering is only available when importing via CSV or Google Spreadsheet. For all other import methods (GitHub repositories, ArtifactHub/Helm packages, or live Kubernetes clusters), all available resources are processed and organized into models based on their source.</p>
</div>
<p><strong>When to Use Group Filtering:</strong></p>
<p>Group filtering is useful when:</p>
<ul>
<li>You want to create separate models for different API groups from the same source</li>
<li>You&rsquo;re working with a large collection of CRDs and need to organize them by Kubernetes API group</li>
<li>You need fine-grained control over which CRDs are included in a specific model</li>
</ul>
<p>For most use cases, the automatic source-based grouping is sufficient and requires no additional configuration.</p>
<h3 id="post-model-generation">
	Post Model Generation
</h3>
<p>During model generation, corresponding components are created. Next step is to enrich these component details and define their capabilities and relationships.</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Enrich Component Details</strong>
When a Component is initially generated, a new Component definition is created with default properties (e.g. colors, icons, capabilities, etc.), some of which are inherited from their respective Model.</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>1.1. Customize Shapes and Colors</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Default shape for new components is a circle</li>
<li>Consider enriching components&rsquo; details based on what they represent</li>
<li>Reference Cytoscape <a href="https://js.cytoscape.org/demos/node-types/">node types</a> for possible shapes</li>
<li>Example: Use a pentagon shape to represent a Deployment</li>
<li>Know more about <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides/configuration-management/identifying-components">components shapes and colors</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>1.2. Customize Icons</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Components inherit the icon (colored and white SVGs) of their respective Model by default</li>
<li>Propose specific icons best suited to visually represent each component</li>
<li>Example: Use a skull icon for a DaemonSet</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>1.3. Review Capabilities</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Review and confirm assigned capabilities</li>
<li>Modify capabilities as needed</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p>See the <a href="%7B%7Bsite.baseurl%7D%7D/project/contributing/contributing-components">Contributing to Components</a> for detailed instructions.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Identify Relationships</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>2.1. Review Available Types</strong>
Review and familiarize yourself with the predefined relationship kinds, types, and subtypes. See <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/relationships/">&ldquo;Relationships logical concepts&rdquo;</a></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>2.2. Map Component Relationships</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Identify appropriate relationships for your new components</li>
<li>Consider how components relate to others within the same model</li>
<li>Consider relationships with components in other models</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>2.3. Create Definitions</strong>
Codify the relationships you have identified into a Relationship Definition</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p>See the <a href="%7B%7Bsite.baseurl%7D%7D/project/contributing/contributing-relationships">Contributing to Relationships</a> for detailed instructions.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<h2 id="next-steps">
	Next Steps
</h2>
<p>The Meshery team is currently working on the following:</p>
<ul>
<li>Extending the model to support additional entities</li>
<li>Improving the tooling for working with models</li>
<li>Defining relationships between components and embedding those policies within models</li>
</ul>
<p>We encourage you to get involved in the development of Meshery Models and to share your feedback!</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Meshery Models are extensible</div>
<p>Meshery Models are designed to be extensible, allowing you to define new components as needed. If you have an idea for a new component, please create one and share it with the Meshery community.</p>
</div>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
