<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

            <h1>Contributing to Meshery Policies</h1>
          
          <h2 id="background">
	Background
</h2>
<p>Meshery has a built-in policy engine, based on <a href="https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/">Open Policy Agent (OPA)</a>. Meshery uses the <a href="https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/policy-language/">Rego</a> query language to create these <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/logical/policies">policies</a>.</p>
<h2 id="prerequisites">
	Prerequisites
</h2>
<p>To start contributing to Meshery Policy Engine, make sure you have <a href="https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/#running-opa">OPA CLI</a> installed on your system. You will also need to clone the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/">Meshery Server</a> project from Github.</p>
<h2 id="components-of-meshery-policy-engine">
	Components of Meshery Policy Engine
</h2>
<p>Rego policies are the declarative logic behind the policy engine. These policies define how the underlying engine understands relationships within Meshery Designs. Rego policies can be found <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/server/meshmodel/meshery-core/0.7.2/v1.0.0/policies">here</a> in the Meshery Github repository.</p>
<p>Currently the Rego policies are invoked from the Go code in Meshery Server. This requires configuring the OPA context as seen <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit/blob/master/models/meshmodel/core/policies/rego_policy_relationship.go">here</a>.</p>
<p>The Meshery Policy Engine is invoked by calling the <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/reference/rest-apis#api-meshmodels-relationships-evaluate">evaluation endpoint</a>. This endpoint is passed a Meshery Design in JSON which it passes to the Meshery Policy Engine for validation.</p>
<h2 id="working-with-meshery-policy-engine">
	Working with Meshery Policy Engine
</h2>
<p>Working with the Meshery Policy Engine can feel complex because of the large number of different relationships a Meshery Design might contain. Contributors must then be careful to test any changes thoroughly to avoid unexpected results. When working with the Rego policies themselves it makes testing and development easier to be able to test the policies directly without running the entire Meshery Server. When working on the policies keep the following in mind:</p>
<ul>
<li>Since we will be running these policies using the OPA CLI directly without the Go bootstrap code we need to provide the necessary context for the policy engine. This means providing a data structure containing the valid Meshery Relationships the policy engine will evaluate against.</li>
<li>The input to the policy engine is a Meshery Design as a JSON data structure. When testing the Meshery Policy Engine you will need to provide this design as input. If you are working on a bug you will need to get the design from the issue or directly from the individual who reported the bug.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="executing-opa">
	Executing OPA
</h2>
<p>You can evaluate the Rego policies against test data stored in the <code>policies/test</code> folder:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make rego-eval</code>
	</div>
</pre>


        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Contributing to Model Relationships</h1>
          
          <p><strong>Relationships follow a schema-defined structure.</strong> The <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/tree/master/schemas/constructs/v1alpha3/relationship">Relationship schema</a> specifies how relationships between components are expressed. Refer to the schema when defining new relationship types or selectors. See <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/">Contributing to Schemas</a> for details.</p>
<p><a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/relationships/">Relationships</a> within <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/">Models</a> play a crucial role in establishing concrete visualisations of efficient data flow between different components of Meshery. These are used to classify the nature of interaction between one or more interconnected <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/">Components</a>.</p>
<h2 id="overview-of-steps-to-create-relationships">
	Overview of Steps to Create Relationships
</h2>
<p><strong>Prework:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-relationships/#relationship-identification">Relationship Identification</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-relationships/#relationship-visualizations">Relationship Classification</a></li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Development:</strong>
3. <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-relationships/#relationship-definitions">Relationship Definition</a>
4. <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-relationships/#relationship-scopes">Relationship Scopes</a></p>
<p><strong>Postwork:</strong>
5. <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-relationships/#relationship-testing">Relationship Testing</a>
6. <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-relationships/#relationship-contribution">Relationship Contribution</a></p>
<h2 id="prework">
	Prework
</h2>
<p><a id="relationship-identification"></a></p>
<h3 id="1-characterize-the-relationship-and-any-specific-constraints">
	1. Characterize the relationship and any specific constraints
</h3>
<p>Using your domain expertise, define the qualities of this new relationship. Identify and qualify any specific constraints to be enforced between one or more specific components within the same or different models. Let&rsquo;s take an example to understand this better.</p>
<p>For example, you might know that a Kubernetes <code>Service</code> can have a network-based relatinship with a Kubernetes <code>Pod</code>. To codify this relationship, you would define the relationship as a <code>kind: edge</code> relationship with a <code>type: network</code>.</p>
<details close>
<summary>Relationship Example</summary>
<pre><code class="language-yaml highlighter-rouge">
{
  "schemaVersion": "core.meshery.io/v1alpha2",
  "kind": "edge",
  "type": "network",
  "version": "v1.0.0",
  "metadata": {"description": "A relationship that defines network edges between components."}
  selector: [{
      "allow": {
         "from": [
            {
               "kind": "Service",
               "model": "kubernetes"
            }
         ],
         "to": [
            {
               "kind": "Pod",
               "model": "kubernetes"
            }
         ]
      },
      "deny": {}
   }]
<p></code></pre></p>
</details>
<p>You might <em>also</em> know that this relationship is constrained by the presence of a Kubernetes <code>Deployment</code> as the parent of the Kubernetes <code>Pod</code>. This constraint would be codified in the relationship definition by including the <code>deny</code> function in your selector.</p>
<details close>
<summary>Example Relationship with Constraints</summary>
<pre><code class="language-yaml highlighter-rouge">
selector: [
   {
      "allow": {
         "from": [
            {
               "kind": "Service",
               "model": "kubernetes"
            }
         ],
         "to": [
            {
               "kind": "Pod",
               "model": "kubernetes"
            }
         ]
      },
      "deny": {
         "from": [
            {
               "kind": "Service",
               "model": "kubernetes"
            }
         ],
         "to": [
            {
               "kind": "Pod",
               "model": "kubernetes",
               "parent": "Deployment"
            }
         ]
      }
   }
]
</code></pre>
</details>
<p>Codify relationships leveraging your domain expertise. In this example, the relationship between the <code>Service</code> and <code>Pod</code> components in the Kubernetes model is defined with appropriate consideration of surrounding constraints (e.g. presence of a <code>Deployment</code>).</p>
<h4 id="understand-relationship-classifications">
	Understand Relationship Classifications
</h4>
<p>Relationships can be classified into three main categories:</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Hierarchical</strong> relationships involve either an ancestral connection of the components i.e. the creation/ deletion of a Component higher up affects the existence of the Components below in the lineage or a connection that involves the inheritance of features from one Component to the other.</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Parent</strong>: A parent-child relationship implies the requirement of the parent component before the child component can be created. For example, a <code>Namespace</code> in Kubernetes can be a parent of <code>Pods</code> within that namespace. The namespace must exist before creating pods within it.</li>
<li><strong>Inventory</strong>: A hierarchical inventory relationship implies the configuration of a(parent) component is patched with the configuration of other (child) component. For example, Wasm filters can inherit features and functionalities from Envoy filters. This can be used to build on existing functionalities provided by Envoy filters and further extend them using Wasm filters. It enables a modular and scalable approach to customize the behavior of the proxy while maintaining a clear hierarchy of features.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Edge</strong> relationships indicate the possibility of traffic flow between two components. They enable communication and interaction between different Components within the system.</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Mount</strong>: This subtype addresses the storage and access possibility between involved components. For example, a <code>PersistentVolume</code> can be mounted to a <code>Pod</code> to provide persistent storage for the pod&rsquo;s data.</li>
<li><strong>Network</strong>: This deals with IP addresses and DNS names and provides stable endpoints for communication. For example, a <code>Service</code> provides a stable endpoint for accessing multiple replicas of a <code>Deployment</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Firewall</strong>: This acts as an intermediary for communications which include standard networking protocols like TCP and UDP. It can enforce network policies to control traffic between components. For example, a <code>NetworkPolicy</code> can be used to manage the traffic flow between different <code>Pods</code> in the cluster.</li>
<li><strong>Permission</strong>: This defines the permissions for components if they can have a possible relationship with other Components. It ensures that only authorized Components can interact with each other. For example, a <code>Role</code> can define permissions for Components to access specific resources.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Sibling</strong> relationships represent connections between components that are at the same hierarchical level or share a common parent. Siblings can have the same or similar functionalities or may interact with each other in specific ways. These relationships facilitate communication and cooperation between components that are in the same group or category. For example, a Service and a Pod in Kubernetes are siblings as they share a common parent and are at the same hierarchical level.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p><a id="relationship-visualizations"></a></p>
<h3 id="2-classify-relationship-type-and-specify-visual-representation">
	2. Classify relationship type and specify visual representation
</h3>
<p>Browse and pick the most appropriate visualization for this relationship by using one of the predefined relationship visualizations.</p>

<p>Once selected, note the relationship&rsquo;s <code>kind</code>, <code>type</code>, and <code>subtype</code> of your selected visualization. Alternatively, if an existing visualization does not seem appropriate for the relationship, please propose a new visualization at-will. Simply use the whiteboard feature of Meshery&rsquo;s extensions to sketch out the relationship and propose it as a new visualization.</p>
<h2 id="development">
	Development
</h2>
<p><a id="relationship-definitions"></a></p>
<h3 id="3-create-a-relationship-definition-as-a-json-file">
	3. Create a Relationship Definition as a JSON file
</h3>
<p>Create a relationship definition as a JSON file, placing this new definition file into its respective model folder (see <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-models/">Contributing to Models</a>). Relationship definition files are commonly named  <code>relationships.yaml</code> as a convention, however, this name is not required. A model may include any number of relationship definitions. Include the following attributes in your relationship definition:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>kind</code>: The genre of relationship (e.g., hierarchical, edge, sibling).</li>
<li><code>type</code>: The augmentative category of the relationship (e.g., binding, non-binding, inventory).</li>
<li><code>subType</code>: The specific representative visual paradigm (e.g., parent, mount, network, wallet, badge).</li>
<li><code>selectors</code>: The scope of the relationship, including the components involved and any constraints. Selector specify to which component(s) the relationship applies or does not apply (think of in terms of the <code>AND</code> operators in a query). Selector Sets are used to combine multiple selectors for more granular control over the logic used when matchmaking (establishing a relationship) between components (think of in terms of the <code>OR</code> operators in a query).</li>
<li><code>evaluationQuery</code>: Name of the policy or policies (Open Policy Agent rego file(s)) to invoke for relationship evaluation. Identify an existing OPA policy as the <code>evaluationQuery</code> suitable to the relationship. If no policy exists, propose a new policy (rego). <em>(rarely necessary)</em> Create a new policy for the evaluation of your relationship using Rego. <em>This step is only necessary and can typically be skipped. Contact a maintainer if the relationship requires a new policy to evaluate the relationship.</em></li>
<li><code>description</code>: A characterization of the relationship, its purpose, and any constraints or considerations of its application.</li>
</ul>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Use Existing Relationships as Examples</div>
<p>Browse the <a href='https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/server/meshmodel'>existing relationships in the Meshery repository</a> to find examples of how to existing relationships, using them as a template. Alternatively, you can review a prior pull request as an example as well, for example <a href='https://github.com/meshery/meshery/pull/9880/files'>PR #9880</a>.</p>
</div>
<p><a class="anchorjs-link" id="relationship-scopes"></a></p>
<h3 id="4-configuring-the-scope-of-relationships">
	4. Configuring the Scope of Relationships
</h3>
<p>The extent to which a relationship affects components within a model or beyond a model is defined and controlled using scopes. Scopes exist at two levels in Meshery relationships.</p>
<h4 id="global-scope">
	Global Scope
</h4>
<p>Global scope is defined using the <code>model</code> and <code>version</code> attributes in the relationship definition.</p>
<p>Relationships can be confined to a specific model, a specific model version, or can be allowed to affect all models. The relationship schema has a <code>model</code> and <code>version</code> attribute which facilitates this control. For example, if the model is specified as <code>aws-ec2-controller</code>, the relationship will work for those components that belong to the <code>aws-ec2-controller</code> model.</p>
<h4 id="local-scope">
	Local Scope
</h4>
<p>Local scope is defined and controlled via <code>selectors</code> attributes in the relationship definition.</p>
<p>Relationship selectors refine the scope of applicability the relationship. It is the details included within the Selector that determines whether there is a match and relationship to be formed. These details include which models and components are involved in the relationship and any constraints in its formation. Selector specify to which component(s) the relationship applies or does not apply (think of in terms of the <code>AND</code> operators in a query). Selector Sets are used to combine multiple selectors for more granular control over the logic used when matchmaking (establishing a relationship) between components (think of in terms of the <code>OR</code> operators in a query).</p>
<!-- @leecalcote: The following needs rewritten using Selector Sets, @MUzairS15 -->
<p>Selectors are structured as an array wherein each entry comprises a <code>from</code> (self) property and a <code>to</code> (others) property. The <code>from</code> and <code>to</code> combined with the <code>allow</code> and <code>deny</code> properties delineate between components involved in a particular relationship. These entries define the constraints necessary for the existence of a relationship, thus scoping a relationship. Each item in the selector uniquely defines a relation between the components listed. i.e. <code>from</code> and <code>to</code> fields are evaluated within the context of the selector.</p>
<p>Only the components within the same selector relate to each other via 1:many kind of relation between components listed inside the <code>from</code> and <code>to</code> field. i.e. Each object inside the <code>from</code> relates to each item inside the <code>two</code> field within a particular selector.</p>
<p>When defining relationships that involve a large number of combinations between <code>from</code> and <code>to</code>, selectors sets provide a mechanism to organize and manage these relationships. This prevents the need for crafting complex deny attributes and facilitates easier maintenance. Use of selector sets enhances flexibility and reusability in the definition and configuration of relationships among components.</p>
<p><em>Note: When defining Hierarchical relationships, remember that the <code>from</code> field represents the child component, while the <code>to</code> field represents the parent component.</em></p>
<details close>
<summary>Relationship Selector Example</summary>
<pre><code class="language-yaml highlighter-rouge">
selector: [
   {
      "allow": {
         "from": [
            {
               "kind": "WASMFilter",
               "model": "istio-base",
               "patch": {
                  "patchStrategy": "replace",
                  "mutatorRef": [
                     [
                        "settings",
                        "config"
                     ],
                     [
                        "settings",
                        "wasm-filter"
                     ]
                  ],
                  "description": "WASM filter configuration to be applied to Envoy Filter."
               }
            },
            {
               "kind": "EBPFFilter",
   .....
            }
         ],
         "to": [
            {
               "kind": "EnvoyFilter",
               "model": "istio-base",
               "patch": {
                  "patchStrategy": "replace",
                  "mutatedRef": [
                     [
                        "settings",
                        "configPatches",
                        "_",
                        "patch",
                        "value"
                     ]
                  ],
                  "description": "Receive the WASM filter configuration."
               }
            },
            {
               "kind": "WASMPlugin",
   ....
            }
   ...
         ]
      },
      "deny": {
   ...
      }
   },
   {
      "allow": {
         "from": [
            {
               "kind": "ConfigMap",
               "model": "kubernetes",
               "patch": {
                  "patchStrategy": "replace",
                  "mutatorRef": [
                     [
                        "name"
                     ]
                  ],
                  "description": "In Kubernetes, ConfigMaps are a versatile resource that can be referenced by various other resources to provide configuration data to applications or other Kubernetes resources.\n\nBy referencing ConfigMaps in these various contexts, you can centralize and manage configuration data more efficiently, allowing for easier updates, versioning, and maintenance of configurations in a Kubernetes environment."
               }
            }
         ],
         "to": [
            {
               "kind": "Deployment",
               "model": "kubernetes",
               "patch": {
                  "patchStrategy": "replace",
                  "mutatedRef": [
                     [
                        "spec",
                        "containers",
                        "_",
                        "envFrom",
                        "configMapRef",
                        "name"
                     ]
                  ],
                  "description": "Deployments can reference ConfigMaps to inject configuration data into the Pods they manage. This is useful for maintaining consistent configuration across replica sets.\n\nThe keys from the ConfigMap will be exposed as environment variables to the containers within the pods managed by the Deployment."
               }
            },
            {
               "kind": "StatefulSets",
               "model": "kubernetes",
               "patch": {
   ....
               }
            }
   ...
         ]
      },
      "deny": {
   ...
      }
   }
]
</code></pre>
<br/>
<p>The <code>selector</code> defined for the relationship between <code>WasmFilter</code> and <code>EnvoyFilter</code> components (the first item in the array) is entirely independent of the <code>selector</code> identified for the relationship between <code>ConfigMap</code> and <code>Deployment</code> components. This ensures independence in how these components relate to each other while still permitting similar types of relationships.</p>
<p>This example relationship demonstrates how the <code>WASMFilter</code> and <code>EBPFFilter</code> components identified in <code>from</code> relate to other <code>EnvoyFilter</code> <code>WASMPlugin</code> components identified in <code>to</code> selector. Similarly, <code>ConfigMap</code> component identified in the <code>from</code> selector corresponds to each <code>Deployment</code>, <code>StatefulSet</code>, and so on component identified in the <code>to</code> selector.</p>
</details>
<h4 id="understanding-relationship-policies-and-their-evaluation">
	Understanding Relationship Policies and their Evaluation
</h4>
<p>The <code>evaluationQuery</code> property in your relationship definition is used to identity the name of the policy to be used by Meshery&rsquo;s evaluation engine. Meshery embeds Open Policy Agent as it&rsquo;s policy engine</p>
<p><strong>How should you determine the value for <code>evaluationQuery</code></strong></p>
<p>All relationship definitions are backed by OPA policies and each relationship depends on their <code>kind</code>, <code>type</code>, and <code>subType</code> in order to be properly evaluated. Which evaluation policy or set of policies used during the evaluation moment is defined by the <code>evaluationQuery</code> property, which follows the naming convention of combining each of their  <code>kind</code>, <code>type</code>, and <code>subType</code>  properties with an underscore and the word &ldquo;_relationship&rdquo;, like so: <code>kind_type_subtype_relationship</code>.</p>
<p>So, for example, if you are defining or updating a relationship definition with <code>kind: edge</code> and <code>type: network</code>, the value for the attribute <code>evaluationQuery</code> should be <code>edge_network_relationship</code>.</p>
<p>Each policy has a set of evaluation rules defined and the <code>evaluationQuery</code> attribute corresponds to the main rule defined inside the policy, during the policy eval the results are collected from this rule.</p>
<h2 id="postwork">
	Postwork
</h2>
<p><a id="relationship-testing"></a></p>
<h4 id="relationship-authoring-best-practices-and-considerations">
	Relationship Authoring Best Practices and Considerations
</h4>
<h5 id="general">
	General
</h5>
<ol>
<li>Use camelCasing as the formatting convention.</li>
</ol>
<h5 id="scoping">
	Scoping
</h5>
<ol>
<li>To configure a relationship to be applied across models, ensure the <code>model</code> property for those relationships is set to <code>*</code>, to limit the relationships to a specific model, specify the correct <code>model</code>(case sensitive).</li>
<li>To configure a relationship to be applied across all versions of a particular model, ensure the <code>version</code> property for those relationships is set to <code>*</code>, to limit the relationships to a specific version of a model, specify the correct model version.</li>
<li>Specify <code>version</code> property as a regex to ensure relationships are applied to a subset of versions of a model.</li>
</ol>
<h5 id="actions">
	Actions
</h5>
<ol>
<li>If a path <code>mutatedRef/mutatorRef</code> contains more than one array path then only the first array position can be specified as <code>\_</code> for others explicitly mention them as 0</li>
<li>Currently <code>mutatedRef</code> doesn’t support having an array.</li>
</ol>
<h5 id="matching">
	Matching
</h5>
<ol>
<li>Targets of a Relationship can be specific Components or entire Models.</li>
<li>Values for propoerties like <code>kind</code>, <code>version</code>, and <code>model</code> are case-sensitive.</li>
<li>Absence of a property in the <code>selector</code> is interpretted as the wildcard <code>*</code>.
<ul>
<li>For example, a selector with <code>kind: Pod</code>, <code>Model: Kubernetes</code>, and the absence of the <code>version</code> property would be interpretted as <code>version: *</code>, which
means that all the versions of the Kubernetes Pod resource (k8s.io/v1/betav2) will match the selector.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>The <code>evaluationQuery</code> property determines the OPA policy to invoke for relationship evaluation, specify the correct rego query.</li>
</ol>
<h5 id="conflicts">
	Conflicts
</h5>
<ol>
<li>Ensure that the <code>deny</code> selectors and <code>allow</code> selectors do not conflict with each other i.e. relations are not getting overlapped for <code>allow</code> and <code>deny</code> selectors.</li>
<li>In the event of conflicting Relationship Definitions, the union between them is taken.
<ul>
<li>If we have two Relationships, one from (Component A) to (Component B and Component F), and another
from (Component A) to (Component B and Component C), then it is similar to having a Relationship
from Component A to Component B, C and F</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>In the event of an overlapping set of complementary Relationship Definitions, Union.</li>
<li>In the event of an overlapping set of conflicting Relationship Definitions, no relationship type (Kind) is inherently more important than the next one, so will not be any case of conflict.</li>
</ol>
<p><a class="anchorjs-link" id="relationship-contribution"></a></p>
<h4 id="4-contribute-your-relationship-to-the-meshery-project">
	4. Contribute your relationship to the Meshery project
</h4>
<p>Submit a pull request to the Meshery repository with your new relationship definition, so that all users can benefit from the relationship(s) you have defined.</p>
<p>Keeping your relationship definition in a separate file allows for easier management and review of the relationship(s) you have defined.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Keeping your custom Relationships private</div>
<p>Alternatively, if you would like to keep the relatioship definition private, you can bundle your relatinship(s) in a custom model, import the custom model into your Meshery deployment. Your private relationship definition(s) will be registered in your Meshery Server&rsquo;s <a href='/concepts/logical/registry'>registry</a> and available for use within your Meshery deployment.</p>
</div>
<p>For more information refer - <a href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/16z5hA8qVfSq885of9LXFUVvfom-hQXr-6oTD_GgoFmk/edit">Model - Construct Models in Meshery</a></p>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Contributing to Meshery Schemas</h1>
          
          <p>This comprehensive guide covers everything you need to know to contribute to the Meshery Schemas repository. Meshery follows <strong>Schema-Driven Development (SDD)</strong>, where the structure of data is centrally defined using schemas that power consistency, validation, and code generation across the platform.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="table-of-contents">
	Table of Contents

<h2 id="overview">
	Overview
</h2>
<p>Meshery schemas offer a powerful system designed for:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Model-Driven Management</strong>: Meshery uses explicit models for describing infrastructure and applications.</li>
<li><strong>Dynamic Discovery</strong>: Process different kinds of relationships and styles for adaptive configurations.</li>
<li><strong>Lifecycle Management</strong>: Track status and lifecycle of resources via schema properties.</li>
<li><strong>Extensibility</strong>: Open-ended metadata and modular schema components enable expansion.</li>
<li><strong>Visual Representation</strong>: Properties for styling edges and nodes create user-friendly visuals.</li>
<li><strong>Automated Operations</strong>: Support validation, automated configuration, and patching.</li>
</ul>
<p>Meshery uses the <strong>OpenAPI v3</strong> specification with a <strong>modular, versioned, and extensible</strong> schema strategy:</p>
<ul>
<li>✅ <strong>Versioned schemas</strong> for backward compatibility</li>
<li>🧩 <strong>Modular constructs</strong> for maintainability and reuse</li>
<li>🧪 <strong>Schemas are used</strong> for validation, API documentation, and automatic code generation</li>
</ul>
<hr>
<h2 id="prerequisites">
	Prerequisites
</h2>
<p>Before contributing, ensure you have the following installed:</p>
<h3 id="1-go-v1240">
	1. Go (v1.24.0+)
</h3>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1"># Verify installation</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">go version
</span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="2-oapi-codegen">
	2. oapi-codegen
</h3>
<p>Essential for generating Go code from OpenAPI specifications:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">go install github.com/oapi-codegen/oapi-codegen/v2/cmd/oapi-codegen@latest
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nb">export</span> <span class="nv">PATH</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">&#34;</span><span class="si">${</span><span class="nv">GOPATH</span><span class="k">:-</span><span class="nv">$HOME</span><span class="p">/go</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2">/bin:</span><span class="nv">$PATH</span><span class="s2">&#34;</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="3-nodejs--npm">
	3. Node.js &amp; npm
</h3>
<p>Required for TypeScript generation and build process:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1"># Verify installation</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">node --version
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">npm --version
</span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="4-make">
	4. make
</h3>
<p>The repository uses Makefiles for automation:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1"># Verify installation</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">make --version
</span></span></code></pre></div><hr>
<h2 id="quick-start">
	Quick Start
</h2>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1"># Clone the repository</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">git clone https://github.com/meshery/schemas.git
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nb">cd</span> schemas
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1"># Install dependencies</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">make setup
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">npm install
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1"># Generate all code (Go, TypeScript, RTK Query)</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">make build
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1"># Build TypeScript distribution</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">npm run build
</span></span></code></pre></div><hr>
<h2 id="schema-directory-structure">
	Schema Directory Structure
</h2>
<p>All schemas are located in the <code>schemas/constructs/</code> directory:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>schemas/
├── constructs/
│   ├── &lt;schema-version&gt;/               # e.g., v1alpha1, v1beta1
│   │   └── &lt;construct&gt;/                # e.g., model, component, design
│   │       ├── api.yml                 # Index file: refs subschemas + defines API endpoints
│   │       ├── &lt;construct&gt;.yaml        # Subschema: data model definition
│   │       ├── &lt;construct&gt;_core.yml    # Subschema: core/shared types (optional)
│   │       └── templates/              # Manually defined template files
│   │           ├── &lt;construct&gt;_template.json
│   │           └── &lt;construct&gt;_template.yaml
│   │
│   ├── v1alpha1/
│   │   ├── core/
│   │   │   └── api.yml                 # Core schema definitions (timestamps, UUIDs, etc.)
│   │   └── capability/
│   │       └── api.yml
│   │
│   ├── v1alpha3/
│   │   └── relationship/
│   │       ├── api.yml
│   │       ├── relationship_core.yml
│   │       └── templates/
│   │
│   └── v1beta1/
│       ├── model/
│       │   ├── api.yml
│       │   ├── model.yaml
│       │   ├── model_core.yml
│       │   └── templates/
│       ├── component/
│       │   ├── api.yml
│       │   ├── component.yaml
│       │   └── templates/
│       ├── design/
│       ├── environment/
│       ├── workspace/
│       └── ...
│
├── models/                             # Auto-generated Go code (do NOT commit)
│   └── &lt;version&gt;/&lt;package&gt;/&lt;package&gt;.go
│
├── typescript/
│   ├── index.ts                        # Manually maintained - public API surface
│   ├── generated/                      # Auto-generated TypeScript (do NOT commit)
│   │   └── &lt;version&gt;/&lt;package&gt;/
│   │       ├── &lt;Package&gt;.d.ts          # Type definitions
│   │       └── &lt;Package&gt;Schema.ts      # Schema as JS object
│   └── rtk/                            # RTK Query client configurations
│
├── dist/                               # Built distribution (do NOT commit)
│   ├── index.js, index.d.ts
│   ├── cloudApi.js, mesheryApi.js
│   └── constructs/&lt;version&gt;/&lt;package&gt;/&lt;Package&gt;Schema.js
│
└── _openapi_build/                     # Bundled OpenAPI specs (do NOT commit)
    ├── merged_openapi.yml
    ├── cloud_openapi.yml
    └── meshery_openapi.yml
</code></pre><hr>
<h2 id="understanding-apiyml---the-construct-index-file">
	Understanding <code>api.yml</code> - The Construct Index File
</h2>
<p>Each construct directory contains an <code>api.yml</code> file that serves as the <strong>index file</strong> for that construct. This is the entry point for code generation tools.</p>
<h3 id="the-three-roles-of-apiyml">
	The Three Roles of <code>api.yml</code>
</h3>
<ol>
<li><strong>References all subschemas</strong> - Aggregates and references all related schema definitions via <code>$ref</code></li>
<li><strong>Defines API endpoints</strong> - Contains all REST operations (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) for the construct</li>
<li><strong>Acts as the entry point</strong> - Used by code generators (oapi-codegen, openapi-typescript)</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="example-apiyml-structure">
	Example <code>api.yml</code> Structure
</h3>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-yaml" data-lang="yaml"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">openapi</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">3.0.0</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">info</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">title</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Model API</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">version</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">v1beta1</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">paths</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">/api/models</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">get</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">operationId</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">getModels</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">summary</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Get all models</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">responses</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span><span class="s2">&#34;200&#34;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">description</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Success</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">content</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">            </span><span class="nt">application/json</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">              </span><span class="nt">schema</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">                </span><span class="nt">type</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">array</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">                </span><span class="nt">items</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">                  </span><span class="nt">$ref</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;#/components/schemas/ModelDefinition&#34;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">post</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">operationId</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">createModel</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">summary</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Create a new model</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="c"># ...</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">components</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">schemas</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">ModelDefinition</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">$ref</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;./model.yaml#/ModelDefinition&#34;</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c"># Reference to subschema</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">ModelReference</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">$ref</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;./model_core.yml#/ModelReference&#34;</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c"># Reference to another subschema</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span></code></pre></div><hr>
<h2 id="schema-file-roles">
	Schema File Roles
</h2>
<table>
  <thead>
      <tr>
          <th>File</th>
          <th>Purpose</th>
      </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
      <tr>
          <td><code>api.yml</code></td>
          <td><strong>Index file</strong> - aggregates all subschemas via <code>$ref</code> and defines API endpoints for the construct</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><code>&lt;construct&gt;.yaml</code></td>
          <td><strong>Subschema</strong> - defines the main data model (noun) for the construct</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><code>&lt;other-subschemas&gt;.yml</code></td>
          <td><strong>Subschema</strong> - defines core/shared types used by the main schema</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><code>templates/*.json</code></td>
          <td><strong>Templates</strong> - example instances with default values</td>
      </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<hr>
<h2 id="naming-conventions">
	Naming Conventions
</h2>
<h3 id="property-names">
	Property Names
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Use <strong>camelCase</strong> for property fields: <code>schemaVersion</code>, <code>displayName</code>, <code>componentsCount</code></li>
<li>Identifier fields use <strong>lowerCamelCase with &ldquo;Id&rdquo; suffix</strong>: <code>modelId</code>, <code>registrantId</code>, <code>categoryId</code></li>
<li>Enums use <strong>lowercase words</strong>: <code>enabled</code>, <code>ignored</code>, <code>duplicate</code></li>
</ul>
<h3 id="openapi-schema-names">
	OpenAPI Schema Names
</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>PascalCase nouns</strong> under <code>components/schemas</code>: <code>Model</code>, <code>Component</code>, <code>Design</code></li>
<li><strong>Files/folders are lowercase</strong>: <code>api.yml</code>, <code>model.yaml</code>, <code>component.yaml</code></li>
<li>Template files: <code>templates/&lt;construct&gt;_template.json</code></li>
</ul>
<h3 id="endpoints-and-operations">
	Endpoints and Operations
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Paths under <code>/api</code> with <strong>kebab-case, plural nouns</strong>: <code>/api/workspaces</code>, <code>/api/environments</code></li>
<li>Path params are <strong>camelCase</strong>: <code>{subscriptionId}</code>, <code>{connectionId}</code></li>
<li>Non-CRUD actions append a verb segment: <code>.../register</code>, <code>.../export</code>, <code>.../cancel</code></li>
<li><code>operationId</code> is <strong>camelCase VerbNoun</strong>: <code>getModels</code>, <code>createDesign</code>, <code>registerMeshmodels</code></li>
</ul>
<h3 id="versioning">
	Versioning
</h3>
<ul>
<li><code>schemaVersion</code> uses <strong>group/version</strong>: <code>models.meshery.io/v1beta1</code>, <code>components.meshery.io/v1beta1</code></li>
<li>Version strings follow <strong>k8s-style</strong>: <code>v1</code>, <code>v1alpha1</code>, <code>v1beta1</code></li>
<li>Semver fields use <strong>standard SemVer</strong>: <code>1.0.0</code>, <code>2.3.1</code></li>
</ul>
<h3 id="db-mirrored-fields">
	DB-Mirrored Fields
</h3>
<p>DB-mirrored fields such as <code>created_at</code>, <code>updated_at</code>, and <code>user_id</code> intentionally remain <strong>snake_case</strong> to mirror existing database columns. Do not rename these to camelCase.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="adding-a-new-schema">
	Adding a New Schema
</h2>
<h3 id="step-1-create-the-directory-structure">
	Step 1: Create the Directory Structure
</h3>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">mkdir -p schemas/constructs/v1beta1/mypackage/templates
</span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="step-2-create-the-index-file-apiyml">
	Step 2: Create the Index File (<code>api.yml</code>)
</h3>
<p>Create <code>schemas/constructs/v1beta1/mypackage/api.yml</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-yaml" data-lang="yaml"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">openapi</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">3.0.0</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">info</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">title</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">MyPackage API</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">version</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">v1beta1</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">description</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">API for managing MyPackage resources</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">paths</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">/api/mypackages</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">get</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">operationId</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">getMyPackages</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">summary</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Get all mypackages</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">tags</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span>- <span class="l">MyPackage</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">responses</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span><span class="s2">&#34;200&#34;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">description</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Success</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">content</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">            </span><span class="nt">application/json</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">              </span><span class="nt">schema</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">                </span><span class="nt">type</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">array</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">                </span><span class="nt">items</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">                  </span><span class="nt">$ref</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;#/components/schemas/MyPackage&#34;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">post</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">operationId</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">createMyPackage</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">summary</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Create a new mypackage</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">tags</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span>- <span class="l">MyPackage</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">requestBody</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">required</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">true</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">content</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">application/json</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">            </span><span class="nt">schema</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">              </span><span class="nt">$ref</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;#/components/schemas/MyPackage&#34;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">responses</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span><span class="s2">&#34;201&#34;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">description</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Created</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">components</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">schemas</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">MyPackage</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">$ref</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;./mypackage.yaml#/MyPackage&#34;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="step-3-create-subschema-files-optional">
	Step 3: Create Subschema Files (Optional)
</h3>
<p>Create <code>schemas/constructs/v1beta1/mypackage/mypackage.yaml</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-yaml" data-lang="yaml"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">MyPackage</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">type</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">object</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">required</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span>- <span class="l">id</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span>- <span class="l">name</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">properties</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">id</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">$ref</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">../../v1alpha1/core/api.yml#/components/schemas/uuid</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">x-order</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">1</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">name</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">type</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">string</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">description</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Name of the package</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">minLength</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">1</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">maxLength</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">100</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">x-order</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">2</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">description</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">type</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">string</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">description</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Description of the package</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">x-order</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">3</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">created_at</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">$ref</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">../../v1alpha1/core/api.yml#/components/schemas/created_at</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">x-order</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">10</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">updated_at</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">$ref</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">../../v1alpha1/core/api.yml#/components/schemas/updated_at</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">x-order</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">11</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="step-4-create-template-files">
	Step 4: Create Template Files
</h3>
<p>Create <code>schemas/constructs/v1beta1/mypackage/templates/mypackage_template.json</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-json" data-lang="json"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nt">&#34;id&#34;</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nt">&#34;name&#34;</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;Example Package&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nt">&#34;description&#34;</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;An example package instance&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nt">&#34;created_at&#34;</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;0001-01-01T00:00:00Z&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nt">&#34;updated_at&#34;</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;0001-01-01T00:00:00Z&#34;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">}</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="step-5-build-and-test">
	Step 5: Build and Test
</h3>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1"># Run the build - your schema will be automatically discovered</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">make build
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">npm run build
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1"># Verify Go code was generated</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">ls models/v1beta1/mypackage/
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1"># Verify TypeScript was generated</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">ls typescript/generated/v1beta1/mypackage/
</span></span></code></pre></div><hr>
<h2 id="modifying-existing-schemas">
	Modifying Existing Schemas
</h2>
<h3 id="adding-a-new-field">
	Adding a New Field
</h3>
<ol>
<li><strong>Update the schema / yml file</strong> (e.g., <code>model.yaml or api.yml</code>):</li>
</ol>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-yaml" data-lang="yaml"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">properties</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="c"># ... existing properties</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">newField</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">type</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">string</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">description</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Description of the new field</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">x-order</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">20</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">x-oapi-codegen-extra-tags</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">yaml</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;newField&#34;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">json</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;newField&#34;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span></code></pre></div><ol start="2">
<li><strong>Update template files</strong> with default values:</li>
</ol>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-json" data-lang="json"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nt">&#34;newField&#34;</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;default value&#34;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">}</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><ol start="3">
<li><strong>Run the build</strong>:</li>
</ol>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">make build
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">npm run build
</span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="adding-a-new-api-endpoint">
	Adding a New API Endpoint
</h3>
<p>Edit the <code>api.yml</code> file to add new paths:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-yaml" data-lang="yaml"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">paths</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="c"># ... existing paths</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="l">/api/models/{id}/export:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">post</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">operationId</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">exportModel</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">summary</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Export a model</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">parameters</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span>- <span class="nt">$ref</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;../../v1alpha1/core/api.yml#/components/parameters/id&#34;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="nt">responses</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span><span class="s2">&#34;200&#34;</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">description</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Model exported successfully</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span></code></pre></div><hr>
<h2 id="code-generation">
	Code Generation
</h2>
<p>The build system generates code from your schemas automatically.</p>
<h3 id="build-pipeline">
	Build Pipeline
</h3>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span class="line"><span class="cl">schemas/constructs/**/*.yml  (you write these)
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    │
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    ▼
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">bundle-openapi.js            (bundles + dereferences schemas)
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    │
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    ├──▶ generate-golang.js  → models/**/*.go       (Go structs via oapi-codegen)
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    ├──▶ generate-typescript.js → typescript/generated/  (TypeScript types)
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    └──▶ generate-rtk.js     → typescript/rtk/      (RTK Query hooks)
</span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="what-gets-generated">
	What Gets Generated
</h3>
<table>
  <thead>
      <tr>
          <th>Output</th>
          <th>Location</th>
          <th>Description</th>
      </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Go structs</strong></td>
          <td><code>models/&lt;version&gt;/&lt;package&gt;/</code></td>
          <td>Strongly-typed models for backend</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>TypeScript types</strong></td>
          <td><code>typescript/generated/&lt;version&gt;/&lt;package&gt;/&lt;Package&gt;.d.ts</code></td>
          <td>Interface definitions</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>TypeScript schemas</strong></td>
          <td><code>typescript/generated/&lt;version&gt;/&lt;package&gt;/&lt;Package&gt;Schema.ts</code></td>
          <td>OpenAPI schema as const JS object</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>RTK Query clients</strong></td>
          <td><code>typescript/rtk/</code></td>
          <td>Auto-generated API hooks for Redux</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><strong>Bundled OpenAPI</strong></td>
          <td><code>_openapi_build/</code></td>
          <td>Merged API specifications</td>
      </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<h3 id="build-commands">
	Build Commands
</h3>
<table>
  <thead>
      <tr>
          <th>Command</th>
          <th>Description</th>
      </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
      <tr>
          <td><code>make build</code></td>
          <td>Full build: bundles OpenAPI + generates Go/TypeScript</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><code>make bundle-openapi</code></td>
          <td>Bundle and merge OpenAPI specs only</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><code>make generate-golang</code></td>
          <td>Generate Go code (requires bundled specs)</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><code>make generate-ts</code></td>
          <td>Generate TypeScript types and schemas</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td><code>npm run build</code></td>
          <td>Build TypeScript distribution with tsup</td>
      </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<h3 id="dynamic-schema-discovery">
	Dynamic Schema Discovery
</h3>
<p>Schemas are discovered automatically by scanning <code>schemas/constructs/</code> for directories containing an <code>api.yml</code> file. No manual configuration needed!</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="vendor-extensions-x--annotations">
	Vendor Extensions (<code>x-*</code> Annotations)
</h2>
<p>OpenAPI vendor extensions provide metadata that the Meshery build pipeline uses to control code generation behavior.</p>
<h3 id="x-oapi-codegen-extra-tags">
	<code>x-oapi-codegen-extra-tags</code>
</h3>
<p>Added to individual properties to inject custom Go struct tags into generated code. Commonly used for JSON, YAML, and database column mappings.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-yaml" data-lang="yaml"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">roleName</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">type</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">string</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">x-oapi-codegen-extra-tags</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">json</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;role_name,omitempty&#34;</span><span class="w">
