You detect a part of existing code that is not following the schema driven development principle (model is a struct created in mesheryctl command), you have two options:</p>
<ul>
<li>If you know how to implement, update the existing code to use a proper struct generated from the <code>meshery/schemas</code> repository
<ul>
<li>Update the CLI logic</li>
<li>Add/Adjust tests if needed</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>If you don&rsquo;t know how to implement it, open an issue on Github using either a mesheryctl issue template (<a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/issues/new?template=mesheryctl_feature.md">feature</a>, <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/issues/new?template=mesheryctl_bug.md">bug</a>)</li>
</ul>
<p>c. Add a new schema on an existing command</p>
<p><strong>Steps:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Add the new verb in <code>openapi.yaml</code> under the appropriate construct (e.g., <code>model/</code>)</li>
<li>Update <code>&lt;construct&gt;.json</code> if new properties are needed</li>
<li>Run:</li>
</ul>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">make generate-types
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">make golang-generate 
</span></span></code></pre></div><ul>
<li>Update the CLI logic</li>
<li>Add/Adjust tests if needed</li>
</ul>
<blockquote>
<p><em>Why it matters:</em> This reduces drift between backend logic and API contract, enforces consistency between Meshery&rsquo;s components (Server, UI, CLI) and , resulting in higher quality code.</p>
</blockquote>
<h3 id="2-meshery-server-contributor-flow">
	2. Meshery Server Contributor Flow
</h3>
<p><strong>Example:</strong> Add a new <code>status</code> field to <code>component</code>.
<strong>Steps:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Add the new property in <code>component.json</code></li>
<li>Run:</li>
</ul>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">make validate-schemas
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">make golang-generate
</span></span></code></pre></div><ul>
<li>The generated Go structs (from <code>oapi-codegen</code>) are used in the backend.</li>
<li>If the backend uses GORM with auto-migration enabled, these structs may be used to update the DB schema.</li>
<li>Avoid manually editing the generated models, as they will be overwritten when schemas are regenerated.</li>
</ul>
<blockquote>
<p><em>Why it matters:</em> This reduces drift between backend logic and API contract, enforces consistency between Meshery&rsquo;s components (Server, UI, CLI) and , resulting in higher quality code.</p>
</blockquote>
<h3 id="3-meshery-ui-contributor-flow">
	3. Meshery UI Contributor Flow
</h3>
<p><strong>Example:</strong> Show the new <code>version</code> field on the Model dashboard.
<strong>Steps:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Check <code>openapi.yaml</code> to verify the new field exists</li>
<li>Wait for the backend to regenerate and expose the property</li>
<li>Use RTK + TypeScript types to access and render data</li>
</ul>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Note</strong>: <code>make generate-types</code> now generates only TypeScript types and schema-related objects. <code>_template.json</code> / <code>_template.yaml</code> files are no longer auto-generated.</p>
</blockquote>
<p><em>Why it matters:</em> UI stays in sync with the backend - fewer bugs, fewer mismatches, easier onboarding.</p>
<h3 id="4-meshery-docs-contributor-flow">
	4. Meshery Docs Contributor Flow
</h3>
<p><strong>Example:</strong> You are writing a guide!
<strong>Steps:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Read the schema structure and workflows</li>
<li>Walk through the scenarios above</li>
<li>Write a guide that&rsquo;s accurate, actionable, and friendly</li>
</ul>
<p><em>Why it matters:</em> Docs are often the first impression contributors get. Schema-driven clarity starts here.</p>
<h2 id="getting-help">
	Getting Help
</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/issues">GitHub Issues</a> - Report bugs or request features</li>
<li><a href="https://slack.meshery.io">Community Slack</a> - Real-time discussions with maintainers</li>
<li><a href="https://meshery.io/calendar">Weekly Meetings</a> - Join our community calls</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="further-reading">
	Further Reading
</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/blob/master/README.md">meshery/schemas README</a> - Full reference for schema authoring</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/blob/master/AGENTS.md">AGENTS.md</a> - Contributor checklist</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/blob/master/schemas/constructs/v1alpha1/core/api.yml">Core schema definitions</a> - Reusable building blocks</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/blob/master/schemas/constructs/v1beta1/academy/api.yml">Academy construct</a> - Exemplar for advanced patterns including <code>x-generate-db-helpers</code></li>
</ul>
<hr>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Community Resources</strong>
For more contribution guidelines, see the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md">Meshery Contributing Guide</a>.</p>
</blockquote>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Contributing to Meshery Server Events</h1>
          
          <p>Meshery incorporates an internal events publication mechanism that provides users with real-time updates on the processes occurring within the Meshery server when interacting with its endpoints. It ensures that users are kept in the loop regarding the ongoing activities within the API, and guides users towards future steps to resolve issues. This guide will provide step-by-step instructions on sending events from the server, including when to trigger events and what information to include.</p>
<p>First, let&rsquo;s take a look at how the event object is constructed,</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 eventBuilder := events.NewEvent()
                  .ActedUpon(UUID)
                  .FromUser(UUID)
                  .FromSystem(UUID)
                  .WithCategory(string)
                  .WithAction(string)
                  .WithSeverity(EventSeverity)
                  .WithDescription(string)
                  .WithMetadata(map[string]interface{})
                  .Build()
  </div>
 </pre>
<p>  </p>
<p><em>Note: <code>events</code> is a package <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit">github.com/meshery/meshkit/models/events</a> from MeshKit containing source code of event related functionality</em></p>
<p>The event mechanism utilizes <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Builder_pattern">builder pattern</a> to construct event objects, <code>events.NewEvent()</code> creates an instance of <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit/blob/ea3c60907a1cd1902902a4113206579992772083/models/events/build.go#L9">EventBuilder</a> type, which functions as a builder class for constructing <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit/blob/ea3c60907a1cd1902902a4113206579992772083/models/events/events.go#L37">Event</a> objects.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>ActedUpon(UUID)</code> : it takes <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/gofrs/uuid#UUID">UUID</a> of the resource being provisioned on the server, and the events are associated with that resource.</li>
<li><code>FromUser()</code> : it takes <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/gofrs/uuid#UUID">UUID</a> of the user initiating the HTTP request to the server. This enables the server to publish events intended for that specific user in response.</li>
<li><code>FromSystem(UUID)</code> : it takes <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/gofrs/uuid#UUID">UUID</a> of the running meshery instance (Handler instance contains it <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/c73d3687da3eb3b2aaaabbd27e91f99906fc5838/server/handlers/handler_instance.go#L29"><code>h.SystemID</code></a>).</li>
<li><code>WithCategory</code> : The string argument to specify under which category this event falls, For example, when a user is provisioning a Kubernetes connection, the specified category for the event is &ldquo;connection.</li>
<li><code>WithAction</code> : The string argument to specify the type of action the server is performing, for instance, when registering a Kubernetes connection, the action would be &ldquo;register&rdquo;.</li>
</ul>
<p><em>Note: categories and actions must be in snake case,</em>
example categories: <strong>&ldquo;signup_request&rdquo;, &ldquo;github_artifacts&rdquo;</strong>.
example actions: <strong>&ldquo;remove_from_organization&rdquo;, &ldquo;add_to_organization&rdquo;</strong>.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>WithSeverity</code>: it takes <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit/blob/ea3c60907a1cd1902902a4113206579992772083/models/events/events.go#L75">EventSeverity</a> (underlying type is string), to specify severity of the event to bring user&rsquo;s attention to the event accordingly.</li>
</ul>
<p><em>Note: In certain conditions you must add some fields with specific keys:</em></p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>If the severity is &ldquo;Error&rdquo;, include a field in Metadata using the key <code>err</code> with the corresponding error value.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>When you want to add a link to meshery docs, include a field in Metadata using the key <code>doc</code> with the corresponding link value.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>WithDescription</code> : The string argument provides a detailed, descriptive message that depicts the specific operation or action being executed on the server.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>WithMetadata</code>: it takes a Map <code>map[string]interface{}</code> data structure containing any supplementary information that the developer/contributor deems essential for the user to be informed about.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>Build</code> : returns the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit/blob/ea3c60907a1cd1902902a4113206579992772083/models/events/events.go#L37">Event</a> instance constructed upon the previously described functions and prepares it for publication through the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/1b5d78ed34648e0a91df8c2273026b930f748fbc/server/models/event_broadcast.go#L14">Broadcast</a>, which is responsible for disseminating events.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<a href="/project/contributing/images/events-table.png">
    <img src="/project/contributing/images/events-table.png" alt="Event Schema" style="width:50%;">
</a>
<h2 id="event-persistence-in-meshery">
	Event Persistence in Meshery
</h2>
<p>Events in Meshery are persisted through two distinct mechanisms to ensure reliable event management. <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/providers/">Read more about providers</a>.</p>
<h3 id="local-event-storage">
	Local Event Storage
</h3>
<p>The <code>provider.PersistEvent(*event,nil)</code> method stores all events in Meshery&rsquo;s local database. This method works identically for both Local and Remote providers, ensuring events are always accessible within your Meshery instance.</p>
<h3 id="remote-event-publishing">
	Remote Event Publishing
</h3>
<p>The <code>provider.PublishEventToProvider(token, event)</code> method enables event synchronization with remote providers (like Meshery Cloud). For Local providers, this method is a no-op (does nothing), while Remote providers use it to send events to their remote services.</p>
<p>To see it in action and gain a better understanding, you can explore the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/server/handlers/design_engine_handler.go">design_engine_handler.go</a> file.</p>
<h2 id="an-example-in-code">
	An Example in Code
</h2>
<pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
func (h *Handler) KubernetesPingHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request, _ *models.Preference, user *models.User, provider models.Provider) {
	userID := uuid.FromStringOrNil(user.ID)
	token, ok := req.Context().Value(models.TokenCtxKey).(string)
	if !ok {
		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusInternalServerError)
		fmt.Fprintf(w, "failed to get the token for the user")
		return
	}

	connectionID := req.URL.Query().Get("connection_id")
	eventBuilder := events.NewEvent().FromUser(userID).FromSystem(*h.SystemID).WithCategory("connection").WithAction("ping")
	if connectionID != "" {
		// Get the context associated with this ID
		k8sContext, err := provider.GetK8sContext(token, connectionID)
		eventBuilder.ActedUpon(uuid.FromStringOrNil(connectionID))
		if err != nil {
			eventBuilder.WithSeverity(events.Error).WithDescription(fmt.Sprintf("Encountered an issue while retrieving kubernetes context for connection ID `%s`", connectionID)).
			WithMetadata(map[string]interface{}{
				"error": err,
			})
			event := eventBuilder.Build()
		    _ = provider.PersistEvent(*event,nil)
		    go h.config.EventBroadcaster.Publish(userID, event)
			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusInternalServerError)
			fmt.Fprintf(w, "failed to get kubernetes context for the given ID")
			return
		}
		eventBuilder.WithSeverity(events.Success).WithDescription("Retrieved kubernetes context successfully").
		WithMetadata(map[string]interface{}{
			"Context Name":   k8sContext.Name,
			"Server Address": k8sContext.Server,
		})
		event := eventBuilder.Build()
		_ = provider.PersistEvent(*event,nil)
		go h.config.EventBroadcaster.Publish(userID, event)

		// Remaining code ...
    }
}
 </div>
</pre>
<p>  </p>
<p>In the given code block, the &ldquo;resource&rdquo; refers to the connection on which the server is performing the &ldquo;ping&rdquo; action. The &ldquo;ActedUpon&rdquo; field is supplied with the &ldquo;connectionID&rdquo; value obtained from the query parameter. <code>provider.GetK8sContext</code> returns the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/995ab671a12013088f874430cfa2c0f025b073d2/server/models/k8s_context.go#L26">K8sContext</a> object which serves as a representation of a Kubernetes context within the Meshery. if <code>provider.GetK8sContext</code> returns an error, the event is constructed with severity <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit/blob/ea3c60907a1cd1902902a4113206579992772083/models/events/events.go#L18">Error</a>, description and enriched with metadata fields to provide the user with a complete context about the event.</p>
<p>If <code>provider.GetK8sContext</code> succeeds, an event with a <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshkit/blob/ea3c60907a1cd1902902a4113206579992772083/models/events/events.go#L21">Success</a> severity level is constructed. The event includes a success message and metadata containing the context name and the address of the Kubernetes API server, obtained from the operation. This information aims to provide users with relevant details about the successful operation.</p>
<p>after constructing the Event object using the Build function, event is stored into database for records and subsequently published in a new goroutine through <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/995ab671a12013088f874430cfa2c0f025b073d2/server/models/handlers.go#L241">EventBroadcaster</a> member variable of <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/995ab671a12013088f874430cfa2c0f025b073d2/server/models/handlers.go#L206">HandlerConfig</a>, which is part of <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/995ab671a12013088f874430cfa2c0f025b073d2/server/handlers/handler_instance.go#L18">Handler</a> instance.</p>
<p>To gain a deeper understanding and examine events more closely, you can explore the source code files <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/server/handlers/k8sconfig_handler.go">k8config_handler.go</a> and <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/server/handlers/design_engine_handler.go">design_engine_handler.go</a> within the Meshery project&rsquo;s codebase.</p>
<h2 id="sending-events-to-meshery-server">
	Sending Events to Meshery Server
</h2>
<p>Meshery has two primary clients: Mesheryctl and Meshery UI. Both clients will produce multiple events throughout their lifecycle. Meshery Server is designed to accept these client-generated events and broadcast them using the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/1b5d78ed34648e0a91df8c2273026b930f748fbc/server/models/event_broadcast.go#L14">Broadcaster</a>.</p>
<p>Clients can send HTTP POST requests to <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/reference/rest-apis#api-events"><code>api/events</code></a> with the event encapsulated in a JSON request body. Upon receiving an event, the server processes, validates, and broadcasts it using the Broadcaster. This ensures that all relevant events generated by Mesheryctl and Meshery UI are effectively communicated and managed by the Meshery Server.</p>
<h3 id="example">
	Example
</h3>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-javascript" data-lang="javascript"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">async</span> <span class="kd">function</span> <span class="nx">sendClientEvent</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">clientId</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">eventPayload</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="c1">// Create a new event
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="kr">const</span> <span class="nx">event</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">category</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;client_event&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">action</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;create&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">severity</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;info&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">description</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;Client event creation&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">metadata</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="nx">eventPayload</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">};</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="k">try</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="c1">// Send event to Meshery Server
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="kr">const</span> <span class="nx">response</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kr">await</span> <span class="nx">fetch</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">&#34;http://localhost:9081/api/events&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="nx">method</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;POST&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="nx">headers</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">        <span class="s2">&#34;Content-Type&#34;</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;application/json&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="p">},</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="nx">body</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="nx">JSON</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">stringify</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">event</span><span class="p">),</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="p">});</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="k">if</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="nx">response</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">ok</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="k">throw</span> <span class="k">new</span> <span class="nb">Error</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sb">`Server returned non-200 status: </span><span class="si">${</span><span class="nx">response</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">status</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="sb">`</span><span class="p">);</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">console</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">log</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">&#34;Event sent successfully&#34;</span><span class="p">);</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">}</span> <span class="k">catch</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">error</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">console</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">error</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">&#34;Failed to send event:&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">error</span><span class="p">);</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nx">sendClientEvent</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">clientId</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">eventPayload</span><span class="p">);</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Contributing to Meshery Server</h1>
          
          <p>As a new contributor, you’re going to want to familiarize with the project in order to resolve the issues in the best way. Installing and playing around with Meshery will give you context for any issues that you might work on.</p>
<p>Once an issue has been addressed, you’ll need to test it as well. Ideally, these tests are run from the user’s perspective (someone running Meshery in a container), not from a contributor’s perspective (someone running Meshery as a locally-compiled service).</p>
<h2 id="compiling-and-running-meshery-server">
	Compiling and Running Meshery server
</h2>
<p>To build and run Meshery server from source:</p>
<ol>
<li>First, build the static assets for the UI by running</li>
</ol>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make ui-setup
make ui-build</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<ol start="2">
<li>Next, build &amp; run the server code by running</li>
</ol>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make server</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Any time changes are made to the Go code, you will have to stop the server and run the above command again.
Once the Meshery server is up and running, you should be able to access Meshery on your <code>localhost</code> on port <code>9081</code> at <code>http://localhost:9081</code>. One thing to note, you might NOT see the <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-server/#contributing-ui">Meshery UI</a> until the UI code is built as well.
After running Meshery server, you will need to select your <strong>Cloud Provider</strong> by navigating to <code>localhost:9081</code>. Only then you will be able to use the Meshery UI on port <code>3000</code>.</p>
<p><strong>Please note</strong>: If you get error while starting the server as <strong>&ldquo;Meshery Development Incompatible&rdquo;</strong> then follow the below guideline 👇</p>
<a href="/project/contributing/images/meshery-development-incompatible-error.png">
  <img style= "max-width: 450px;" src="/project/contributing/images/meshery-development-incompatible-error.png" />
</a>
<p>Potential Solution:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Go to your meshery folder in your local-system where you’ve cloned it.
Execute:</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>git remote add upstream https://github.com/meshery/meshery</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>git fetch upstream</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Restart the meshery server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Additionally, before restarting the server, if you like to pull the latest changes, you can do: <code>git pull upstream master</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="building-docker-image">
	Building Docker image
</h4>
<p>To build a Docker image of Meshery, please ensure you have <code>Docker</code> installed to be able to build the image. Now, run the following command to build the Docker image:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make docker</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h4 id="define-and-validate-errors">
	Define and validate errors
</h4>
<p>Every Golang-based component within the Meshery ecosystem incorporates a utility to define and manage error messages for every error instance. This is internally done with several make commands, but one can explicitly validate with the help of the following make command. This checks and validates the errors that are present in the particular project.</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make error</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>For more details, <a href="/project/contributing/contributing-error">Error Utility</a></p>
<h3 id="configuring-log-levels-at-runtime">
	Configuring Log levels at Runtime
</h3>
<p>The server log levels can be configured at runtime by changing the env variable <code>LOG_LEVEL</code> defined in file <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/server/cmd/server-config.env"><code>server-config.env</code></a>. The configuration library (<code>viper</code>) watches for the env file, any change in the file content results in the <code>file_system</code> event to be emitted and the log level is updated accordingly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Should there be any alterations to the location or name of the environment file, it will result in the inability to configure log levels during runtime. In the event of such modifications, it is essential to update the server to preserve proper functionality.</em></strong></p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code class="language-Available" data-lang="Available"> - Panic - 0
 - Fatal - 1
 - Error - 2
 - Warn  - 3
 - Info  - 4
 - Debug - 5
 - Trace level - 6
</code></pre><p>The default setting for the <code>LOG_LEVEL</code> is <code>4</code> (Info). However, if the <code>DEBUG</code> environmental variable is configured as <code>TRUE</code>, it supersedes the value set in the <code>LOG_LEVEL</code> environmental variable, and the logging level is then adjusted to <code>5</code>(Debug).</p>
<h3 id="runtime-configuration-environment-variables">
	Runtime Configuration Environment Variables
</h3>
<p>Meshery Server supports several runtime configuration environment variables that control various aspects of server behavior:</p>
<h4 id="provider-and-extension-configuration">
	Provider and Extension Configuration
</h4>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong><code>PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES_FILEPATH</code></strong>: Specifies a local file path to load provider capabilities from a static JSON file instead of fetching from the remote provider&rsquo;s endpoint. Useful for offline development and testing.</p>
<ul>
<li>Default: Not set (capabilities fetched from remote provider)</li>
<li>Example: <code>PROVIDER_CAPABILITIES_FILEPATH=/path/to/capabilities.json</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong><code>SKIP_DOWNLOAD_EXTENSIONS</code></strong>: Controls whether Meshery downloads and refreshes provider extension packages during login and capability refresh operations.</p>
<ul>
<li>Default: <code>false</code> (extensions are downloaded/refreshed)</li>
<li>Example: <code>SKIP_DOWNLOAD_EXTENSIONS=true</code></li>
<li>Use cases: Development environments, pre-packaged deployments, reducing startup time</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="kubernetes-configuration">
	Kubernetes Configuration
</h4>
<ul>
<li><strong><code>KUBECONFIG_FOLDER</code></strong>: Specifies the folder path where Meshery should look for Kubernetes configuration files. This allows you to provide a Meshery deployment with a predefined Kubernetes context.
<ul>
<li>Default: <code>$HOME/.kube</code> (or <code>/home/appuser/.kube</code> in containerized deployments)</li>
<li>Example: <code>KUBECONFIG_FOLDER=/home/appuser/.kube</code></li>
<li>Use cases: Custom kubeconfig locations, pre-configured Kubernetes contexts, containerized deployments</li>
<li>Note: Meshery looks for a <code>config</code> file within this folder (e.g., <code>/home/appuser/.kube/config</code>)</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="other-configuration-variables">
	Other Configuration Variables
</h4>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong><code>SKIP_DOWNLOAD_CONTENT</code></strong>: Skips downloading seed content for patterns, filters, and applications.</p>
<ul>
<li>Default: <code>false</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong><code>SKIP_COMP_GEN</code></strong>: Skips component generation during startup.</p>
<ul>
<li>Default: <code>false</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong><code>PLAYGROUND</code></strong>: Enables playground mode for Meshery.</p>
<ul>
<li>Default: <code>false</code></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="using-custom-meshkit-code-for-meshery-server-development">
	Using custom Meshkit code for Meshery server development
</h3>
<ol>
  <li>
    <p>Checkout <strong>meshery</strong> and <strong>meshkit</strong> repository in adjacent directories.</p>
    
    
    <pre class="codeblock-pre">
    	<div class="codeblock">
    		<code class="clipboardjs">$ git clone https://github.com/meshery/meshery.git
        $ git clone https://github.com/meshery/meshkit.git</code>
    	</div>
    </pre>

  </li>
  <li>
    <p>In your <code>meshery</code> go.mod, update the meshkit package.</p>
    
    
    <pre class="codeblock-pre">
    	<div class="codeblock">
    		<code class="clipboardjs">github.com/meshery/meshkit =&gt; ../meshkit</code>
    	</div>
    </pre>

    <p>Remember to remove this go.mod change when creating pull requests.</p>
  </li>
</ol>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

            <h1>Contributing to Meshery UI - Notification Center</h1>
          
          <div class="prereqs"><p><strong style="font-size: 20px;">Prerequisite Reading</strong></p>
  <ol><li><a href="contributing-ui">Contributing to Meshery UI</a></li></ol>
</div>
<h2 id="table-of-contents">
	Table of Contents
</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#what-is-the-notification-center">What is the Notification Center?</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#metadata-formatter">Metadata Formatter</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#how-notification-metadata-is-rendered">How Notification Metadata is Rendered</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#types-of-event-specific-notification-formatters">Types of Event Specific Notification Formatters</a>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#common-formatter">Common Formatter</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#error-formatter">Error Formatter</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#model-registration-formatter">Model Registration Formatter</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#relationship-evaluation-formatter">Relationship Evaluation Formatter</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#dry-run-formatter">Dry Run Formatter</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#deployment-summary-formatter">Deployment Summary Formatter</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#propertyformatters-and-propertylinkformatters">PropertyFormatters and PropertyLinkFormatters</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<video style="width:min(100%,750px)" height="auto" autoplay muted loop>
  <source src="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/assets/65964225/345672de-3f61-4be0-b3c8-0e7480cc496c" type="video/mp4">

<h2 id="what-is-the-notification-center">
	What is the Notification Center?
</h2>
<p>The Notification Center is a dedicated panel in Meshery’s UI that helps you monitor, understand, and respond to events across your system. It acts as a central place where you can see important updates related to your infrastructure, workloads, and Meshery’s internal operations.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Want to understand how users interact with the Notification Center? <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides/infrastructure-management/notification-management">Learn more here</a>.</p>
</blockquote>
<hr>
<p>The <code>NotificationCenter</code> component of Meshery UI Switching to Graphql subscriptions and implementing robust filtering. Events are persisted in Meshery Server and state management on client is done using Redux Toolkit and RTK.</p>
<h3 id="user-facing-features">
	User-facing Features
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Robust filtering support inspired by GitHub&rsquo;s notification filtering style.
<ul>
<li>Search is also included.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Proper hierarchial presentation of error details, including probable cause and suggested remeditation.</li>
<li>Support for notification status (notifications can be marked as read and unread)
<ul>
<li><em>Future: Notifications can be acknowledged or resolved.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Event-based notification via Graphql subscription (provided by Meshery Server and any upstream components or externally managed systems, like Kubernetes)</li>
<li>Infinite scroll for pagination.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="state-management-and-internal-details">
	State Management and Internal Details
</h3>
<ul>
<li>The State on client is managed using <code>Redux Tooltik</code> and <code>Rtk-query</code></li>
<li>Update and Delete operations are optimistically handled.</li>
<li>Network Request are cached and are invalidated when new events come or events are deleted/updated.</li>
<li>Due to need for infinite scroll and optimistic update the events are stored globally in Redux.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="bulk-operations">
	Bulk Operations
</h3>
<p>Bulk operations in the Notification Center allow users to perform actions like deleting multiple notifications or changing the status of multiple notifications in a batch. This documentation outlines the key features and functionality of bulk operations, including the restriction of performing only one bulk operation at a time, the disabling of buttons during ongoing operations, and the display of a loading icon to indicate ongoing activity.</p>
<h3 id="initiating-a-bulk-operation">
	Initiating a Bulk Operation
</h3>
<ul>
<li>Users select the notifications they want to include in the bulk operation. This is typically done by checking checkboxes next to each notification.</li>
<li>After selecting notifications, users trigger the desired bulk operation (e.g., delete or change status) by clicking the corresponding action button.</li>
<li>Once initiated, the bulk operation begins processing the selected notifications.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="metadata-formatter">
	Metadata Formatter
</h2>
<p>When the server sends an event, it follows a consistent schema that contains metadata intended for user presentation. This metadata typically includes fields such as <code>description</code>, <code>date</code>, <code>user_id</code>, <code>system_id</code>, <code>action</code>, and the resources involved.</p>
<p>In some cases, the metadata may also contain more detailed information—such as a traceback, a summary, or a complete error log—which is dynamically generated at runtime and encapsulated within the event.</p>
<p>Presenting this structured information in a clear and accessible way is essential, as it provides valuable insights into system behavior and ongoing operations.</p>
<p>To accomplish this task, we employ metadata formatters that transform structured data into visually appealing formats. There are currently two types of formatters in use:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Metadata Specific Formatters:</strong> These formatters are specifically designed for particular types of metadata, such as Error and DryRunResponse. Metadata Specific Formatters are implemented as React components that take the metadata as input and render it within the component.</li>
<li><strong>Dynamic Formatter:</strong> Since metadata can vary significantly in structure, it is not practical to create a specific formatter for each kind. Dynamic formatters analyze the schema&rsquo;s structure and apply custom-defined rules for formatting:
<ul>
<li>Text strings are rendered using the BodySectionRenderer (more on this later).</li>
<li>Arrays are rendered using the ArrayRenderer.</li>
<li>Key-value pairs are rendered using the KeyValueRenderer.</li>
<li>Nested objects are recursively rendered.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="bodysectionrenderer">
	BodySectionRenderer
</h3>
<p>The BodySectionRenderer is responsible for formatting and rendering raw text strings into React components. During this process, it parses the string to replace external links with <code>&lt;Link&gt;</code> components and checks if the link matches predefined sites to render the link accordingly.</p>
<h3 id="arrayrenderer">
	ArrayRenderer
</h3>
<p>The ArrayRenderer is responsible for rendering an array of items in a recursive manner, presenting them as a bulletized list using the MetdataFormatter.</p>
<h3 id="keyvaluerenderer">
	KeyValueRenderer
</h3>
<p>Object properties with string values are considered key-value pairs and are rendered as such.</p>
<h3 id="the-metadata-specific-formatter">
	The Metadata Specific Formatter
</h3>
<p>Certain metadata, such as Kubernetes responses and Errors, hold high importance and have dedicated renderers. These dedicated renderers can still utilize the dynamic formatter to format specific parts of the response, such as DryRunResponse.</p>
<h3 id="reusability">
	Reusability
</h3>
<p>While this system was initially developed for our events and notification center, the components it comprises are highly reusable and can be employed in other contexts where dynamic formatting of structured data is required.</p>
<h2 id="how-notification-metadata-is-rendered">
	How Notification Metadata is Rendered
</h2>
<p>When a notification event is received from the server, it includes a <code>metadata</code> field containing structured, event-specific information. The purpose of formatters is to present this data in a clean, readable, and user-friendly format inside the expanded view of each notification.</p>
<p>The core logic for rendering metadata is handled by the <code>FormattedMetadata</code> component in <code>metadata.js</code>, which follows this decision tree:</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Event-Specific Formatter Check</strong><br>
If a formatter exists for the event&rsquo;s type (registered under <code>EventTypeFormatters</code>), that dedicated formatter is used to fully control how the metadata is displayed.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Fallback to Property-Based Formatting</strong><br>
If no event-specific formatter is found, the <code>FormattedMetadata</code> component falls back to the <code>FormatStructuredData</code> function (also in <code>metadata.js</code>).</p>
<ul>
<li>This function renders each key-value pair from the <code>metadata</code> using the mappings defined in:
<ul>
<li><code>PropertyFormatters</code> – for structured or specialized visual formats.</li>
<li><code>PropertyLinkFormatters</code> – for rendering clickable links (e.g., file paths, URLs).</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="key-files-and-directories">
	Key Files and Directories
</h3>
<p>This section outlines the essential files and folders that you&rsquo;ll interact with when working on Notification Center metadata formatters.</p>
<h4 id="notificationcenter-root-directory">
	<code>NotificationCenter/</code> <em>(Root Directory)</em>
</h4>
<ul>
<li><strong>index.js</strong>: Contains the main context provider (<code>NotificationCenterProvider</code>), the drawer component (<code>NotificationCenterDrawer</code>), and orchestrates the overall structure.</li>
<li><strong>metadata.js</strong>: Defines <code>PropertyFormatters</code>, <code>LinkFormatters</code>, <code>PropertyLinkFormatters</code>, and <code>EventTypeFormatters</code>. Contains the <code>FormattedMetadata</code> component which decides <em>how</em> to format the metadata based on event type or specific properties.</li>
<li><strong>notification.js</strong>: Defines how an individual notification is rendered.</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="formatters-notificationcenterformatters">
	<code>formatters/</code> <em>(NotificationCenter/formatters)</em>
</h4>
<p>This directory houses reusable formatter components dedicated to specific types of metadata or event types.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>common.js</strong>: Contains shared components like <code>TitleLink</code>, <code>DataToFileLink</code>, <code>EmptyState</code>.</li>
<li><strong>error.js</strong>: Defines <code>ErrorMetadataFormatter</code> for displaying structured error details.</li>
<li><strong>model_registration.js</strong>: Contains formatters for model import/registration events (<code>ModelImportMessages</code>, <code>ModelImportedSection</code>).</li>
<li><strong>pattern_dryrun.js</strong>: Defines <code>DryRunResponseFormatter</code> which utilizes components from <code>DesignLifeCycle</code>.</li>
<li><strong>relationship_evaluation.js</strong>: Defines <code>RelationshipEvaluationEventFormatter</code> responsible for rendering notifications related to the evaluation of relationships between components in a design.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="types-of-event-specific-notification-formatters">
	Types of Event Specific Notification Formatters
</h2>
<h3 id="common-formatter">
	Common Formatter
</h3>
<p>The following reusable components standardize how notification links, empty states, and downloadable traces are displayed:</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>TitleLink</strong>: Renders a styled title with an external link icon.<br>
Props:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>href</code> (required): URL of the link.</li>
<li><code>children</code>: The link text.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>EmptyState</strong>: Displays a description when no specific data is available for an event.<br>
Props:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>event.description</code> (optional): Text description of the event.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>DataToFileLink</strong>: Converts event data into a downloadable <code>.txt</code> file.<br>
Props:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>data</code> (required): Can be a string or JSON object.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="error-formatter">
	Error Formatter
</h3>
<p>The <code>ErrorMetadataFormatter</code> is used for formatting error-related notifications in the Meshery UI Notification Center. It structures error details, probable causes, and suggested remediations in a readable format.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Details</strong>: A comprehensive explanation of the error, often broken into multiple points or steps.</li>
<li><strong>Probable Cause</strong>: A list of potential reasons why the error occurred, helping the user understand the root cause.</li>
<li><strong>Suggested Remediation</strong>: Actionable steps or recommendations to resolve the issue.</li>
<li>Inside the ellipse menu, the user can find the error code docs link for further explanation of the error.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Props:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><code>metadata</code> (object): Contains error metadata fields such as:
<ul>
<li><code>LongDescription</code>: Provides details about the error.</li>
<li><code>ProbableCause</code>: Lists possible reasons for the error.</li>
<li><code>SuggestedRemediation</code>: Suggests solutions to fix the error.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><code>event</code> (object, optional): Contains the notification event data.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Path:</strong> <code>ui/components/NotificationCenter/formatters/error.js</code></p>
<p><strong>Example:</strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-javascript" data-lang="javascript"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">ErrorMetadataFormatter</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nx">metadata</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">LongDescription</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;An unexpected error occurred while deploying the mesh.&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">ProbableCause</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;Misconfigured Kubernetes cluster.&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">SuggestedRemediation</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;Check your kubeconfig file and retry deployment.&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nx">event</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">description</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;Mesh deployment failed&#34;</span> <span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="err">/&gt;</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><p><a href="/project/contributing/images/error-formatter.png"><img alt="Error Formatter" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/project/contributing/images/error-formatter.png" /></a></p>
<p><strong>When to Use:</strong></p>
<p>The <code>ErrorMetadataFormatter</code> is used when dealing with structured error events that follow a pattern (description, cause, remediation). A new formatter should be created only if the error metadata deviates significantly from the <code>ErrorMetadataFormatter</code> metadata structure.</p>
<h3 id="model-registration-formatter">
	Model Registration Formatter
</h3>
<p>The <code>Model Registration Formatter</code> formats and displays model registration details, including components and relationships, in Meshery UI&rsquo;s Notification Center. It ensures structured representation of imported models and error handling during the import process.</p>
<p><strong>Path:</strong> <code>ui/components/NotificationCenter/formatters/model_registration.js</code></p>
<p><strong>Components:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>UnsuccessfulEntityWithError</strong>: This component is used to handle error cases during model import. It identifies the type and count of entities that failed to import.</p>
<p><strong>Props:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><code>modelName</code> (string): The name of the model being imported.</li>
<li><code>error</code> (object): Contains details about the error encountered during import.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>ModelImportedSection</strong>: Displays the details of the imported model along with components, relationships, and any errors that occur.</p>
<p><strong>Props:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><code>modelDetails</code> (object) – Contains model import data.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<p><a href="/project/contributing/images/model-register-formatter.png"><img alt="Model Register Formatter" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/project/contributing/images/model-register-formatter.png" /></a></p>
<h3 id="relationship-evaluation-formatter">
	Relationship Evaluation Formatter
</h3>
<p>The <strong>Relationship Evaluation Formatter</strong> is responsible for rendering notifications related to the evaluation of relationships between components in a design. It provides a detailed breakdown of changes in components and relationships, such as additions, updates, and removals, during the evaluation process.</p>
<p><strong>Path:</strong> <code>ui/components/NotificationCenter/formatters/relationship_evaluation.js</code></p>
<h4 id="key-components">
	Key Components
</h4>
<ol>
<li><strong>RelationshipEvaluationEventFormatter</strong>:<br>
The main formatter component that renders the event description and invokes the <code>RelationshipEvaluationTraceFormatter</code> to display detailed traces.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Props:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><code>event</code> (object): Contains:
<ul>
<li><strong>description</strong>: A description of the evaluation process.</li>
<li><strong>metadata.trace</strong>: Contains categorized changes in components and relationships:
<ul>
<li><code>componentsAdded</code> (Array)</li>
<li><code>componentsUpdated</code> (Array)</li>
<li><code>componentsRemoved</code> (Array)</li>
<li><code>relationshipsAdded</code> (Array)</li>
<li><code>relationshipsUpdated</code> (Array)</li>
<li><code>relationshipsRemoved</code> (Array)</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="/project/contributing/images/relationship-evaluation-formatter.png"><img alt="Relationship Evaluation Formatter" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/project/contributing/images/relationship-evaluation-formatter.png" /></a></p>
<h4 id="when-to-use">
	When to Use
</h4>
<p>The <strong>Relationship Evaluation Formatter</strong> is specifically designed to handle notifications related to changes in components and their relationships during an evaluation process. Use this formatter in the following scenarios:</p>
<ol>
<li>When a notification involves the evaluation of relationships between components in a design.</li>
<li>When you need to display categorized changes in components and relationships.</li>
<li>When the event metadata includes a <code>trace</code> object containing detailed information about the changes in components and relationships.</li>
</ol>
<h4 id="user-experience-relationship-evaluation-notification">
	User Experience: Relationship Evaluation Notification
</h4>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Evaluation Summary</strong>:<br>
The notification starts with a summary of the evaluation process.<br>
Example:<br>
<code>&quot;Relationship evaluation completed for design 'Deploy Meshery using Meshery-X' at version '0.0.11'&quot;</code><br>
This gives the user context about which design and version were evaluated.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Detailed Changes</strong>:<br>
The notification breaks down the changes into categories:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Components</strong>:
<ul>
<li><strong>Added</strong>: New components introduced in the design.</li>
<li><strong>Updated</strong>: Existing components that were modified.</li>
<li><strong>Removed</strong>: Components that were deleted from the design.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Relationships</strong>:
<ul>
<li><strong>Added</strong>: New relationships established between components.</li>
<li><strong>Updated</strong>: Existing relationships that were modified.</li>
<li><strong>Removed</strong>: Relationships that were deleted.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Component Details</strong>:<br>
For each component, the notification displays:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Kind</strong>: The type of the component (e.g., <code>Deployment</code>, <code>Service</code>).</li>
<li><strong>Name</strong>: The name of the component.</li>
<li><strong>Model and Version</strong>: The model and version associated with the component.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Relationship Details</strong>:<br>
For each relationship, the notification displays:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Type</strong>: The type of relationship.</li>
<li><strong>Source and Target</strong>: The components involved in the relationship (e.g., <code>Pod</code> to <code>Pod</code>).</li>
<li><strong>Model and Version</strong>: The model and version associated with the relationship.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="dry-run-formatter">
	Dry Run Formatter
</h3>
<p>The <strong>Dry Run Formatter</strong> is responsible for rendering notifications related to the dry run validation of a design. A dry run simulates the deployment or undeployment of a design to identify potential errors without actually applying the changes.</p>
<p><strong>Path:</strong> <code>ui/components/DesignLifeCycle/DryRun.js</code></p>
<h4 id="key-components-1">
	Key Components
</h4>
<ol>
<li><strong>FormatDryRunResponse</strong>:<br>
The main formatter component that renders the dry run validation results. It displays the total number of errors.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Props:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>dryRunErrors</strong> (array): An array of errors detected during the dry run. Each error includes:
<ul>
<li><code>type</code>: The type of error (e.g., <code>RequestError</code>, <code>ComponentError</code>).</li>
<li><code>fieldPath</code>: The specific field in the design where the error occurred.</li>
<li><code>message</code>: A detailed error message.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>configurableComponentsCount</strong> (number): The number of configurable components in the design.</li>
<li><strong>annotationComponentsCount</strong> (number): The number of annotation components in the design.</li>
<li><strong>validationMachine</strong> (object): The state machine handling the dry run validation process.</li>
<li><strong>currentComponentName</strong> (string): The name of the component currently being validated.</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="/project/contributing/images/dry-run-formatter.png"><img alt="Dry Run Formatter" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/project/contributing/images/dry-run-formatter.png" /></a></p>
<h4 id="when-to-use-1">
	When to Use
</h4>
<p>The <strong>Dry Run Formatter</strong> is used in the following scenarios:</p>
<ol>
<li>When a notification involves the validation of a design through a dry run process.</li>
<li>When you need to display errors detected during the dry run.</li>
<li>When the event metadata includes details about configurable and annotation components.</li>
</ol>
<h2 id="deployment-summary-formatter">
	Deployment Summary Formatter
</h2>
<p>The <strong>Deployment Summary Formatter</strong> is responsible for rendering notifications related to the deployment or undeployment of components in a design.</p>
<p><strong>Path:</strong> <code>ui/components/DesignLifeCycle/DeploymentSummary.js</code></p>
<h4 id="key-components-2">
	Key Components
</h4>
<ol>
<li><strong>DeploymentSummaryFormatter</strong>:<br>
This component is used to display:
<ul>
<li><strong>Event Description</strong>: A brief description of the deployment event.</li>
<li><strong>Errors</strong>: Any errors encountered during the deployment process.</li>
<li><strong>Component Details</strong>: A list of components with their deployment status and metadata.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Props:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>event</strong> (object): Contains:
<ul>
<li><strong>description</strong>: A brief description of the deployment event.</li>
<li><strong>action</strong>: The type of action performed (e.g., <code>deploy</code>, <code>undeploy</code>).</li>
<li><strong>severity</strong>: The severity level of the event.</li>
<li><strong>metadata</strong>:
<ul>
<li><strong>summary</strong>: A detailed summary of the deployment process, including component details.</li>
<li><strong>error</strong>: Any errors encountered during the deployment process.</li>
<li><strong>design_name</strong>: The name of the design being deployed.</li>
<li><strong>design_id</strong>: The ID of the design being deployed.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="when-to-use-2">
	When to Use
</h4>
<p>The <strong>Deployment Summary Formatter</strong> should be used in the following scenarios:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Deployment or Undeployment Events</strong>:<br>
When the <code>event.action</code> is either <code>deploy</code> or <code>undeploy</code> and the <code>event.metadata</code> includes <code>design_name</code>.</li>
<li>When a notification involves the deployment or undeployment of a design.</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="propertyformatters-and-propertylinkformatters">
	PropertyFormatters and PropertyLinkFormatters
</h3>
<p><strong>Purpose:</strong><br>
When an event does not match an event in <code>EventTypeFormatters</code>, <strong>PropertyFormatters</strong> and <strong>PropertyLinkFormatters</strong> are used to format and render specific metadata fields in a structured and visually appealing way.</p>
<h4 id="examples-of-property-formatters">
	Examples of Property Formatters
</h4>
<ol>
<li><strong>trace</strong>: Converts large trace data into a downloadable file link.</li>
<li><strong>ShortDescription</strong>: Displays a short description of the event.</li>
<li><strong>Error</strong>: Uses the <code>ErrorMetadataFormatter</code> to display structured error details.</li>
</ol>
<h4 id="when-to-use-3">
	When to Use
</h4>
<p>Use <strong>PropertyFormatters</strong> and <strong>PropertyLinkFormatters</strong> in the following scenarios:</p>
<ol>
<li>When an event does not have a specific <code>EventTypeFormatter</code> defined.</li>
<li>When you need to render individual metadata fields in a structured and visually appealing way.</li>
<li>When metadata includes fields like trace data, short descriptions, or error details that require specialized formatting.</li>
</ol>
<hr>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>
