        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Schema-Driven UI Development in Meshery</h1>
          
          <p>Meshery aims to decouple the UI logic from hardcoded structures and become fully schema-driven. This allows the UI to dynamically adapt based on changes in the underlying schema without requiring constant manual updates. This document explains how to integrate schema definitions from the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas"><code>meshery/schemas</code></a> repository into the Meshery UI using a code-generation approach.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="overview">
	Overview
</h2>
<p>Meshery’s schemas define the <strong>structure of data (constructs)</strong> using JSON Schema and <strong>their behavior (API operations)</strong> using OpenAPI specifications. From these definitions, Meshery auto-generates:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Go structs</strong> for backend validation and API handling</li>
<li><strong>TypeScript types and objects</strong> for frontend development</li>
<li><strong>Templates</strong> in JSON and YAML formats</li>
</ul>
<p>This approach ensures the <strong>schemas remain the single source of truth</strong>.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="repository-structure">
	Repository Structure
</h2>
<p>All schema definitions live in the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas"><code>meshery/schemas</code></a> repository.</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>schemas/
  constructs/
    v1beta1/
      design/
        design.json              # JSON schema for the noun
        design_template.json     # JSON template (generated)
        design_template.yaml     # YAML template (generated)
        openapi.yml               # OpenAPI spec defining operations
        subschemas/               # Optional reusable schema parts
</code></pre><ul>
<li><strong><code>&lt;construct&gt;.json</code></strong>: Defines structure (noun) — e.g., what a <code>Design</code> looks like.</li>
<li><strong><code>openapi.yml</code></strong>: Describes operations (verbs) — e.g., how to <code>GET</code>, <code>POST</code>, or <code>DELETE</code> a design.</li>
<li><strong><code>Templates</code></strong>: Valid, default-filled, resolved objects from the schema.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="schema-driven-ui-development-workflow">
	Schema-Driven UI Development Workflow
</h2>
<p>Meshery follows a <strong>schema-first</strong> approach where the UI is driven by JSON schemas and OpenAPI specifications. Here&rsquo;s how you can contribute to and use these schemas in the Meshery UI.</p>
<hr>
<h3 id="step-1-define-or-update-the-schema">
	Step 1: Define or Update the Schema
</h3>
<p>If you&rsquo;re introducing or modifying a UI feature that requires a new schema:</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p>Navigate to the appropriate schema directory:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>schemas/constructs/&lt;version&gt;/&lt;construct&gt;/
</code></pre></li>
<li>
<p>Define the schema structure in <strong><code>&lt;construct&gt;.json</code></strong> using <strong>JSON Schema v7</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Define API operations related to this schema in <strong><code>openapi.yml</code></strong> using <strong>OpenAPI v3</strong>. This helps generate consistent API types and models that align with your UI needs.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<hr>
<h3 id="step-2-generate-typescript-types-and-schema-objects">
	Step 2: Generate TypeScript Types and Schema Objects
</h3>
<p>Use the following command to generate TypeScript types and JavaScript schema objects:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">make generate-types
</span></span></code></pre></div><p>This will:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Generate <code>.ts</code> and <code>.d.ts</code> files under:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>typescript/constructs/&lt;version&gt;/&lt;construct&gt;/
</code></pre></li>
<li>
<p>Create:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Typed interfaces</strong> for schema validation and component props</li>
<li><strong>Schema objects</strong> usable for dynamic UI (e.g., forms, validations)</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<hr>
<h3 id="step-3-build-and-export-typesschema-objects">
	Step 3: Build and Export Types/Schema Objects
</h3>
<p>After generation:</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p>Open <a href="https://github.com/meshery/schemas/blob/master/typescript/index.ts"><code>typescript/index.ts</code></a></p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Export the newly generated types and schema objects from here.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Example:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-ts" data-lang="ts"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">export</span> <span class="o">*</span> <span class="kr">from</span> <span class="s2">&#34;./constructs/v1beta1/design&#34;</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p>Build the TypeScript package to make the changes usable:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">npm run build
</span></span></code></pre></div></li>
</ol>
<hr>
<h3 id="step-4-use-schema-package-in-ui">
	Step 4: Use Schema Package in UI
</h3>
<p>To consume the schema in the UI:</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p>Install the schema package locally:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">npm install &lt;path-to-schemas-repo&gt;
</span></span></code></pre></div><p>Examples:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Relative path:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">npm install ../../schemas
</span></span></code></pre></div></li>
<li>
<p>Absolute path:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">npm install /home/user/code/schemas
</span></span></code></pre></div></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p>This will update your <code>package.json</code> to something like:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-json" data-lang="json"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="s2">&#34;@meshery/schema&#34;</span><span class="err">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;file:../../schemas&#34;</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div></li>
<li>
<p>Now you can import types and schema objects in your UI components:</p>
</li>
</ol>
<h4 id="example-importing-and-using-a-type">
	Example: Importing and Using a Type
</h4>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-ts" data-lang="ts"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">DesignTypes</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="kr">from</span> <span class="s2">&#34;@meshery/schema&#34;</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="c1">// Type safety!
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">const</span> <span class="nx">renderDesignCard</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">design</span>: <span class="kt">Design</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nt">div</span><span class="p">&gt;{</span><span class="nx">design</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">name</span><span class="p">}&lt;/</span><span class="nt">div</span><span class="p">&gt;;</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><h4 id="example-accessing-runtime-schema">
	Example: Accessing Runtime Schema
</h4>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-ts" data-lang="ts"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">DesignSchema</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="kr">from</span> <span class="s2">&#34;@meshery/schema&#34;</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">const</span> <span class="nx">validateDesign</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">data</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="kr">const</span> <span class="nx">isValid</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nx">ajv</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">validate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">DesignSchema</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">data</span><span class="p">);</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="nx">isValid</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">};</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Can't find a Schema Import in the UI?</div>
<p>If you're trying to import a schema object or type in the UI but it's missing, it's likely because it hasn't been exported yet from the schemas package.</p>
<p>To keep the package lightweight, only actively used types and objects are exported by default. If you need access to a new schema, simply export it in the <a href='https://github.com/meshery/schemas' target='_blank'>Meshery Schemas repository</a> and regenerate the package.</p>
</div>
<hr>
<h2 id="integration-points-in-ui">
	Integration Points in UI
</h2>
<h3 id="a-rjsf-json-schemas">
	A. RJSF JSON Schemas
</h3>
<p>Meshery uses <a href="https://github.com/rjsf-team/react-jsonschema-form">react-jsonschema-form</a> to render forms dynamically based on JSON schemas. All of Meshery’s RJSF schemas are defined in the <code>@sistent/sistent</code> package, which extends schemas from the <code>@meshery/schema</code> package.</p>
<p>This approach enables us to generate forms that automatically adapt to the schema structure without hardcoding field properties like type, enum, description, and others.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-ts" data-lang="ts"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">DesignSchema</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="kr">from</span> <span class="s2">&#34;@meshery/schema&#34;</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">const</span> <span class="nx">designSchema</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">...</span><span class="nx">DesignSchema</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nx">properties</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="p">...</span><span class="nx">DesignSchema</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">properties</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">name</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="p">...</span><span class="nx">DesignSchema</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">properties</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">name</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="nx">description</span>: <span class="kt">DesignSchema.properties.description</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="nx">ui</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">        <span class="nx">label</span>: <span class="kt">DesignSchema.properties.name.title</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">        <span class="nx">placeholder</span>: <span class="kt">DesignSchema.properties.name.description</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="p">},</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="p">},</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="c1">// Other properties with UI-specific enhancements
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">},</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">};</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><hr>
<h3 id="b-general-form-ui">
	B. General Form UI
</h3>
<p>OpenAPI schemas (especially request bodies for POST/PUT operations) serve as the foundation for building form logic. These definitions include:</p>
<ul>
<li>Field validations (e.g. <code>required</code>, <code>format</code>, <code>maxLength</code>)</li>
<li>Field types and formats (e.g. <code>string</code>, <code>integer</code>, <code>date-time</code>)</li>
<li>Descriptions and examples</li>
<li>Enum constraints and conditional logic</li>
<li>Custom extensions like <code>x-rjsf-*</code> for layout</li>
</ul>
<p>This ensures alignment between frontend form behavior and backend expectations.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-ts" data-lang="ts"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">DesignTypes</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="kr">from</span> <span class="s2">&#34;@meshery/schema&#34;</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">const</span> <span class="nx">DesignForm</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">({</span> <span class="nx">design</span> <span class="p">}</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">design</span>: <span class="kt">DesignTypes</span> <span class="p">})</span> <span class="o">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">(</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nt">form</span><span class="p">&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nt">input</span> <span class="na">type</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s">&#34;text&#34;</span> <span class="na">value</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">design</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">name</span><span class="p">}</span> <span class="p">/&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="p">{</span><span class="cm">/* More fields derived from the schema */</span><span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">&lt;/</span><span class="nt">form</span><span class="p">&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">);</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><hr>
<h3 id="c-ui-specific-descriptions-and-enhancements">
	C. UI-Specific Descriptions and Enhancements
</h3>
<p>Any UI-specific metadata—such as <code>name</code>, <code>type</code>, <code>hints</code>, <code>descriptions</code>, <code>defaults</code>, etc.—is defined directly within the relevant schema object. Elements like tooltips, descriptions, and other metadata are frequently needed across the UI, so having a single source of truth in the schema object ensures consistency and reduces duplication.</p>
<p>For example, if we have a <code>Design</code> schema, the UI retrieves details like the design’s name, description, and other properties directly from the schema object.</p>
<hr>
<h3 id="d-type-safety-for-component-props">
	D. Type Safety for Component Props
</h3>
<p>Generated TypeScript types from the schema ensure UI components are type-safe and consistent with backend contracts.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-ts" data-lang="ts"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">DesignTypes</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="kr">from</span> <span class="s2">&#34;@meshery/schema&#34;</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">const</span> <span class="nx">DesignCard</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">({</span> <span class="nx">design</span> <span class="p">}</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">design</span>: <span class="kt">DesignTypes</span> <span class="p">})</span> <span class="o">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">(</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nt">div</span><span class="p">&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nt">h2</span><span class="p">&gt;{</span><span class="nx">design</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">name</span><span class="p">}&lt;/</span><span class="nt">h2</span><span class="p">&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nt">p</span><span class="p">&gt;{</span><span class="nx">design</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">description</span><span class="p">}&lt;/</span><span class="nt">p</span><span class="p">&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">&lt;/</span><span class="nt">div</span><span class="p">&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">);</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div>
        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

            <h1>Contributing to Meshery UI - Sistent</h1>
          
          <div class="prereqs"><p><strong style="font-size: 20px;">Prerequisite Reading</strong></p>
  <ol><li><a href="contributing-ui">Contributing to Meshery UI</a></li></ol>
</div>
<h2 id="contributing-to-meshery-ui---sistent">
	<a name="contributing-ui-sistent">Contributing to Meshery UI - Sistent</a>
</h2>
<p><code>Sistent</code> is the design system used by Meshery UI. Sistent is an open source design system that offers building blocks to create consistent, accessible, and user-friendly interfaces. It&rsquo;s aimed at developers who want to design applications aligned with the same brand and ensure a uniform user experience across different products.</p>
<p>Sistent leverages Material UI libraries and provides a custom theme on top of it for a consistent look and feel. It includes components, icons, and design tokens that developers can readily integrate into their applications. By using Sistent, developers can save time and effort while maintaining a high-quality user experience throughout Meshery.</p>
<p><strong>Example</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>This <code>Modal</code> is a Sistent Standard Modal used in validation of design.</li>
</ul>
<a href="/project/contributing/images/sistent-modal.png">
<img style= "width: 600px;" src="/project/contributing/images/sistent-modal.png" />
</a>
<h3 id="how-to-use-sistent-in-meshery-ui">
	How to use Sistent in Meshery UI
</h3>
<p><strong>Table of Contents</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-sistent/#usage">Usage</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-sistent/#how-to-use-tokenscolors-from-sistent-theme">How to use Sistent tokens/theme colors</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-sistent/#examples">Examples</a></li>
</ul>
<p>The Sistent design system includes a variety of base components such as <code>Button</code>, <code>Textfield</code>, <code>Checkbox</code>, and more, which can be found <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sistent/sistent/tree/master/src/base">here</a>
Additionally, it provides custom components like <code>Modal</code>, <code>TransferList</code>, and others, which are available <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sistent/sistent">here</a></p>
<h3 id="usage">
	Usage
</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Import any base or custom component from <code>@sistent/sistent</code></strong>. Here&rsquo;s how you can do it:</li>
</ul>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-javascript" data-lang="javascript"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">import</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">Button</span><span class="p">}</span> <span class="nx">from</span> <span class="sb">`@sistent/sistent`</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kd">function</span> <span class="nx">MyComponent</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="k">return</span> <span class="p">(</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">div</span><span class="o">&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">Button</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">        <span class="nx">variant</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">&#34;contained&#34;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">        <span class="nx">onClick</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">onClick</span><span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="o">&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="p">{</span><span class="cm">/* Text to display */</span><span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="err">/Button&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="err">/div&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">);</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">export</span> <span class="k">default</span> <span class="nx">MyComponent</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="how-to-use-tokenscolors-from-sistent-theme">
	How to use <code>Tokens/Colors</code> from Sistent theme
</h3>
<p>Let&rsquo;s start with a few of the common terms that we will come across frequently, as understanding what they mean will inform us of applicable use cases and proper procedures that should not be overlooked.</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Theme:</strong>
A theme provides a cohesive and consistent look and feel for a product, achieved through harmonious color palettes, legible fonts, and layout patterns. Sistent specifies both light and dark themes.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Value:</strong>
A value is a unique visual attribute assigned to a token via themes, such as hex codes or RGBA values, used to highlight specific colors. Avoid referencing exact values directly to ensure consistency; instead, use tokens to manage and implement reusable values.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Tokens:</strong>
Tokens serve as a shared language between design and development, detailing how to build user interfaces. Tokens represent context (background, text, component), role (success, warning, brand, inverse), and modifiers (secondary, tertiary, hover) derived from the <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sistent/sistent">color palette</a>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Role:</strong>
Roles specify the context for applying colors. Different roles can share the same value but will have different use cases due to the token structure. These values can vary depending on the current theme.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="how-to-use-these-tokenscolors-from-sistent-theme">
	How to use these tokens/colors from Sistent theme
</h4>
<ul>
<li>Import the <code>useTheme</code> hook from <code>@sistent/sistent</code> to access the current theme.</li>
<li>Utilize the <code>useTheme</code> hook to access theme properties and apply them to your components, such as setting the background style of the <code>Button</code>.</li>
</ul>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-javascript" data-lang="javascript"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">import</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">Button</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">useTheme</span><span class="p">}</span> <span class="nx">from</span> <span class="s2">&#34;@sistent/sistent&#34;</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kd">function</span> <span class="nx">MyComponent</span><span class="p">()</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="kr">const</span> <span class="nx">theme</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nx">useTheme</span><span class="p">();</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="p">(</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">div</span><span class="o">&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="nx">Button</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">        <span class="nx">variant</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s2">&#34;contained&#34;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">        <span class="nx">onClick</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">onClick</span><span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">        <span class="nx">style</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">          <span class="nx">background</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="nx">theme</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">palette</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">background</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="k">default</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">          <span class="nx">text</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="nx">theme</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">palette</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">text</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">secondary</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">        <span class="p">}}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="o">&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">        <span class="p">{</span><span class="cm">/* Text to display */</span><span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">        <span class="nx">Click</span> <span class="nx">Me</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="err">/Button&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="err">/div&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">);</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">export</span> <span class="k">default</span> <span class="nx">MyComponent</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">NOTE</div>
<p>The <a href='https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sistent/sistent'>tokens</a> and their roles are specific to their use. For example, use the background palette for background styles and the text palette for text styles.</p>
</div>

        </div>

        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Contributing to Meshery UI End-to-End Tests</h1>
          
          <p>To automate functional integration and end-to-end testing Meshery uses <a href="https://playwright.dev/">Playwright</a> as one of the tools to automate browser testing. End-to-end tests run with each pull request to ensure that the changes do not break the existing functionality.</p>
<h2 id="prerequisites">
	Prerequisites:
</h2>
<p>Before diving into Meshery&rsquo;s testing environment, certain prerequisites are necessary:</p>
<ul>
<li>A verified account in your chosen provider which integrate with Meshery.</li>
<li>A compatible browser such as Chromium, Chrome, or Firefox.</li>
<li>Installations of Golang, NodeJS, and Makefiles for Native OS build (Optional for docker based build).</li>
<li>Kubernetes clusters (Required for connection to Kubernetes test cases)</li>
<li>Already have <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/architecture/adapters">Meshery Adapters</a> up and running (Required for adapters test cases)</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="setting-up-environment-variable">
	Setting up environment variable
</h2>
<p>To run the tests successfully, three environment variables must be configured:<br>
• <code>REMOTE_PROVIDER_USER_EMAIL</code> (Required): The email associated with your account within your provider.<br>
• <code>REMOTE_PROVIDER_USER_PASSWORD</code> (Required): The password associated with your account within your provider.<br>
• <code>PROVIDER_TOKEN</code> (Optional): Your provider token, can be generated from an account registered within your provider</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Accessing Remote Providers</div>
<p>In the case you are using Meshery Cloud as a remote provider, you can <a href="https://cloud.meshery.io/security/tokens">generate a token from your user account</a> to use while writing and executing tests.</p>
</div>
<p>During the setup phase, Playwright utilizes these environment variables to log in and store credentials securely in the <code>playwright/.auth</code> directory. To protect sensitive data, the <code>.gitignore</code> file is configured to exclude the <code>.env</code> file and any JSON files within the <code>/playwright/.auth</code> directory from the GitHub repository.</p>
<p>There are several tools to help you to working with environment variables locally for each project such as <a href="https://github.com/direnv/direnv">direnv</a>, it can work across multiple shell such as Bash, Powershell, Oh my zsh, Fish, etc</p>
<h2 id="starting-up-meshery-ui-and-server">
	Starting up Meshery UI and Server
</h2>
<p>There are a few ways to set up the Meshery UI and server, but for end-to-end testing, we aim to get as close to a production environment as possible. We know developers might need to make some tweaks for UI and Server. Rebuilding the whole project can take time, and we don’t support hot reload because it’s more for development than for end-to-end testing.</p>
<div class="alert alert-warning" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Several Test may break</div>
<p>Some test cases required you to have kubernetes cluster and build meshery adapter as well, be aware of that. Which is out of scope for this documentation</p>
<ul><li><a href="/installation/kubernetes/minikube">Kubernetes Cluster</a>: Installation of kubernetes cluster with Minikube.</li>
<li><a href="/installation/multiple-adapters">Meshery Adapters</a>: Using Multiple Adapters</li></ul>
</div>
<h3 id="native-os-build-recommended">
	Native OS Build (Recommended)
</h3>
<p>This approach is very quick to build, but also dependent on your operating system, so you need to have all dependencies necessary to be able compile and running the server.</p>
<ul>
<li>Install &amp; Build the NextJS application for both the UI and UI Provider</li>
</ul>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make ui-build</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<ul>
<li>Compile the Golang into binary file for Meshery Server</li>
</ul>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make build-server</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<ul>
<li>Run the Meshery Server on localhost port 9081</li>
</ul>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make server-binary</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="meshery-cli">
	Meshery CLI
</h3>
<p>There is also Meshery CLI which can help you run the UI and Server, for more detail, you go to <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing/contributing-cli-guide#process">Meshery CLI documentation</a></p>
<h3 id="docker-based-build">
	Docker Based Build
</h3>
<p>Alternatively, a Docker-based setup can be utilized, simplifying the process, and ensuring consistency across different environments. It is closer to the production environment than the native solution but slower in terms of build time.</p>
<ul>
<li>Build the docker container locally:</li>
</ul>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make docker-testing-env-build</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<ul>
<li>Run the docker container on port 9081</li>
</ul>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make docker-testing-env</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="setup-playwright">
	Setup Playwright
</h2>
<p>For Playwrights, always try to use a native OS whenever possible. The Docker-based approach is intended only for unsupported OSes and is generally not recommended because it runs on top of Ubuntu images, which can be redundant if you already using Ubuntu or Windows.</p>
<h3 id="playwright-on-native-os-recommended">
	Playwright on Native OS (Recommended)
</h3>
<p>Setup playwright:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make ui-test-setup</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Run the all project and test cases:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make ui-test</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="playwright-server-on-docker-based-image">
	Playwright server on docker based image
</h3>
<p>The first step is to pull the docker image from <a href="https://mcr.microsoft.com/en-us/product/playwright/tags">Azure Container Registry</a> where the playwright stores their image using this command:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">docker pull mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:&lt;version&gt;-&lt;base-image&gt;</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<div class="alert alert-warning" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Playwright Versioning</div>
<p>Make sure the version you are using matches the version of <code>@playwright/test</code> in the <code>package.json</code> dev dependencies</p>
</div>
<p>Here is the example of pulling playwright v1.44.0 with Ubuntu 22.04 LTS</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">docker pull mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.44.0-jammy</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Starting up playwright docker server:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">docker run --rm --network host --init -it mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.44.0-jammy /bin/sh -c &#34;cd /home/pwuser &amp;&amp; npx -y playwright@1.44.0 run-server --port 8080&#34;</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<div class="alert alert-warning" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Unsafe Environment</div>
<p>Keep in mind this is just for development purposes inside your local system and don&rsquo;t try to expose your container network to the host system using &ndash;network host on production or CI</p>
</div>
<p>In the last step go to ui folder,


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">cd ui;</code>
	</div>
</pre>
</p>
<h2 id="run-the-test-cases-with-playwright-cli">
	Run the test cases with Playwright CLI
</h2>
<p>There are several options we can use to run the test cases, in CLI:</p>
<p>To run playwright UI mode using the browser, you can add <code>--ui</code> in the cli, for example:


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">npx playwright test --ui</code>
	</div>
</pre>
</p>
<p>If you are using playwright from docker, you can use <code>--ui-port=&lt;playwright-docker-server&gt;</code>, for example:


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">npx playwright test --ui-port=8080</code>
	</div>
</pre>
</p>
<p>To run playwright for specific project only, for example meshery-provider, you can run this command:


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">npx playwright test --ui --project=chromium-meshery-provider</code>
	</div>
</pre>
</p>
<p>To run specific test, you can add the test file location, for example:


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">npx playwright test --ui --project=chromium-meshery-provider tests/e2e/service-mesh-performance.spec.js</code>
	</div>
</pre>
</p>
<p>For more detail, you can read the <a href="https://playwright.dev/docs/test-cli">Playwright Cli docs</a></p>
<h2 id="testing-meshery--local-provider">
	Testing Meshery &amp; Local Provider
</h2>
<p>By default our test cases is running against both Meshery and Local Provider, we are utilizing playwright feature such as:</p>
<ul>
<li>StorageState: In meshery <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/ui/tests/e2e/auth.setup.js">setup auth</a>, we have 2 storage state, which store a session for Meshery and Local provider.</li>
<li>Project: After the setup completes, it will run the project-based test depending on which storage state for the Local Provider and one for the Meshery Provider</li>
<li>Test Parameterize:  In the Local provider we are limiting some features to test against. For the missing features, we leverage this playwright feature to check or even skip the test. If it is not possible to run then you need to specify the <code>provider</code> directly from the test, and make sure the test is wrapped using:</li>
</ul>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">import { expect, test } from &#39;./fixtures/project&#39;;

test(&#39;Random test&#39;, async ({ provider }) =&gt; {
  if (provider === &#34;Meshery&#34;) {
    // Run this for testing Meshery provider
  }

  if (provider === &#34;None&#34;) {
    // Run this for testing Local provider
  }
});</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="testing-policy">
	Testing Policy
</h2>
<p>After merging a pull request, ensuring test stability across CI/CD runs is crucial. A test may pass locally but fail in the CI/CD environment due to differences in execution conditions. While one approach is to mark all new tests as @unstable by default, a more effective strategy is to apply the @unstable tag only if a test exhibits intermittent failures or flaky behavior.</p>
<p>After merging into the master branch, monitor the GitHub workflow that executes the new test case and assess its stability. If the test fails, raise another PR to mark it as @unstable and communicate this to the team. For example:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">import { expect, test } from &#39;./fixtures/project&#39;;

test(&#39;Random test&#39;,  { tag: &#39;@unstable&#39; }, async ({ provider }) =&gt; {
  // Test cases here
  // ...
});</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="debugging-test-on-github-actions">
	Debugging Test on Github Actions
</h2>
<p>End-to-end test results are stored as artifacts on every PR in Github Actions. In case you need to debug a failed test:</p>
<ul>
<li>Visit the PR in question. Go to the bottom of PR directly above the comment.</li>
<li>Wait until all Github Actions completed, and scroll until you see <code>Meshery UI and Server / UI end-to-end tests</code></li>
<li>Click details and it will redirect you to the actions workflow</li>
<li>Go to summary tab, scroll down until you see artifact, and check the artifact <code>playwright-report</code></li>
<li>Download the artifact</li>
<li>Extract the file into a folder</li>
<li>Go to <a href="https://trace.playwright.dev/">Playwright Trace Page</a></li>
<li>From the test folder pick one folder which represents the test, you want to check</li>
<li>Upload the trace file</li>
</ul>
<p>Watch the training session on Playwright testing and trace debugging.</p>
<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/x-W60mvDYuo?si=coN7RpRjkI4a_ndk&amp;start=1524" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>
<h3 id="find-tests-here">
	Find Tests here
</h3>
<p>Refer to <a href="https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13Ir4gfaKoAX9r8qYjAFFl_U9ntke4X5ndREY1T7bnVs/edit?usp=sharing">Meshery Test Plan</a> for test scenarios.</p>
<p>To filter and view only UI-related tests using the Sheet Views feature:</p>
<ol>
<li>In the top menu bar, click Data → Change view</li>
<li>Choose the pre-defined view labeled &ldquo;UI&rdquo;</li>
</ol>
<p><img class="content-image" src="/project/contributing/images/meshery-test-plan-v0.8.0-ui.png" alt="Meshery Test Plan Screenshot"  /></p>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Contributing to Meshery UI - Dashboard Widgets</h1>
          
          <div class="prereqs"><p><strong style="font-size: 20px;">Prerequisite Reading</strong></p>
  <ol><li><a href="contributing-ui">Contributing to Meshery UI</a></li></ol>
</div>
<p>Meshery&rsquo;s dashboard is a composable and extensible interface made up of individual widgets. These widgets allow contributors to surface specific Meshery data or capabilities within a modular layout system.</p>
<p>This guide walks through the process of creating and integrating a custom widget into the <a href="https://playground.meshery.io/">Meshery dashboard</a>. You’ll learn about layout configuration, design best practices, and how to register new widgets.</p>
<h2 id="1-widget-architecture">
	1. Widget Architecture
</h2>
<p>Widgets are React components located <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/ui/components/DashboardComponent/widgets">here</a>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">/ui/components/DashboardComponent/widgets/
</span></span></code></pre></div><p>Each widget is rendered inside a card component (<code>&lt;PlainCard /&gt;</code>, <code>&lt;DesignCard /&gt;</code>, etc.), which is sourced from the <a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sistent/sistent">Sistent design system</a>.</p>
<p>Widgets can:</p>
<ul>
<li>Pull data from APIs (REST, GraphQL, RSS)</li>
<li>Display static links or interactive components</li>
<li>Include icons and thumbnails for user familiarity</li>
</ul>
<hr>
<h2 id="2-creating-a-new-widget">
	2. Creating a New Widget
</h2>
<p>Create a new file inside <code>widgets/</code>, e.g.:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-jsx" data-lang="jsx"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="err">/ui/components/DashboardComponent/widgets/LatestBlogs.js</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><p>Use design system components from <code>@sistent/sistent</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-jsx" data-lang="jsx"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">import</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">useTheme</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">PlainCard</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">BellIcon</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="nx">from</span> <span class="s2">&#34;@sistent/sistent&#34;</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">const</span> <span class="nx">LatestBlogs</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="nx">props</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="kr">const</span> <span class="nx">theme</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nx">useTheme</span><span class="p">();</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="kr">const</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">data</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="nx">blogs</span> <span class="p">}</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nx">useFetchBlogsQuery</span><span class="p">();</span> <span class="c1">// fetch data from rtk query
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="k">return</span> <span class="p">(</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nt">PlainCard</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="na">title</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="s">&#34;LATEST BLOGS&#34;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="na">icon</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{&lt;</span><span class="nt">BellIcon</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="na">...props.iconsProps</span><span class="p">}</span> <span class="p">/&gt;}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">      <span class="na">resources</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="p">{</span><span class="nx">resources</span><span class="p">}</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="p">/&gt;</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">);</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">};</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">export</span> <span class="k">default</span> <span class="nx">LatestBlogs</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><p>Use <code>useTheme()</code> for consistent color tokens across themes.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="3-adding-thumbnails">
	3. Adding Thumbnails
</h2>
<p>Thumbnails are image previews of widgets. Place them here:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">/ui/components/DashboardComponent/widgets/Thumbnails/
</span></span></code></pre></div><p>Recommended format: <code>.png</code> or <code>.svg</code></p>
<p>Example:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-js" data-lang="js"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">import</span> <span class="nx">LatestBlogsThumbnail</span> <span class="nx">from</span> <span class="s2">&#34;./Thumbnails/LatestBlogs.png&#34;</span><span class="p">;</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><p>To verify your thumbnail appears correctly, click on the &ldquo;Edit&rdquo; button on the Dashboard. A visual card with your thumbnail and widget title will be listed there, allowing users to add it to their layout.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="4-registering-the-widget">
	4. Registering the Widget
</h2>
<p>Register your widget inside <code>getWidgets.js</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-jsx" data-lang="jsx"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="kr">export</span> <span class="kr">const</span> <span class="nx">getWidgets</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">()</span> <span class="p">=&gt;</span> <span class="p">({</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nx">LATEST_BLOGS</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">title</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="s2">&#34;Latest Blogs&#34;</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">isEnabled</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="nx">alwaysShown</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">component</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nt">LatestBlogs</span> <span class="p">/&gt;,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">defaultSizing</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="p">{</span> <span class="nx">w</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nx">h</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="mi">2</span> <span class="p">},</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">    <span class="nx">thumbnail</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="nx">LatestBlogsThumbnail</span><span class="o">?</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nx">src</span><span class="p">,</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="p">},</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">});</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><ul>
<li><code>title</code>: Display name</li>
<li><code>component</code>: JSX element</li>
<li><code>isEnabled</code>: Visibility flag</li>
<li><code>defaultSizing</code>: Default dimensions</li>
<li><code>thumbnail</code>: Path to preview image</li>
</ul>
<hr>
<h2 id="5-adding-to-default-layout">
	5. Adding to Default Layout
</h2>
<p>To include your widget in the default dashboard layout:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">/ui/components/DashboardComponent/defaultLayout.js
</span></span></code></pre></div><p>Layouts are defined per <strong>screen size breakpoint</strong> (e.g., <code>sm</code>, <code>xs</code>, <code>xxs</code>) to ensure responsiveness. Each layout item is an object with grid-based properties defined by the <code>react-grid-layout</code> library.</p>
<pre><code>sm: tablets and desktops
xs: large phones
xxs: small phones
</code></pre>
<h3 id="example-layout-item">
	Example Layout Item:
</h3>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-js" data-lang="js"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">{</span>
</span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nx">h</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span>                  <span class="c1">// Height in grid units
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nx">i</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="s1">&#39;LATEST_BLOGS&#39;</span><span class="p">,</span>     <span class="c1">// Widget identifier (unique string)
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nx">moved</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span>          <span class="c1">// Internal flag (do not change manually)
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="kr">static</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">,</span>         <span class="c1">// If true, the widget cannot be dragged or resized
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nx">w</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span>                  <span class="c1">// Width in grid units
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nx">x</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span>                  <span class="c1">// Horizontal grid position (column index)
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">  <span class="nx">y</span><span class="o">:</span> <span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span>                  <span class="c1">// Vertical grid position (row index)
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="p">}</span>
</span></span></code></pre></div><h3 id="layout-field-descriptions">
	Layout Field Descriptions:
</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>i</strong>: A unique string ID for the widget. This should match the widget’s <code>id</code> used elsewhere in your code.</li>
<li><strong>x</strong>: The column (starting from 0) where the widget should be placed.</li>
<li><strong>y</strong>: The row (starting from 0) where the widget should be placed. Widgets with the same <code>y</code> value appear in the same row.</li>
<li><strong>w</strong>: The widget&rsquo;s width in terms of number of grid columns it should span.</li>
<li><strong>h</strong>: The widget&rsquo;s height in terms of number of grid rows it should span.</li>
<li><strong>static</strong>: When <code>true</code>, the widget is locked in place — it can&rsquo;t be moved or resized.</li>
<li><strong>moved</strong>: Used by the library to track user interactions. Leave as <code>false</code>.</li>
</ul>
<blockquote>
<p>Here layout is based on a 12-column CSS grid. Each widget’s position is defined in terms of this virtual grid, which helps in building a responsive and flexible dashboard layout.</p>
</blockquote>
<hr>
<p>Define the widget’s position (x, y) and size (w, h) in each breakpoint for responsive behavior. The code for it can be found <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/ui/components/DashboardComponent/defaultLayout.js">here</a>.</p>
<p>Note: Layouts for <strong>Remote Providers</strong> are dynamically generated based on user configuration and stored remotely. Local providers use a predefined layout (<code>LOCAL_PROVIDER_LAYOUT</code>). Widgets must be added to both if you want consistent behavior across environments.</p>
<p>Meshery stores user layout preferences either in local storage or via the provider&rsquo;s backend, depending on login state.</p>
<p>This is how your default widget would appear in the dashboard:</p>
<a href="/project/contributing/images/dashboard-widgets.png">
<img style= "width: 600px;" src="/project/contributing/images/dashboard-widgets.png" />
</a>
<hr>
<h2 id="6-best-practices">
	6. Best Practices
</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Naming</strong>: Use uppercase keys (e.g. <code>MY_DESIGNS</code>) for clarity</li>
<li><strong>Icons</strong>: Use consistent design system icons (e.g., <code>CatalogIcon</code>, <code>DesignIcon</code>)</li>
<li><strong>Themes</strong>: Use <code>useTheme()</code> to access tokens</li>
<li><strong>Responsiveness</strong>: Define layout for multiple viewports (<code>sm</code>, <code>xs</code>, <code>xxs</code>)</li>
<li><strong>Reusability</strong>: Break logic into reusable hooks when needed</li>
<li><strong>Thumbnails</strong>: Always include a visual thumbnail</li>
<li><strong>Permissions</strong>: If your widget accesses protected resources, ensure user has correct provider login state or roles.</li>
</ul>
<hr>
<h2 id="7-other-examples">
	7. Other Examples
</h2>
<table>
  <thead>
      <tr>
          <th>Widget</th>
          <th>File</th>
          <th>Data Source</th>
          <th>UI Component</th>
      </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
      <tr>
          <td>Latest Blogs</td>
          <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/ui/components/DashboardComponent/widgets/LatestBlogs.js">LatestBlogs.js</a></td>
          <td>RSS Feed</td>
          <td>PlainCard</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td>Help Center</td>
          <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/ui/components/DashboardComponent/widgets/HelpCenterWidget.js">HelpCenterWidget.js</a></td>
          <td>Static Links</td>
          <td>PlainCard</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td>My Designs</td>
          <td><a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/ui/components/DashboardComponent/widgets/MyDesignsWidget.js">MyDesignsWidget.js</a></td>
          <td>REST Api</td>
          <td>DesignCard</td>
      </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<p>Note: <code>MyDesignsWidget</code> demonstrates integration with RTK Query hooks like <code>useGetLoggedInUserQuery()</code> and <code>useGetUserDesignsQuery()</code>.</p>
<p>Have a look at existing Widgets <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/ui/components/DashboardComponent/widgets">here</a>.</p>
<hr>
<h2 id="8-publishing">
	8. Publishing
</h2>
<p>Once your widget is working:</p>
<ul>
<li>Ensure it appears in the widget selector UI</li>
<li>Validate layout and responsiveness</li>
<li>Submit a PR with the new component, layout entry, and thumbnail. <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/pull/13629">Here</a> is a PR that adds Latest Blogs widget to Meshery Dashboard.</li>
<li>Add your widget in the <a href="https://meshery.io/extensions">Meshery Extensions Catalog</a> if appropriate</li>
</ul>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>
