            <h1>Contributing to Meshery UI</h1>
          
          <h2 id="ui-contribution-flow">
	<a name="contributing-ui">UI Contribution Flow</a>
</h2>
<p>Meshery UI is built on React and Next.js. In nearly all cases, while contributing to Meshery UI, you will need to build and run Meshery Server as well. Meshery Server is written in <code>Go</code> (Golang) and leverages Go Modules. To make building of each component easier a <code>Makefile</code> is included in the main repository folder. Use <code>make</code> to build any and all components.</p>
<h2 id="architecture">
	Architecture
</h2>
<p>The following is a list of top-level frameworks, libraries, design system used in Meshery UI.</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://nextjs.org/">NextJS</a> - Server and router</li>
<li><a href="https://reactjs.org/">ReactJS</a> - User Interface library</li>
<li><a href="https://material-ui.com/">Material UI</a> - Design System</li>
<li><a href="https://naver.github.io/billboard.js/">BillboardJS</a> - Charting library, used for exposing Grafana and Prometheus-collected metrics</li>
<li><a href="https://js.cytoscape.org/">CytoscapeJS</a> - a visualization tool for canvas-based, visual topology (networks)</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="build-system">
	Build System
</h3>
<p>Meshery UI and Provider UI use <a href="https://nextjs.org/">Next.js</a> with <a href="https://swc.rs/">SWC</a> (Speedy Web Compiler) for fast builds and optimal performance.</p>
<h2 id="schema-driven-ui-development">
	Schema-Driven UI Development
</h2>
<p>Meshery UI uses a schema-driven approach where components and forms are generated from JSON schemas. This enables dynamic UI adaptation, consistent validation, and type-safety across the application.</p>
<p><strong>⚠️ Required Reading:</strong> Before contributing, you must read the <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-schemas/">Schema-Driven UI Development Guide</a> to understand how Meshery&rsquo;s UI components are generated and maintained using schemas.</p>
<h2 id="meshery-server-apis">
	Meshery Server APIs
</h2>
<p>The <a href="/v0.9/extensibility/api/">API overview</a> in the Extensibility guide offers high-level insight, while each API reference (below) offers details pertaining to each API endpoints&rsquo; behavior and use.</p>
<h3 id="rest-api">
	REST API
</h3>
<p>Meshery provides a REST API available through the default port of <code>9081/tcp</code> at <code>&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;/api/</code>. See the <a href="/v0.9/reference/rest-apis/">REST API Reference</a> for a complete list of endpoints available with short description of their purpose and example code.</p>
<h3 id="graphql-api">
	GraphQL API
</h3>
<p>Meshery provides a GraphQl API available through the default port of <code>9081/tcp</code> at <code>&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;/api/graphql/query</code>. See the <a href="/v0.9/reference/graphql-apis/">GraphQL API Reference</a> <a href="https://relay.dev">Relay</a> is the client used.</p>
<h2 id="design">
	Design
</h2>
<p>Meshery UI is a significant component of the value proposition Meshery offers to individuals and organizations seeking to adopt and operate a cloud native infrastructure.</p>
<h3 id="user-flows--wireframing--mockups">
	User Flows / Wireframing / Mockups
</h3>
<p>Figma is used as the user flow and UI mockup design tool. The <a href="https://www.figma.com/file/SMP3zxOjZztdOLtgN4dS2W/Meshery-UI">Meshery UI design file</a> can be viewed by using this <a href="https://www.figma.com/team_invite/redeem/GvB8SudhEOoq3JOvoLaoMs">open invitation</a> for view access. Fill-in a <a href="https://meshery.io/newcomers">community member form</a> to gain access to additional community resources.</p>
<h3 id="design-goals">
	Design Goals
</h3>
<p>The designs in this specification should result in enabling:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>User experience should be intuitive</strong> - Meshery&rsquo;s UX, which includes Meshery UI as a component of the overall UX, needs to be simple, but powerful. This is achieved through intuitive layouts and predefined filters that accommodate common tasks. This is achieved through sensible defaults, consistency of user interaction paradigms and features that delight the user.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Extensible</strong> - Meshery UI should be a first-class component of Meshery, but also facilitate third-party integrations.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Real-time</strong> - Meshery UI should be event-driven where possible.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="setup">
	Setup
</h2>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Windows User?</div>
<p>See <a href='/project/contributing/meshery-windows'>Setting up Meshery Development Environment on Windows</a>.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="required-node-version">
	Required Node Version
</h3>
<p>Node 20 LTS</p>
<h3 id="linting-ui">
	Linting-UI
</h3>
<p>When contributing to Meshery UI, it is advisable to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Use prettier plugin for Visual Studio Code.</li>
<li>Disable plugins other than <code>prettier</code> and <code>eslint</code> for formatting and linting, if any.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="install-ui-dependencies">
	Install UI dependencies
</h3>
<p>To install/update the UI dependencies:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make ui-setup</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="build-and-export-ui">
	Build and export UI
</h3>
<p>To build and export the UI code:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make ui-build</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Using this command, changes that you make are not rebuilt automatically. You will have to run this command again to rebuild the UI and see them.</p>
<p>Now that the UI code is built, Meshery UI will be available at <code>http://localhost:9081</code> when Meshery Server is running (Read below).</p>
<p>To build and export the UI code <em>and</em> build and run Meshery Server:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make ui-server</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="run-meshery-server">
	Run Meshery Server
</h2>
<p>To start running Meshery Server locally:</p>
<p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make server</code>
	</div>
</pre>

Now, Meshery will run on the default port <code>http://localhost:9081</code>.</p>
<p><strong>Please note</strong>: If you see &ldquo;Meshery Development Incompatible&rdquo; while trying to sign into Meshery Server, then follow these steps:</p>
<a href="/project/contributing/images/meshery-development-incompatible-error.png">
  <img style= "width: 600px;" src="/project/contributing/images/meshery-development-incompatible-error.png" />
</a>
<p>Potential Solution:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Go to your meshery folder in your local-system where you’ve cloned it.
Execute:</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>git remote add upstream https://github.com/meshery/meshery</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>git fetch upstream</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Restart the meshery server</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Additionally, before restarting the server, if you like to pull the latest changes, you can do: <code>git pull upstream master</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="ui-development-server">
	UI Development Server
</h3>
<p>If you want to work on the UI, it will be a good idea to use the included UI development server. You can run the UI development server by running the following command:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">make ui</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Refer to <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-server/">Contributing to Meshery Server</a>, if needed.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Make sure to have Meshery Server configured, up and running on the default port <code>http://localhost:9081</code> and choose a provider to login with (visit <code>http://localhost:9081</code>) before proceeding to access and work on the UI server at <code>http://localhost:3000</code>.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>Any UI changes made now will <em>automatically</em> be rebuilt and served in your browser.</p>
<h3 id="running-end-to-end-integration-tests">
	Running end-to-end integration tests
</h3>
<p>Refer to <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-tests/">Meshery UI Testing</a> for details of how to contribute and benefit from Meshery UI testing.</p>
<h3 id="static-files-icons-and-images">
	Static Files, Icons and Images
</h3>
<p>The Meshery UI public folder contains static files. Its folder structure looks like this:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>meshery
└── ui
    └── public
        └── static
            ├── favicon.png
            ├── fonts
            ├── img
            └── style
</code></pre><p>Images and icons used in Meshery UI need to be sourced from the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/ui/public/static/img">public directory of images</a>. The files written inside this directory should only end with the extensions like <code>.svg</code>, <code>.png</code>, <code>.jpg</code> or <code>.jpeg</code>. Always use vector-based graphics (<code>.svg</code>), unless your have extenuating circumstances.</p>
<h5 id="conventions-for-svg-files">
	Conventions for SVG files
</h5>
<ol>
<li>SVGs should be optimized and compressed.
<ol>
<li>Use an online, SVG optimizer, like <a href="https://www.svgviewer.dev">https://www.svgviewer.dev</a>, to compress the file(s) to smaller size.</li>
</ol>
</li>
<li>All SVGs should have <code>height</code> and <code>width</code> properties set to 20px x 20px by default. Ensure that height and width attributes are always set in original SVG.</li>
<li>All SVGs should have <code>height</code> and <code>width</code> included as a style prop in their React component.</li>
<li>Always include this XML header in each SVG image:</li>
</ol>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">&lt;?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?&gt;&lt;!DOCTYPE svg&gt;</div></div>
</pre>
<ol start="5">
<li>Svg can only fall under two categories, and this categories should be the name of folder \
<ol>
<li>white: containing white or mono-colored version of that SVG</li>
<li>color: containing colored version of that SVG.
e.g.: the Meshery logo icon folder structure looks like this:</li>
</ol>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>└── img
    └── meshery
        ├── white
        |   └── meshery-white.svg
        └── color
            └── meshery-color.svg
</code></pre></li>
<li>Avoid any kind of duplicity in the versions of icons used.</li>
</ol>
<p>For accessing the svg file as data-url, the utf8 encoding should be used in place of base64.Use <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/encodeURIComponent">encodeURIComponent</a> on SVG data URIs. \</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">let svg = &#39;data:image/svg+xml;utf8,&#39; + encodeURIComponent(svgFile);</code>
	</div>
</pre>


        </div>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

<h1 id="contributing">
	Contributing
</h1>
<p>Please do! Thanks for your help! 🎈 Meshery is community-built and welcomes collaboration. Contributors are expected to adhere to the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md">CNCF&rsquo;s Code of Conduct</a>.</p>
<h2 id="general-contribution-flow">
	General Contribution Flow
</h2>
<p>Meshery and it&rsquo;s various architectural components are written in different languages, including Golang, Javascript (React.js and Next.js) To make building, testing, and the experience of contributing consistent across all Meshery components, a <code>Makefile</code> is included in the every repository. These <code>make</code> targets are what you will use to build, run, test, and document.</p>
<p>To contribute to Meshery, please follow this basic fork-and-pull request <a href="%7B%7Bsite.baseurl%7D%7D/project/contributing/contributing-gitflow">gitflow</a>.</p>
<details>
<summary>Adding your sign-off on commits (Developer Certificate of Origin)</summary>
<ul>
<li>
To contribute to this project, you must agree to the Developer Certificate of
Origin (DCO) for each commit you make. The DCO is a simple statement that you,
as a contributor, have the legal right to make the contribution.
</li>
<li>
See the <a href="https://developercertificate.org"> DCO </a> file for the full text of what you must agree to
and how it works <a href="https://github.com/probot/dco#how-it-works">here</a>.
To signify that you agree to the DCO for contributions, you simply add a line to each of your
git commit messages:
<pre><code>
Signed-off-by: Jane Smith <jane.smith@example.com>
</code></pre></li>
<li>
In most cases, you can add this signoff to your commit automatically with the
<code>-s</code> or <code>--signoff</code> flag to <code>git commit</code>. You must use your real name and a reachable email
address (sorry, no pseudonyms or anonymous contributions). An example of signing off on a commit:
<pre><code>$ git commit -s -m “my commit message w/signoff”</code></pre>
</li>
<li>
To ensure all your commits are signed, you may choose to add this alias to your global <code>.gitconfig</code>:
<p>~/.gitconfig</p>
<pre><code>
[alias]
  amend = commit -s --amend
  cm = commit -s -m
  commit = commit -s
</code></pre>
<p>Or you may configure your IDE, for example, VSCode to automatically sign-off commits for you:<a href="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7570704/64490167-98906400-d25a-11e9-8b8a-5f465b854d49.png" ><img src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7570704/64490167-98906400-d25a-11e9-8b8a-5f465b854d49.png" width="50%"/></a></p>
</li>
</ul>
</details>
<h2 id="not-sure-where-to-start">
	Not sure where to start?
</h2>
<details>
<summary>Follow these steps and you'll be right at home.</summary>
<ol>
  <li>See the <a href="https://meshery.io/community">Newcomers Guide</a> for how, where, and why to contribute.</li>
  <li>Sign up for a <a href="https://meshery.io/community#meshmates"><em>MeshMate</em></a> to find the perfect Mentor to help you explore the projects and find your place in the community.</li>
  <li><strong>Identify</strong> your area of interest: Use the time with your MeshMate to familiarize yourself with the architecture and technologies used in the projects. Inform your MeshMate of your current skills and what skills you aim to develop.</li>
  <li><strong><a href="https://play.meshery.io">Play with Meshery</a></strong>: Put on your user hat and walk-through all of Meshery’s features and functions as a user.</li>
  <li><strong>Build Meshery Server and UI</strong>: Confirm that you have a usable development environment. See <a href="#contributing-guides">Guides</a> below.</li>
  <li><strong>Discuss</strong> with the community by engaging in the <a href="https://discuss.meshery.io">discussion forum</a>.</li>
  <li><strong>Contribute</strong> by grabbing any open issue with the <a href="https://github.com/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+archived%3Afalse+org%3Ameshery+org%3Ameshery-extensions+org%3Aservice-mesh-performance+org%3Aservice-mesh-patterns+label%3A%22help+wanted%22+">help-wanted label</a> and jump in. If needed, create a <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/issues/new/choose">new issue</a>. All <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/pulls">pull requests</a> should reference an open issue. Include keywords in your pull request descriptions, as well as commit messages, to <a href="https://help.github.com/en/github/managing-your-work-on-github/closing-issues-using-keywords">automatically close issues in GitHub</a>.</li>
  <li><strong>Fill in</strong> a <a href="https://meshery.io/newcomers">community member form</a> to gain access to community resources.</li>
</ol>
</details>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" standalone="yes"?>

    <item>
      <title>Build &amp; Release (CI)</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/build-and-release/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/build-and-release/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery’s build and release system incorporates many tools, organized into different workflows each triggered by different events. Meshery’s build and release system does not run on a schedule, but is event-driven. GitHub Actions are used to define Meshery’s CI workflows. New builds of Meshery and its various components are automatically generated upon push, release, and other similar events, typically in relation to their respective master branches.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;alert alert-info&#34; role=&#34;alert&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;h4 alert-heading&#34; role=&#34;heading&#34;&gt;Meshery Test Documents&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The Meshery Test Strategy (&lt;a href=&#39;https://docs.google.com/document/d/11nAxYtz2SUusCYZ0JeNRrOLIxkgmmbUVWz63MBZV2oE/edit&#39;&gt;1&lt;/a&gt;,&lt;a href=&#39;https://docs.google.com/document/d/14vbwnKafqxrr-cJOmLWEvvj75MFrxFKiUdfPwZRhg64/edit&#39;&gt;2&lt;/a&gt;) is a comprehensive document that outlines the approach to testing, types of tests, frameworks used - test strategy - for each of Meshery&amp;rsquo;s architectural components. The &lt;a href=&#39;https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13Ir4gfaKoAX9r8qYjAFFl_U9ntke4X5ndREY1T7bnVs/edit&#39;&gt;Meshery Test Plan&lt;/a&gt; is a tactical spreadsheet that &lt;em&gt;itemizes&lt;/em&gt; specific integration and end-to-end test cases and tracks their status. It includes a list of GitHub workflows and their purpose. Join the &lt;a href=&#39;https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GrVdGHZAYeu6wHNLLoiaKNqBtk7enXE9XeDRCvdA4bY/edit#&#39;&gt;Meshery CI meeting&lt;/a&gt; and/or the &lt;a href=&#39;https://meshery.io/subscribe&#39;&gt;developers mailing list&lt;/a&gt; to get involved. &lt;/div&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery Adapters</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-adapters/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-adapters/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery Adapters are the Extension Points in Meshery&amp;rsquo;s architecture. Their design, the process of creating a new adapter is documented in &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/extensibility/adapters&#34;&gt;Extensibility: Meshery Adapters&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;With the &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#adapter&#34;&gt;CONTRIBUTING.md&lt;/a&gt; in mind, understand that development follows the usual fork-and-pull request workflow described here, see also GitHub Process. On forking GitHub deactivates all workflows. It is safe and good practice to activate them such that the code is validated on each push. This requires that branches filter for “on push” is set to ‘**’ to be triggered also on branches containing ‘/’  in their name.  The actions are parameterized using secrets (see Build &amp;amp; Release Strategy). The Docker image is only built and pushed to Docker Hub if a tag is pushed and the corresponding authentication information is configured.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery CLI</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-cli/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-cli/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; is written in Golang or the Go Programming Language. For development use &lt;a href=&#34;https://go.dev/dl/&#34;&gt;Go version 1.25+&lt;/a&gt;. &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; uses the &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/spf13/cobra&#34;&gt;Cobra&lt;/a&gt; framework. A good first-step towards contributing to &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; would be to familiarize yourself with the &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/spf13/cobra#concepts&#34;&gt;Cobra concepts&lt;/a&gt;. For manipulating config files, &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; uses &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/spf13/viper&#34;&gt;Viper&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;alert alert-info&#34; role=&#34;alert&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;h4 alert-heading&#34; role=&#34;heading&#34;&gt;Meshery CLI Reference Documents&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1q63sIGAuCnIeDs8PeM-0BAkNj8BBgPUXhLbe1Y-318o/edit#gid=0&#34;&gt;Meshery Command Tracker&lt;/a&gt;: Status of mesheryctl command implementation and platform compatibility.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;    &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xRlFpElRmybJ3WacgPKXgCSiQ2poJl3iCCV1dAalf0k/edit#&#34;&gt;Meshery CLI Commands and Documentation&lt;/a&gt;: Detailed documentation of the `mesheryctl` commands.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;    &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13Ir4gfaKoAX9r8qYjAFFl_U9ntke4X5ndREY1T7bnVs/edit?gid=1907616946#gid=1907616946&#34;&gt;Meshery Test Plan&lt;/a&gt;: Test cases for end-to-end testing of Meshery functionality.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&#x9;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/meshery/labels/component%2Fmesheryctl&#34;&gt;mesheryctl open issues and pull requests&lt;/a&gt;: Matching the &#34;component/mesheryctl&#34; label.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;designing-commands&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Designing Commands&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-cli-guide/&#34;&gt;Meshery CLI Style Guide&lt;/a&gt; outlines the process by which new commands are designed and contains a collection of principles and conventions that need to be followed while designing &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; commands. &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; might be the interface that the users first have with Meshery. As such, &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; needs to provide a great UX.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery CLI End-to-End Tests</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-cli-tests/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-cli-tests/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery CLI is the command line interface for Meshery. Meshery CLI, otherwise known as &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt;, is a client of Meshery Server&amp;rsquo;s &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/extensibility/api/&#34;&gt;REST API&lt;/a&gt;. It provides a way to interact with Meshery and perform various operations such as installing, configuring, and managing cloud native infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;This document is intended to help you contribute to the end-to-end tests for &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt;, the Meshery CLI. It is designed to be a guide for developers who are new to the project and want to contribute to the testing of &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery Docker Extension</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-docker-extension/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-docker-extension/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h2 id=&#34;prerequisites&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Prerequisites&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;To start contributing to Meshery Docker Extension, make sure you have &lt;a href=&#34;https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/&#34;&gt;Docker&lt;/a&gt; installed on your system.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;docker-extension-for-meshery&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Docker Extension for Meshery&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The Docker Extension for Meshery extends Docker Desktop’s position as the cloud native developer’s go-to Kubernetes environment with easy access to the next layer of cloud native infrastructure. The extension provides a seamless experience for developers to manage and monitor their Kubernetes applications and services.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h4 id=&#34;using-docker-desktop&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Using Docker Desktop&#xA;&lt;/h4&gt;&#xA;&lt;ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Navigate to the Extensions Marketplace of Docker Desktop.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery Docs</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-docs/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-docs/</guid>
      <description>&lt;div class=&#34;alert alert-info&#34; role=&#34;alert&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;h4 alert-heading&#34; role=&#34;heading&#34;&gt;Important&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Before contributing, please review the &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#documentation-contribution-flow&#34;&gt;Documentation Contribution Flow&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Use the following steps to set up your development environment depending on your Operating System of choice, fork the repository, install dependencies and run the site locally.  You can then make changes, test locally, sign-off and commit, and push the changes made for review.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;alert alert-info&#34; role=&#34;alert&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;h4 alert-heading&#34; role=&#34;heading&#34;&gt;Meshery Documentation Design Specification&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;See the &lt;a href=&#34;https://docs.google.com/document/d/17guuaxb0xsfutBCzyj2CT6OZiFnMu9w4PzoILXhRXSo/edit&#34;&gt;Meshery Documentation Design Specification&lt;/a&gt; which serves to provide an overview of the tooling and approach used to create Meshery&amp;rsquo;s documentation and its information architecture.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery Policies</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-policies/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-policies/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h2 id=&#34;background&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Background&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery has a built-in policy engine, based on &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/&#34;&gt;Open Policy Agent (OPA)&lt;/a&gt;. Meshery uses the &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/policy-language/&#34;&gt;Rego&lt;/a&gt; query language to create these &lt;a href=&#34;https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/logical/policies&#34;&gt;policies&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;prerequisites&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Prerequisites&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;To start contributing to Meshery Policy Engine, make sure you have &lt;a href=&#34;https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/latest/#running-opa&#34;&gt;OPA CLI&lt;/a&gt; installed on your system. You will also need to clone the &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/meshery/&#34;&gt;Meshery Server&lt;/a&gt; project from Github.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;components-of-meshery-policy-engine&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Components of Meshery Policy Engine&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Rego policies are the declarative logic behind the policy engine. These policies define how the underlying engine understands relationships within Meshery Designs. Rego policies can be found &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/server/meshmodel/meshery-core/0.7.2/v1.0.0/policies&#34;&gt;here&lt;/a&gt; in the Meshery Github repository.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery Schemas</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;This comprehensive guide covers everything you need to know to contribute to the Meshery Schemas repository. Meshery follows &lt;strong&gt;Schema-Driven Development (SDD)&lt;/strong&gt;, where the structure of data is centrally defined using schemas that power consistency, validation, and code generation across the platform.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;hr&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;table-of-contents&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Table of Contents&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#overview&#34;&gt;Overview&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#prerequisites&#34;&gt;Prerequisites&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#quick-start&#34;&gt;Quick Start&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#schema-directory-structure&#34;&gt;Schema Directory Structure&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#understanding-apiyml---the-construct-index-file&#34;&gt;Understanding &lt;code&gt;api.yml&lt;/code&gt; - The Construct Index File&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#schema-file-roles&#34;&gt;Schema File Roles&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#naming-conventions&#34;&gt;Naming Conventions&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#adding-a-new-schema&#34;&gt;Adding a New Schema&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#modifying-existing-schemas&#34;&gt;Modifying Existing Schemas&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#code-generation&#34;&gt;Code Generation&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#vendor-extensions-x--annotations&#34;&gt;Vendor Extensions (&lt;code&gt;x-*&lt;/code&gt; Annotations)&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#go-helper-files&#34;&gt;Go Helper Files&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#typescript-integration&#34;&gt;TypeScript Integration&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#common-schema-patterns&#34;&gt;Common Schema Patterns&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#template-files&#34;&gt;Template Files&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#what-not-to-commit&#34;&gt;What NOT to Commit&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#testing-your-changes&#34;&gt;Testing Your Changes&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#common-mistakes-to-avoid&#34;&gt;Common Mistakes to Avoid&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#checklist-for-schema-changes&#34;&gt;Checklist for Schema Changes&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/#getting-help&#34;&gt;Getting Help&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;hr&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;overview&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Overview&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery schemas offer a powerful system designed for:&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery Server</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-server/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-server/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;As a new contributor, you’re going to want to familiarize with the project in order to resolve the issues in the best way. Installing and playing around with Meshery will give you context for any issues that you might work on.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Once an issue has been addressed, you’ll need to test it as well. Ideally, these tests are run from the user’s perspective (someone running Meshery in a container), not from a contributor’s perspective (someone running Meshery as a locally-compiled service).&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery Server Events</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-server-events/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-server-events/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery incorporates an internal events publication mechanism that provides users with real-time updates on the processes occurring within the Meshery server when interacting with its endpoints. It ensures that users are kept in the loop regarding the ongoing activities within the API, and guides users towards future steps to resolve issues. This guide will provide step-by-step instructions on sending events from the server, including when to trigger events and what information to include.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery UI</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h2 id=&#34;ui-contribution-flow&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;&lt;a name=&#34;contributing-ui&#34;&gt;UI Contribution Flow&lt;/a&gt;&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery UI is built on React and Next.js. In nearly all cases, while contributing to Meshery UI, you will need to build and run Meshery Server as well. Meshery Server is written in &lt;code&gt;Go&lt;/code&gt; (Golang) and leverages Go Modules. To make building of each component easier a &lt;code&gt;Makefile&lt;/code&gt; is included in the main repository folder. Use &lt;code&gt;make&lt;/code&gt; to build any and all components.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;architecture&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Architecture&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The following is a list of top-level frameworks, libraries, design system used in Meshery UI.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery UI - Dashboard Widgets</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-widgets/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-widgets/</guid>
      <description>&lt;div class=&#34;prereqs&#34;&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong style=&#34;font-size: 20px;&#34;&gt;Prerequisite Reading&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;  &lt;ol&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;contributing-ui&#34;&gt;Contributing to Meshery UI&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery&amp;rsquo;s dashboard is a composable and extensible interface made up of individual widgets. These widgets allow contributors to surface specific Meshery data or capabilities within a modular layout system.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;This guide walks through the process of creating and integrating a custom widget into the &lt;a href=&#34;https://playground.meshery.io/&#34;&gt;Meshery dashboard&lt;/a&gt;. You’ll learn about layout configuration, design best practices, and how to register new widgets.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;1-widget-architecture&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;1. Widget Architecture&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Widgets are React components located &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/ui/components/DashboardComponent/widgets&#34;&gt;here&lt;/a&gt;:&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery UI - Notification Center</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/</guid>

Contents&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#what-is-the-notification-center&#34;&gt;What is the Notification Center?&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#metadata-formatter&#34;&gt;Metadata Formatter&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#how-notification-metadata-is-rendered&#34;&gt;How Notification Metadata is Specific Notification Formatters&lt;/a&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#common-formatter&#34;&gt;Common Formatter&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#error-formatter&#34;&gt;Error Formatter&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#model-registration-formatter&#34;&gt;Model Registration Formatter&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#relationship-evaluation-formatter&#34;&gt;Relationship Evaluation Formatter&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#dry-run-formatter&#34;&gt;Dry Run Formatter&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#deployment-summary-formatter&#34;&gt;Deployment Summary Formatter&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center/#propertyformatters-and-propertylinkformatters&#34;&gt;PropertyFormatters and PropertyLinkFormatters&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;video style=&#34;width:min(100%,750px)&#34; height=&#34;auto&#34; autoplay muted loop&gt;&#xA;  &lt;source src=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/meshery/assets/65964225/345672de-3f61-4be0-b3c8-0e7480cc496c&#34; type=&#34;video/mp4&#34;&gt;&#xA; Your browser does not support the video tag&#xA;&lt;/video&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;what-is-the-notification-center&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;What is the Notification Center?&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The Notification Center is a dedicated panel It acts as a central place where you can see important updates related to your infrastructure, workloads, and Meshery’s internal operations.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery UI - Sistent</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-sistent/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-sistent/</guid>
      <description>&lt;div class=&#34;prereqs&#34;&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong style=&#34;font-size: 20px;&#34;&gt;Prerequisite Reading&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;  &lt;ol&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;contributing-ui&#34;&gt;Contributing to Meshery UI&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;contributing-to-meshery-ui---sistent&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;&lt;a name=&#34;contributing-ui-sistent&#34;&gt;Contributing to Meshery UI - Sistent&lt;/a&gt;&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;Sistent&lt;/code&gt; is the design system used by Meshery UI. Sistent is an open source design system that offers building blocks to create consistent, accessible, and user-friendly interfaces. It&amp;rsquo;s aimed at developers who want to design applications aligned with the same brand and ensure a uniform user experience across different products.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Sistent leverages Material UI libraries and provides a custom theme on top of it for a consistent look and feel. It includes components, icons, and design tokens that developers can readily integrate into their applications. By using Sistent, developers can save time and effort while maintaining a high-quality user experience throughout Meshery.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery UI End-to-End Tests</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-tests/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-tests/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;To automate functional integration and end-to-end testing Meshery uses &lt;a href=&#34;https://playwright.dev/&#34;&gt;Playwright&lt;/a&gt; as one of the tools to automate browser testing. End-to-end tests run with each pull request to ensure that the changes do not break the existing functionality.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;prerequisites&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Prerequisites:&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Before diving into Meshery&amp;rsquo;s testing environment, certain prerequisites are necessary:&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;A verified account in your chosen provider which integrate with Meshery.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;A compatible browser such as Chromium, Chrome, or Firefox.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Installations of Golang, NodeJS, and Makefiles for Native OS build (Optional for docker based build).&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Kubernetes clusters (Required for connection to Kubernetes test cases)&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Already have &lt;a href=&#34;https://docs.meshery.io/concepts/architecture/adapters&#34;&gt;Meshery Adapters&lt;/a&gt; up and running (Required for adapters test cases)&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;setting-up-environment-variable&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Setting up environment variable&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;To run the tests successfully, three environment variables must be configured:&lt;br&gt;&#xA;• &lt;code&gt;REMOTE_PROVIDER_USER_EMAIL&lt;/code&gt; (Required): The email associated with your account within your provider.&lt;br&gt;&#xA;• &lt;code&gt;REMOTE_PROVIDER_USER_PASSWORD&lt;/code&gt; (Required): The password associated with your account within your provider.&lt;br&gt;&#xA;• &lt;code&gt;PROVIDER_TOKEN&lt;/code&gt; (Optional): Your provider token, can be generated from an account registered within your provider&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Meshery using git</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-gitflow/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-gitflow/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h1 id=&#34;working-by-forking&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Working by Forking&#xA;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Just head over to the GitHub page and click the &amp;ldquo;Fork&amp;rdquo; button. It&amp;rsquo;s just that simple. Once you&amp;rsquo;ve done that, you can use your favorite git client to clone your repo or just head straight to the command line:&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;clone-your-fork-to-your-local-machine&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Clone your fork to your local machine&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;pre tabindex=&#34;0&#34;&gt;&lt;code&gt;git clone git@github.com:USERNAME/FORKED-PROJECT.git&#xA;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;p&gt;Keeping Your Fork Up to Date&#xA;While this isn&amp;rsquo;t a necessary step, if you plan on doing anything more than just a tiny quick fix, you&amp;rsquo;ll want to make sure you keep your fork up to date by tracking the original &amp;ldquo;upstream&amp;rdquo; repo that you forked. To do this, you&amp;rsquo;ll need to add a remote:&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Model Components</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-components/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-components/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Components are defined by schemas.&lt;/strong&gt; Each component&amp;rsquo;s structure, capabilities, and metadata follow the &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/schemas/tree/master/schemas/constructs/v1beta1/component&#34;&gt;Component schema&lt;/a&gt; in &lt;code&gt;meshery/schemas&lt;/code&gt;. When creating or modifying components, ensure they conform to the schema specification. See &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/&#34;&gt;Contributing to Schemas&lt;/a&gt; for details.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;In Meshery, a &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/&#34;&gt;Components&lt;/a&gt; is a fundamental building block used to represent and define the infrastructure under management. Each component provides granular and specific support for your infrastructure and applications. Once registered with Meshery Server (in the &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/registry/&#34;&gt;Registry&lt;/a&gt;), components are available for inclusion in &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/designs/&#34;&gt;Designs&lt;/a&gt; that you create. Components can be created and published by anyone, allowing you to share you custom extensions with the community.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Model Relationships</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-relationships/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-relationships/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Relationships follow a schema-defined structure.&lt;/strong&gt; The &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/schemas/tree/master/schemas/constructs/v1alpha3/relationship&#34;&gt;Relationship schema&lt;/a&gt; specifies how relationships between components are expressed. Refer to the schema when defining new relationship types or selectors. See &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/&#34;&gt;Contributing to Schemas&lt;/a&gt; for details.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/relationships/&#34;&gt;Relationships&lt;/a&gt; within &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/&#34;&gt;Models&lt;/a&gt; play a crucial role in establishing concrete visualisations of efficient data flow between different components of Meshery. These are used to classify the nature of interaction between one or more interconnected &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/&#34;&gt;Components&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;overview-of-steps-to-create-relationships&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Overview of Steps to Create Relationships&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Prework:&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Models</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-models/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-models/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Meshery Models are schema-driven.&lt;/strong&gt; Model definitions, including their structure, metadata, and versioning, are defined by JSON Schemas in the &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/schemas&#34;&gt;&lt;code&gt;meshery/schemas&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt; repository. Before contributing to models, familiarize yourself with the &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/schemas/tree/master/schemas/constructs/v1beta1/model&#34;&gt;Model schema&lt;/a&gt; and see &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/&#34;&gt;Contributing to Schemas&lt;/a&gt; for the development workflow.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;understanding-the-internals-of-mesherys-logical-object-model&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Understanding the internals of Meshery&amp;rsquo;s logical object model&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery uses a logical object model to describe the infrastructure and capabilities it manages in a consistent and extensible way.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h4 id=&#34;what-are-meshery-models&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;What Are Meshery Models?&#xA;&lt;/h4&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;At the core of this system are &lt;strong&gt;Meshery Models&lt;/strong&gt; — packages that define a specific type of infrastructure, application, or capability. These models include:&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Contributing to Models Quick Start</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-models-quick-start/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-models-quick-start/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Models follow Meshery&amp;rsquo;s schema-driven development approach.&lt;/strong&gt; Model, Component, and Relationship definitions are validated against schemas in &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/schemas/tree/master/schemas/constructs/v1beta1/model&#34;&gt;&lt;code&gt;Model schema&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;. See &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-schemas/&#34;&gt;Contributing to Schemas&lt;/a&gt; for details.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/&#34;&gt;Meshery Models&lt;/a&gt; are a way to represent the architecture of a system or application. Models are defined in JSON and can be used to visualize the components and relationships between them. This guide will walk you through the process of creating a new model.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/&#34;&gt;Meshery Components&lt;/a&gt; are the building blocks of a model. Each component represents a different part of the system or application. Components can be anything from a database to a microservice to a server. Relationships define how components interact with each other. For example, a database component might have a relationship with a microservice component that represents the microservice&amp;rsquo;s dependency on the database.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
<item>
      <title>How to write MeshKit compatible errors</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-error/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-error/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery pervasively uses MeshKit as a golang and infrastructure management-specific library in all of its components. MeshKit helps populate error messages with a uniform and useful set of informative attributes.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;To help with creating error codes, MeshKit contains a tool that analyzes, verifies and updates error codes in Meshery source code trees. It extracts error details into a file that can be used for publishing all error code references on the Meshery &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/reference/error-codes/&#34;&gt;error codes reference page&lt;/a&gt;. The objective to create this was to avoid centralized handling of error codes and automating everything&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Meshery CLI Style Guide</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-cli-guide/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-cli-guide/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;These guidelines are a collection of principles and conventions that need to be followed while designing mesheryctl commands.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;design-principles&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Design Principles&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;1. Consistency is quality.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;em&gt;Consistency of interaction drives a quality user experience. Whether that experience is delightful or painful is a related, but separate consideration. Meshery&amp;rsquo;s behavior of user interactions should be consistent even when their user experience is poor.&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Consistency is key when designing intuitive interfaces. Although &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl perf run -f &amp;lt;performance profile name&amp;gt;&lt;/code&gt; may sound more intuitive, users who are experienced in using the CLI will prefer the consistent verb &lt;code&gt;apply&lt;/code&gt; over &lt;code&gt;run&lt;/code&gt;. This will also ensure a consistent command language making memorizing easier. Consistency should also be enforced when chaining commands and using flags.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Meshery Documentation Structure and Organization</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-docs-structure/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-docs-structure/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Providing well-structured, easy-to-navigate documentation tailored for a diverse audience—from beginners to experts.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;target-audience&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Target Audience&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;We first identify &lt;strong&gt;who&lt;/strong&gt; this documentation serves before diving into how it’s organized. By clarifying different user personas, we can better direct them to relevant sections:&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Users&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;New Users&lt;/strong&gt;: Individuals just getting started with Meshery, needing a straightforward, guided setup.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Advanced Users&lt;/strong&gt;: Those who already have some experience and want deeper insights or specialized use cases.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Contributors &amp;amp; System Integrators&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Schema-Driven UI Development in Meshery</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-schemas/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/contributing-ui-schemas/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery aims to decouple the UI logic from hardcoded structures and become fully schema-driven. This allows the UI to dynamically adapt based on changes in the underlying schema without requiring constant manual updates. This document explains how to integrate schema definitions from the &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/schemas&#34;&gt;&lt;code&gt;meshery/schemas&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt; repository into the Meshery UI using a code-generation approach.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;hr&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;overview&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Overview&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery’s schemas define the &lt;strong&gt;structure of data (constructs)&lt;/strong&gt; using JSON Schema and &lt;strong&gt;their behavior (API operations)&lt;/strong&gt; using OpenAPI specifications. From these definitions, Meshery auto-generates:&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Setting up Meshery Development Environment on Windows</title>
      <link>/v0.9/project/contributing/meshery-windows/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/project/contributing/meshery-windows/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;You can use one of the following three approaches to setup a Meshery development environment in Windows:&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Using WSL or WSL2 (Recommended)&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Natively (directly) on Windows&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Using Hyper-V to create a Linux VM&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Setting up a Meshery development environment on WSL(2) or Hyper-V is not much different from setting up on a native Linux platform. The same instructions can be followed as already documented.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;All three methods require the same prerequisites mentioned below in the &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/project/contributing/meshery-windows/#prerequisites&#34;&gt;Prerequisites&lt;/a&gt; section but the Linux-based methods/platforms come with some of the prerequisites pre-installed and have no issues with Linux style commands making it easier to setup the environment.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
  </channel>
</rss>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Setting up Meshery Development Environment on Windows</h1>
          
          <p>You can use one of the following three approaches to setup a Meshery development environment in Windows:</p>
<ol>
<li>Using WSL or WSL2 (Recommended)</li>
<li>Natively (directly) on Windows</li>
<li>Using Hyper-V to create a Linux VM</li>
</ol>
<p>Setting up a Meshery development environment on WSL(2) or Hyper-V is not much different from setting up on a native Linux platform. The same instructions can be followed as already documented.</p>
<p>All three methods require the same prerequisites mentioned below in the <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/meshery-windows/#prerequisites">Prerequisites</a> section but the Linux-based methods/platforms come with some of the prerequisites pre-installed and have no issues with Linux style commands making it easier to setup the environment.</p>
<p>Additionally, all three require methods will require access to a Kubernetes cluster which can be a kind, minikube, Kubernetes in Docker or a cluster elsewhere with network access.</p>
<h2 id="prerequisites">
	Prerequisites
</h2>
<p>All three methods require the following prerequisites:</p>
<ul>
<li>make</li>
<li>gcc</li>
<li>nodejs (for npm)</li>
<li>go</li>
<li>Git or Git Bash</li>
<li>Visual Studio Code for development</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="compatibility">
	Compatibility
</h2>
<p>The following minimum Windows build versions are required:</p>
<table id="compatibility-table">
  <tr>
    <th id="model">Name</th>
    <th id="model">Version</th> 
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><a href="#wsl1">WSL1</a></td>
    <td><b>x64</b> - Windows 7 </td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><a href="#wsl2">WSL2</a></td>
    <td><b>x64</b> - Version 1903, Build 18362; <b>ARM 64</b> - Version 2004, Build 19041</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/release-notes#build-18945">Custom Kernel</a></td>
    <td>Build 18945</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/release-notes#build-19013">Kernel with K8s required modules</a></td>
    <td>Build 19013</td>
  </tr>
</table>
<p>Note
<br />Run the following command on Powershell to check your Windows build and version:</p>
 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">[System.Environment]::OSVersion.Version</div></div>
 </pre>
<h2 id="using-wsl2">
	Using WSL2
</h2>
<p>Here is a link to setting up WSL2: <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install">https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install</a></p>
<p>Once WSL is setup, login to the WSL distribution and use the steps for Linux to setup the development environment.</p>
<h3 id="steps">
	Steps
</h3>
<p>Perform the following steps in order:</p>
<h4 id="1-enable-and-configure-windows-subsystem-for-linux-wsl">
	1. Enable and configure Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL)
</h4>
<p>Open Powershell in administrator mode and run:</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">dism.exe /online /enable-feature /featurename:Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux /all /norestart

Restart-Computer</div></div>
</pre>
<p>For more information visit <a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install-win10">How to install Linux on Windows with WSL</a>.</p>
<h4 id="2-configuring-wsl">
	2. Configuring WSL
</h4>
<p>Enable VM (Virtual Machine) feature. To do so open <em>PowerShell</em> in administrator mode and run:</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">dism.exe /online /enable-feature /featurename:VirtualMachinePlatform /all /norestart</div></div>
</pre>
<p>Ensure WSL2 is the default version:</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">wsl --set-default-version 2</div></div>
</pre>
<h4 id="3-install-a-new-distro">
	3. Install a new distro
</h4>
<p>Refer to the instructions <a href="https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install-win10#install-your-linux-distribution-of-choice">here</a> to install a new distro such as Ubuntu by default.
Feel free to use any distro of your choice.</p>
<h4 id="4-enable-docker">
	4. Enable Docker
</h4>
<p>The Docker Desktop application for Windows includes a comprehensive set of tools, including Docker Engine, Docker CLI client, Docker Compose, Notary, Kubernetes, and a Credential Helper.</p>
<table id="compatibility-table">
  <tr>
    <th id="model">Windows 10 Version</th>
    <th id="model">Docker Desktop</th> 
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Pro/Education/Enterprise</td>
    <td><a href="https://docs.docker.com/docker-for-windows/install/">Docker Desktop for Windows Pro</a></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Home</td>
    <td><a href="https://docs.docker.com/docker-for-windows/install-windows-home/">Docker Desktop for Windows Home</a></td>
  </tr>
</table>
<h2 id="natively-on-windows">
	Natively on Windows
</h2>
<p>This approach can be the most challenging to setup among all and is recommended for users that are very conversant with setting up development environments in Windows.
make, gcc and the other prerequisites do not come pre-installed on Windows and hence these need to be installed manually. You will also need to set the <strong>Path</strong> in <em>Environment Variables</em> for some of them like <em>make</em> and <em>gcc</em>.</p>
<h3 id="installing-prerequsites">
	Installing prerequsites:
</h3>
<p>Here are some links and recommendations to install the prerequisites:</p>
<h4 id="--make">
	- make
</h4>
<p>Use the <a href="https://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/downlinks/make.php">setup program</a> to download the installation package and run it to install make and other dependencies.</p>
<p>If the download link fails, visit the home page at <a href="https://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/packages/make.htm">https://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/packages/make.htm</a></p>
<h4 id="--gcc">
	- gcc
</h4>
<p>Use the <a href="https://www.mingw-w64.org/">mingw-w64</a> project for gcc. The pre-built binaries can be downloaded from <a href="https://github.com/niXman/mingw-builds-binaries/releases">https://github.com/niXman/mingw-builds-binaries/releases</a>. For a typical 64-bit Windows, it is of the <strong>x86_64-XX.X.X-release-posix-seh-ucrt-XX_XXX-XXXX.7z</strong> format. Posix provides cross-platform compatibility and is known to work well. After extracting and copying (typically to the C:\ drive at root), add the path to the <strong>Path</strong> variable in <em>Environment Variables</em>.</p>
<p>For example, here&rsquo;s a <a href="https://github.com/niXman/mingw-builds-binaries/releases/download/15.2.0-rt_v13-rev0/x86_64-15.2.0-release-posix-seh-ucrt-rt_v13-rev0.7z">direct download link</a> to the latest release as of this writing. After installing, ensure the path is in the <strong>Path</strong> variable in <em>Environment Variables</em>. It is usually added automatically.</p>
<p>The <em>Cygwin</em> project is known to fail with errors.</p>
<p>For more information, visit <a href="https://gcc.gnu.org/install/binaries.html">https://gcc.gnu.org/install/binaries.html</a></p>
<h4 id="--nodejs-for-npm">
	- nodejs (for npm)
</h4>
<p>You will need <strong>Node 20</strong>. Download it from <a href="https://nodejs.org/en/download">https://nodejs.org/en/download</a> and install it. The path is usually automatically added.</p>
<h4 id="--go">
	- go
</h4>
<p>Visit <a href="https://go.dev/doc/install">https://go.dev/doc/install</a> to download and install Go. Please use the version specified in the project&rsquo;s <code>go.mod</code> file. As of this writing, Meshery uses <strong>1.26.4</strong>. The path is usually automatically added.</p>
<h4 id="--git-bash">
	- Git Bash
</h4>
<p>Git Bash is a terminal emulator which provides git and Linux-like command line experience. You can download it from: <a href="https://git-scm.com/downloads">https://git-scm.com/downloads</a>.</p>
<h3 id="verify-prerequisites">
	Verify prerequisites
</h3>
<p>Launch Git Bash, PowerShell or VS Code Terminal and run the following commands to ensure prerequisites are met:</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">make --version</div></div>
</pre>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">gcc --version</div></div>
</pre>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">node --version</div></div>
</pre>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">go version</div></div>
</pre>
<p>If any of these result in command not found error, check if the PATH in environment variables has been set properly. To launch the environment variables window Here&rsquo;s an example:
<a href="/project/contributing/images/win-environment-variables.png">
<img style= "max-width: 450px;" src="/project/contributing/images/win-environment-variables.png" />
</a></p>
<p>You are now ready to <a href="/v0.9/project/contributing/">contribute</a> to Meshery.</p>
<h2 id="using-hyper-v-to-install-a-linux-vm">
	Using Hyper-V to install a linux VM
</h2>
<p>Here is a link to install linux VM using Hyper-V: <a href="https://wiki.ubuntu.com/Hyper-V">https://wiki.ubuntu.com/Hyper-V</a></p>
<h2 id="get-the-code">
	Get the code
</h2>
<ul>
<li>Fork and then clone the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery">Meshery repository</a>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span class="line"><span class="cl">$ git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/meshery
</span></span></code></pre></div></li>
</ul>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>
